abstract: Chiang Mai Province faces ongoing football gambling problems and consistent arrest statistics, reflecting those residents are at risk of gambling addiction. This research aimed to study the general characteristics, football gambling behaviors, risk of gambling addiction, influencing factors, and impacts under the framework of Football Gambling, Social Learning Theory, Uses and Gratifications Theory, and Technological Determinism. Data were collected from 400 respondents who had engaged in football gambling using convenience sampling. A questionnaire and the Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) were used as research instruments, considering research ethics. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple regression. The results showed that most football gamblers were male and initiated gambling due to peer influence. More than half were at risk of football gambling addiction. Personal, social, and media factors strongly influenced football gambling behaviors, including enjoyment, peer influence, and betting odds. Moderate impacts were reported, such as stress and insomnia. Hypothesis testing indicated that individuals who had won or lost large amounts of money had a higher risk of gambling addiction than other groups. All three factors were positively associated with gambling risk. Multiple regression analysis showed that these factors significantly predicted the risk of football gambling addiction (Adjusted R² = .257, F = 20.751, p < .001). This study proposes the G-SHIELD (Gambling Shield) Model as a theoretical framework and policy measures to prevent and address football gambling problems, aiming to reduce risks at the individual, family, social, and media levels.

title: Incentivos de marketing en la percepción de riesgo y comportamiento de apuestas deportivas
abstract: El presente estudio tuvo como objetivo analizar los incentivos de marketing en la percepción de riesgo y comportamiento de las apuestas deportivas en las decisiones de los usuarios. La metodología siguió un enfoque cuantitativo, con un diseño no experimental de alcance descriptivo, mediante una encuesta aplicada a 625 personas de la ciudad de Machala que realizan apuestas deportivas, seleccionadas a través de un muestreo por conveniencia. Los resultados evidenciaron que los bonos de bienvenida y las apuestas gratuitas son los incentivos más frecuentes que se encuentran los apostadores, mientras que las redes sociales son el principal medio de difusión de estas promociones. Más de la mitad de los participantes percibe un menor riesgo de perder dinero al recibir estos beneficios y reconoce que apuesta con mayor frecuencia y montos más altos cuando recibe una promoción. Se concluye que los incentivos de marketing funcionan como un mecanismo psicológico en la manera en que los usuarios evalúan el riesgo al apostar y en el comportamiento que adoptan después de apostar, lo que refuerza la necesidad de promover estrategias publicitarias más responsables.

title: Dataset for: The Influence of Social Media Exposure, Financial Literacy, FOMO, and Peer Pressure on Online Betting Intention Among Generation Z in Bangladesh
abstract: This dataset contains survey responses collected from Generation Z individuals in Bangladesh to examine the influence of Social Media Exposure, Financial Literacy, Fear of Missing Out (FOMO), and Peer Pressure on Online Betting Intention. The data were collected through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale. The dataset includes demographic information and measurement items for all study constructs. The data can be used for replication, validation, and further research on online betting behavior among young adults in developing countries.

title: Sports Betting Legalization Amplifies Emotional Cues and Intimate Partner Violence
abstract: Abstract This study explores the relationship between legalized sports gambling, unexpected emotional cues stemming from NFL home team upset losses and reported intimate partner violence (IPV). Using 1995–2022 crime data from NIBRS, replicating and extending Card and Dahl (2011)’s model, we find that legalized gambling increases the impact of upset losses on IPV by 10 percentage points. The e!ect is larger in states with mobile betting, where higher bets were placed, around paydays, and for teams on a winning streak. These results suggest that financial losses from gambling amplify emotional reactions to unexpected team losses.

title: The Rational Mind's Blind Spot: Why Do People Make Irrational Financial Decisions.
abstract: Standard economic theory imagines a decision-maker who has preferences, process information, weighs costs and benefits consistently, faces constraints and chooses the option that maximizes expected utility. Everyday financial behaviour repeatedly departs from this benchmark as real people, and especially those living in this app-driven economy of 2026, do not behave this way. A person may know that saving is beneficial but still spends impulsively; understands that gambling has a negative expected value but still place a bet; intend to hold a long-term investment but still sell it during a market drop. This paper asks why, using four everyday behaviours: impulse spendings, sports betting among teenagers, panic selling during market falls and buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) borrowings. For each behaviour I set the textbook “should” against the observed “does”, trace the psychological mechanisms behind the gap (present bias, loss aversion, mental accounting, overconfidence, social-norms effects and hot emotional states) and asks who profits when those mechanisms are triggered. The central argument is that these behaviours are not four unrelated forms of financial ‘irrationality’ , they are different expressions of a recurring decision architecture: immediate rewards are psychologically salient, delayed costs are discounted, losses are felt disproportionately, social information changes perceived norms and risk and modern financial technologies reduce friction between intention and action, turns out that these four behaviours share one structure, I call it “asymmetric friction”. The paper also considers the role of supply side: the firms and platforms, retailers, betting platforms, brokers and lenders because incentives are not located only inside the individuals but also the supply side as they design the environments that make certain choices easier, faster and more emotionally compelling. Irrationality is therefore systematic, and because it is systematic, it is predictable, measurable, and designable. The final synthesis proposes that improving these behaviours requires more than financial literacy, it requires understanding the interaction between preferences, cognitive limits, emotions and redesigning the environments in which people choose.

title: Apuestas deportivas de contrapartida online, delito de estafa y el artículo 286 BIS.4 del Código Penal
abstract: Gambling has traditionally been fertile ground for criminal behaviour, particularly when financial gains are involved. In the context of sports betting, and especially with the rise of online platforms, certain behaviours have emerged that verge on fraud. When determining the legal significance of these behaviours, the principle of the victim's self-responsibility for their financial loss undoubtedly plays a key role. However, recent decisions of the Spanish Supreme Court have reduced the number of cases in which a court could invoke such a principle. This article aims to determine whether this principle applies in betting cases and, if so, how it might limit the offender's criminal liability. In addition, the possibility of classifying some of the cases described above under the offense set forth in Article 286 bis.4 of the Spanish Criminal Code will be evaluated.

title: A Case Report on Gambling Disorder in the Context of Hopelessness and Values: A Narrative Therapy Intervention
abstract: In recent years, the increasing prevalence of gambling disorder has prompted mental health professionals to explore various treatment modalities. Although several therapeutic approaches have been proposed, there is still a lack of robust empirical evidence regarding their effectiveness. Intervention-based studies have emphasized the need to move beyond symptom reduction and behavioral control by incorporating multidimensional aspects of recovery, thereby highlighting the necessity for innovative therapeutic frameworks. This case report aims to describe and analyze the clinical story and therapeutic process of a 25-year-old male who was considered to have a gambling disorder due to repetitive engagement in online betting and who underwent treatment through the Narrative Therapy approach. The client's symptoms were assessed using the DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for gambling disorder, along with the South Oaks Gambling Screen (SOGS). The client was followed for over a year, during which 28 individual therapy sessions were conducted. This case report discusses the role of values and hopelessness within the context of Narrative-based psychotherapy. Narrative-specific techniques such as externalization and alternative story development are addressed in relation to diagnosis, intervention, and follow-up. Rather than aiming to eliminate the gambling behavior directly, the intervention focused on uncovering and engaging with the underlying values and hopes that drive such behaviors—underscoring a shift from pathology to meaning-making. Narrative Therapy offers practical and applicable techniques for addressing gambling disorder, especially by facilitating a value-oriented and individualized therapeutic process.

title: Behavioral addiction tendencies and associated psychosocial factors in faculty members
abstract: Objective: Behavioral addictions may be associated with psychological symptoms and work-related factors. However, studies evaluating multiple behavioral addiction domains among faculty members remain limited. This study aimed to investigate behavioral addiction tendencies and associated psychosocial factors among faculty members. Methods: This cross-sectional online study included 202 faculty members. Participants completed an online survey consisting of a sociodemographic questionnaire, the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale-21 (DASS-21), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Bergen Work Addiction Scale (BWAS), Smartphone Addiction Scale–Short Version (SAS-SV), Bergen Social Media Addiction Scale (BSMAS), Internet Gaming Disorder Scale–Short Form (IGDS9-SF), Modified Yale Food Addiction Scale (mYFAS 2.0), and Online Gambling Addiction Scale (OGAS). Group comparisons and correlation analyses were performed. Results: Behavioral addiction tendencies were observed at varying levels among faculty members, with work addiction, smartphone addiction, and social media addiction showing the highest scores. Depression, anxiety, and stress were positively associated with work addiction, smartphone addiction, social media addiction, and internet gaming disorder scores. Faculty members working more than 40 hours per week had significantly higher work addiction scores. Smartphone use, social media use, and gaming-related behaviors were positively associated with one another, whereas online gambling/betting tendencies demonstrated a distinct pattern. Conclusion: Behavioral addiction tendencies in faculty members appear to be associated with psychological symptoms and selected work-related characteristics. These findings contribute to the limited literature examining multiple behavioral addiction domains among faculty members and highlight the importance of considering behavioral addictions within a broader psychosocial context.

title: Differences in online gambling expenditure between players from Germany, Spain, Netherlands, Great Britain, US and Canada: A largescale online player tracking study
abstract: The present study aimed to compare the expenditure of real-world online gamblers (N = 926,086) from six countries (Great Britain, Netherlands, Germany, Spain, Canada [Ontario], and US) to identify potential impacts of specific regulatory aspects on the amount of money gambled by players. The dataset comprised 233,221 British players, 167,826 Dutch players, 89,456 German players, 55,229 Spanish players, 18,463 Canadian players, and 361,891 US players. Data were analyzed using the total amount of money bet, lost, and deposited. German players bet (median = €74) and lost (median = €15) the lowest amounts of money gambling. Moreover, the average bet per game (median = €0.17) was the lowest among German players. Canadian (mean = €11,165) and US players (mean = €6434) bet the highest amounts. The US and Canada were the two countries with the largest outliers with respect to amount bet. Analysis also showed that a small percentage of players were responsible for the majority of the revenue in each of the six jurisdictions. More specifically, in the US, the 20% highest spending players accounted for 95% of the amount of money bet. The respective percentages for Canada, Great Britain, Germany, Spain and the Netherlands were 94%, 88%, 86%, 91%, and 79%. The present study's findings suggest that less restrictive regulation is associated with higher gambling expenditure, and that very strict regulation is associated with lower gambling expenditure.

title: Using Machine-Learning Algorithms to Predict Self-Reported Problem Gambling Among a Sample of Online Gamblers
abstract: Abstract Studies suggest that algorithms can effectively be used to predict self-reported problem gambling using player tracking data. The present study analyzed a sample of real-world online gamblers ( N = 1,611) who engaged in lottery playing, casino gambling, bingo playing, and sports betting. The data also comprised each player’s actual gambling activity, as well as age and gender, in the 30 days prior to answering the Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI). Players who engaged in at least one lottery game 30 days prior to answering the PGSI were less likely to be problem gamblers compared to players who did not play lottery games. For all other game-categories the relationship was reversed. The results also indicated that specific behavioral tracking features—such as the average number of monetary deposits per session, total amount of money bet per day, session length, and casino gambling involvement—were among the most significant predictors of self-reported problem gambling. When evaluating different machine algorithms, logistic regression and random forest emerged as the most effective in predicting self-reported problem gambling. The present study is among the few which predicts self-reported problem gambling using a sample of online lottery players, casino gamblers, bingo players and sports bettors, and provides further empirical evidence supporting the use of machine learning models to identify self-reported problem gamblers based on player tracking data. These findings can inform responsible gambling strategies by enabling operators to identify and intervene before gambling-related problems escalate.
venue: International Journal of Mental Health and Addiction

title: O DIREITO PREVIDENCIÁRIO FRENTE AO PROBLEMA DAS BETS: O CUSTO SOCIAL DAS APOSTAS ONLINE E OS DESAFIOS DA SEGURIDADE SOCIAL BRASILEIRA
abstract: O presente artigo investiga se a ludopatia, enquanto transtorno mental reconhecido pelas classificações médicas internacionais, pode ensejar incapacidade previdenciária quando comprometida a aptidão laboral do segurado. A expansão das plataformas digitais de apostas esportivas online, conhecidas como bets, impulsionada pela Lei nº 14.790/2023, produziu uma crise silenciosa de saúde pública, com crescimento exponencial de casos de jogo patológico e reflexos diretos sobre o sistema de seguridade social brasileiro. O estudo desenvolve-se em quatro eixos temáticos encadeados: o marco regulatório das bets e sua insuficiência protetiva; a estrutura dos benefícios previdenciários por incapacidade no Regime Geral de Previdência Social, com exame dos requisitos legais para sua concessão; a caracterização clínica e neurobiológica da ludopatia e seus impactos documentados sobre a aptidão para o trabalho; e, por fim, a análise jurídica da ludopatia como causa de incapacidade laboral previdenciária, respondendo afirmativamente à hipótese central e identificando as lacunas normativas que obstaculizam a proteção efetiva do segurado. Conclui-se que a regulamentação vigente falhou ao desconsiderar o impacto previdenciário das apostas, gerando um paradoxo em que o Estado arrecada com o setor enquanto arca, de forma fragmentada e sem suporte normativo adequado, com os custos sociais e previdenciários do vício que contribuiu para disseminar.
venue: Revista de Direito do Trabalho Processo do Trabalho e Direito da Seguridade Social

title: Adicciones comportamentales: epidemiología, factores de riesgo, fenotipos y resultado terapéutico
abstract: Introducción: El TJ y la AVJ, son dos de las modalidades de AC con mayor prevalencia en las sociedades industrializadas, mostrando un crecimiento alarmantemente en las últimas décadas. Además, son cuadros clínicos cuyas características están en transformación, en gran medida como resultado de la rápida aparición y evolución de nuevas plataformas en formato presencial y virtual. Ante este escenario, los objetivos principales son: a) identificar componentes biopsicosociales que actúan como factores de riesgo del TJ (en especial la adicción a las apuestas deportivas online [AADO]) y la adicción a los videojuegos online (AVJO); b) analizar los mecanismos subyacentes que contribuyen a la expresión fenotípica y endofenotípica de estos comportamientos adictivos y c) determinar las variables con capacidad predictiva a la respuesta al tratamiento mediante la terapia cognitiva conductual (TCC). Resultados: En términos generales, las muestras analizadas estuvieron compuestas mayoritariamente por hombres, solteros, con niveles educativos primarios o secundarios y estatus socioeconómico bajo. En el primer estudio, se observó que la prevalencia de AADO fue del 13.01%, casi cuatro veces superior a la de AVJO, que alcanzó un 3.82% en una muestra de 3.036 pacientes que consecutivamente acudieron a solicitar tratamiento por comportamientos adictivos. Además, se identificó una tendencia lineal creciente en la prevalencia de AADO entre el 2012 (8.6%) y el 2022 (15.5%), mientras que la AVJO mostró solo una ligera tendencia creciente, aunque no alcanzó la significación estadística. A nivel psicopatológico, los pacientes con AADO presentaron mayores niveles de depresión, ansiedad, ideación paranoide y malestar psicológico global, así como mayores índices de impulsividad, desregulación emocional y consumo de sustancias. El perfil de personalidad de este grupo de pacientes se caracterizó por una mayor búsqueda de novedades, mayor dependencia de la recompensa, mayor persistencia y menor evitación del daño. En el segundo estudio, que se realizó mediante análisis de redes, la autotrascendencia fue identificada como el nodo “puente” y el más relevante, seguido del síntoma DSM-5 A7 “mentiras para ocultar el grado de implicación en el juego”, en los pacientes con actos ilegales relacionados al trastorno de juego (AIRTJ). En contraste, con los pacientes sin AIRTJ, el nodo con mayor relevancia y que se identificó como “puente”, fue el síntoma DSM-5 A5 “apuesta cuando se siente estresado (deprimido, culpable o ansioso)”. El tercer estudio evidenció que el riesgo de recaída durante la TCC, aplicada a pacientes con AVJO fue superior en sujetos con puntuaciones más altas en sensibilidad interpersonal, hostilidad y persistencia. Asimismo, ser hombre y presentar un inicio del comportamiento adictivo más tardío aumentó la probabilidad de abandono del tratamiento, mientras que un bajo cumplimiento terapéutico se asoció a mayores niveles de ideación paranoide, dependencia de la recompensa y bajos niveles de cooperatividad. El cuarto estudio que se incluye como anexo en esta tesis doctoral evidenció que, en comparación con sujetos controles sin adicciones, el TJ se asocia directamente con una edad más joven, mayores niveles de impulsividad, mayores déficits a nivel neuropsicológico y un nivel más bajo de LEAP2. De igual modo, se identificaron vínculos indirectos-mediadores que destacaron el papel relevante de la impulsividad y el funcionamiento neuropsicológico en la predisposición al desarrollo del TJ. Conclusiones: Los resultados de los estudios que conforman esta tesis evidencian la heterogeneidad de las AC, así como la presencia de múltiples factores biopsicosociales que influyen en su desarrollo y mantenimiento. Asimismo, se identificaron perfiles diferenciados en los grupos de pacientes con TJ (en particular con AADO) y AVJO, caracterizados por variables sociodemográficas, psicopatológicas y rasgos de personalidad específicos que permiten comprender mejor los mecanismos subyacentes que configuran la expresión fenotípica propia de cada condición clínica. Introducció: El TJ i l'AVJ, són modalitats d'AC amb més prevalença a les societats industrialitzades, mostrant un creixement alarmantment en les darreres dècades. A més, són quadres clínics les característiques dels quals estan en transformació, en gran mesura com a resultat de la ràpida aparició i evolució de noves plataformes en format presencial i virtual. Davant d'aquest escenari, els objectius principals són: a) identificar components biopsicosocials que actuen com a factors de risc del TJ (especialment l'addicció a les apostes esportives en línia [AADO]) i l'addicció als videojocs en línia (AVJO); b) analitzar els mecanismes subjacents que contribueixen a lexpressió fenotípica i endofenotípica daquests comportaments addictius i c) determinar les variables amb capacitat predictiva a la resposta al tractament mitjançant la teràpia cognitiva conductual (TCC). title: Evolving fantasy cricket teams: Applying genetic algorithms for optimal player selection
abstract: In fantasy crickets, users are allowed to make virtual teams on the basis of real performance of a player. The classical techniques, e.g. random sampling and systematic replacements restrict optimization in search of large solution space. Genetic Algorithms (GA) exploit the evolutionary strategies such as crossover, mutation and selection to maximize team configurations. In this paper, it has been argued that GA is a better solution to team selection. GA maximizes the expected performance and ensures the compliance with the credit and role limitations. GA has produced better teams than random sampling, systematic replacements and K-means clustering by continuously adapting to the play outcomes of players. This paper shows that GA is able to perform well at the optimisation of selection of fantasy sports clubs and offers a data-driven and customizable process.

title: Retail Betting Markets
abstract: This paper examines the rapid expansion and convergence of retail betting markets. We analyze market design elements, discuss economic utility, and highlight shared behavioral drivers of sports betting markets, prediction markets, and retail options trading. Our review underscores how technological innovation, behavioral biases, and regulatory arbitrage have shaped recent market evolution. title: Risk Factors and Prevalence of Gambling Among University Students During Academic Disruptions: A Case of Lecturer’s Strike in Kenya 2025
abstract: This study investigated risk factors and prevalence of gambling among university students during academic disruptions brought about by such a case of lecturers' strikes, more so in public universities. A survey was used to collect data with a quantitative approach; a sample size of 620 students continuing with their academic work was randomly selected from 4 public universities in the Nairobi metropolitan area. The study established that several factors, such as socioeconomic factors like financial constraints, academic disruptions like lecturer strikes, environmental factors like exposure to betting platforms, and psychological factors like idleness and stress levels, contribute to gambling behaviours among students. The findings show that students from low socioeconomic backgrounds participate in risk gambling behaviour, which in the long run affects their academic progress and causes psychological distress. The most common form of gambling was sports betting, with the motivation of making quick money from betting. From the study, it was established that there’s a significant relationship between socioeconomic factors and gambling risk behaviours among students. The regulatory framework directly contributes to the growth of gambling in Kenya. Hence, in control measures, betting companies can adopt some technology that will only allow users to bet with limitations to ensure there is no overspending, thus preventing addictions of any kind. Institutions ought to invest in centers of counseling with the establishment of academic programmes geared towards creating awareness to promote responsible gambling even during times of academic disruptions in Kenyan public universities.

title: Screening on Someone Else's Price: Exclusion and Price Discovery in Betting Markets
abstract: Sportsbooks limit bettors whose bets beat the closing line, a price set at sharp books and exchanges where limited bettors then trade. I show that when a dealer screens customers against a price its excluded customers help produce, exclusion and price discovery are strategic complements: a more precise benchmark improves screening, which sends more informed flow to the benchmark venue. When a moderate amount of informed flow reaches the benchmark venue from other sources, this feedback sustains both a segregated and a low-precision market. Rules that force dealers to serve everyone weaken the benchmark and can collapse the segregated market. Because exclusion substitutes for price, such rules also raise the price uninformed customers pay. Screening on the benchmark implies that many correctly limited accounts are losing money when cut.

title: Between-session chasing via time of return in online eCasino gambling
abstract: Background and aims: Chasing refers to continuing and/or intensifying gambling following losses (loss-chasing) and/or wins (win-chasing). It is commonly captured between sessions, i.e., returning another day/time after losses or wins in prior sessions. Between-session chasing is a hallmark of problematic gambling, but the current understanding of between-session chasing in field settings remains limited. Methods: Using a large-scale behavioral tracking dataset (11,156 gamblers; ∼170 million bets), we assessed between-session chasing via time of return. Using pre-registered analyses, we assessed time of return as a function of (a) prior outcome (win/loss), (b) outcome magnitude, (c) game type (Multi-line Slots, Dice game, European Roulette and Multi-hand European Blackjack) and (d) gambler's involvement level (high/low; defined based on monetary and time expenditure). Results: Confirmatory results indicated that overall gamblers returned faster following a winning than a losing session. They returned faster when previous outcome magnitude (both wins and losses) increased. Furthermore, return times of slot gamblers were less sensitive to prior outcomes than other products. Exploratory results indicated that return times of high-involvement gamblers were less sensitive to prior outcome than low-involvement gamblers. Discussion and Conclusions: The current results indicate a pattern of both loss- and win-chasing, demonstrating that the break-even, house money and wealth effects may be at play. Decreased sensitivity to prior outcome among slot and high-involvement gamblers may be attributed to habituation. Future research could disentangle these multi-causal mechanisms, to evaluate time of return as a potential behavioral marker of harm, for better identification and mitigation of problem gambling.

title: Risk Factors Associated with Gambling in Young Adults: A Systematic Review Protocol
abstract: Background Gambling is increasingly getting recognised as a public health problem, with young adults (18-25) being identified as a particularly vulnerable group due to their ongoing neurodevelopment and increased exposure to spreading gambling environments. Individuals who adopt problematic gambling behaviours can either classify as problem gamblers or can in more severe cases meet the criteria for a clinical diagnosis for Gambling Disorder (GD). Different characteristics and traits, known as risk factors, can influence the development of these conditions. This review aims to evaluate the quantitative studies investigating risk factors contributing to problematic gambling behaviours in the young adult populations. Methods A systematic review guided by the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodology will be conducted. This review will consider quantitative and mixed-methods, where quantitative data can be extracted, evidence published from 1990 onwards on risk factors which are associated with gambling in the young adult population. Four databases will be searched as well as grey literature. Methodological quality will be assessed using the JBI critical appraisal tools based on the study designs of each study. Data extraction will be conducted using the JBI standardised extraction tools. The risk of bias will be assessed using the Quality in Prognostic Studies (QUIPS) tool to evaluate the risk-factor-outcome relationship. Discussion Gambling Disorder and Problem Gambling are a growing public health concern. The results of this review are anticipated to benefit researchers, clinicians and policymakers by providing a better understanding on key predictors of gambling-related harm in this population which would then aid in informing early intervention and prevention strategies. Protocol registration number PROSPERO 2026 CRD420261288057

title: Network structure of gambling-related cognitions and risk behaviors among sports bettors in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: a cross-sectional EBICglasso network analysis (N = 2261).
abstract: Background and aims: Sports betting is expanding rapidly in sub-Saharan Africa, yet the network structure of gambling-related cognitions and risk indicators remains understudied. This study analyzed these cognitions and their financial risk, psychological, and social correlates among DRC sports bettors. Methods: A cross-sectional sample of 2261 sports bettors (85.9% male; mean age = 25.59 years, SD = 5.79) was recruited at Kinshasa betting venues (March-May 2026). The Gambling-Related Cognitions Scale (GRCS; α = 0.924) was administered alongside financial, psychological, and social measures. Network structure was estimated using thresholded EBICglasso (γ = 0.5). Bridge centrality and sex-based invariance were assessed via NetworkComparisonTest (100,000 permutations). Results: The thresholded network retained 150 edges (density = 0.302). Guilt and G1 were the most central nodes. Bridge analysis identified guilt and social pressure as bridge nodes. Seven items showed zero bridge strength. Item-level network structure showed no global sex difference (M = 0.195, p = .121), whereas a 14-node sensitivity analysis detected an omnibus structural difference (M = 0.217, p = .022) not localized to any edge. After Bonferroni and FDR corrections, applied separately to 496 edge-level and 90 centrality-level tests, one edge (G1-G15), but no centrality index, differed by sex. Conclusions: This is among the first network analyses of gambling-related cognitions in sub-Saharan Africa, with Gambling Expectancies as the most connected cognitive domain, G1 as a central hub, and guilt and social pressure as bridge nodes. These findings extend the Interaction of Person-Affect-Cognition-Execution (I-PACE) model and inform intervention research.

title: Impacto de apuestas deportivas en menores: responsabilidad del operador, Estado y consumidor
abstract: Las apuestas deportivas digitales han experimentado un crecimiento sostenido, generando desafíos para la protección de niños, niñas y adolescentes debido a la facilidad de acceso, publicidad digital y mecanismos de registro, la presente investigación tuvo como objetivo analizar su impacto en menores y determinar la responsabilidad jurídica del operador, el Estado y los representantes legales, se realizó una revisión bibliográfica con enfoque cualitativo mediante análisis normativo, doctrinario y jurisprudencial, los resultados evidenciaron que la Constitución, el Código de la Niñez y Adolescencia y la normativa de protección de datos establecen una protección reforzada basada en el interés superior, la prioridad absoluta y la prevención de riesgos, se determinó que los operadores deben implementar mecanismos de identificación, verificación de edad y bloqueo; el Estado debe regular, supervisar y sancionar conforme a la ley; y los representantes legales deben ejercer una supervisión razonable, el análisis jurisprudencial evidenció que la regulación de las apuestas deportivas debe respetar los principios de legalidad, proporcionalidad, igualdad y seguridad jurídica, se concluye que la protección de los menores constituye una responsabilidad compartida como diferenciada, la limitada investigación sobre ludopatía infantil exige desarrollar estudios nacionales e implementar programas escolares de prevención, detección temprana, atención psicológica coordinada.

title: THE RISE OF OPTIONS CONTRACTS IN SPORTS, THE POST-MURPHY REGULATORY CONUNDRUM, AND IMPLICATIONS ON FEDERALISM
abstract: The Supreme Court’s decision in Murphy v. N.C.A.A. dismantled the federal prohibition on state-authorized sports betting and returned its primary regulatory authority over to the states. Following Murphy, states adopted widely varying sports-betting regimes. At the same time, advances in financial technology and the growing popularity of prediction markets created a new form of event-based speculation operating outside the traditional sportsbook model. Platforms such as Kalshi began offering “yes-no” contracts tied to sporting outcomes through federally regulated exchanges overseen by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, framing such products not as wagers, but as financial derivatives governed by the Commodity Exchange Act. These developments have exposed a regulatory fault line left unresolved post-Murphy. State regulators have argued that these contracts are functionally indistinguishable from sports betting and therefore subject to state gambling law. Meanwhile, exchanges such as Kalshi maintain that federal regulation preempts state enforcement efforts. The resulting litigation has forced courts to confront difficult questions concerning preemption, administrative law, and federalism. Some courts have emphasized the functional similarity between prediction markets and sports wagering in preserving state authority, while others have treated federal regulatory designation as sufficient to justify preemption. This Note argues that sports-based event contracts cannot be evaluated through formal classification alone. Rather, they reveal the unresolved tension between federal derivatives regulation and the state-centered sports wagering framework that emerged after Murphy.

title: Hot Hand Effects: Analyzing MLB Starting Pitchers in Daily Fantasy Sports and Betting Markets
abstract: This study investigates the existence and market response to the “hot hand” effect among Major League Baseball starting pitchers. Using a novel methodology that classifies pitchers as hot, cold, or neutral based on context-adjusted recent performance, we find strong evidence that short-term streaks predict daily fantasy sports (DFS) outcomes. However, these trends are not fully priced into DraftKings salaries—hot pitchers are underpriced and cold pitchers are overpriced—indicating pricing inefficiencies. In contrast, sportsbook betting lines tend to overreact, particularly for visiting hot and cold home starters. However, simulated betting strategies exploiting these trends do not yield statistically significant positive profits, suggesting that sportsbooks adjust prices to capitalize on user biases. By comparing DFS and betting markets, this paper demonstrates how institutional structures and incentives shape responses to performance signals. The findings offer new insight into pricing dynamics, market efficiency, and behavioral responses in modern sports analytics.

title: Financial Opportunities and Challenges in the Indian Sports Industry: An Empirical Analysis
abstract: The Indian sports industry has been undergoing a radical transformation and growth over the past decade with the commercialisation and media rights, sponsorships and fan engagement through digital platforms, Khelo India and the Fit India Movement are just a few of the changes that have been witnessed by the industry in this period. The success of these domestic leagues, Indian Premier League (IPL), Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) and Indian Super League (ISL) has led to a lot of investments from both domestic and international sources, which has led to a variety of revenue streams, such as broadcasting rights, merchandising, sports tourism, fantasy sports and analytics. However, there are structural problems in the sport: imbalanced infrastructure, cricket-centric funding, absence of cricket sports monetisation, governance issues and absence of financial transparency. The study is based on a quantitative, descriptive approach to understand the finances opportunities and challenges of the Indian sports industry empirically. The primary data was collected on the basis of a structured questionnaire having five point likert scale from 400 respondents which included athletes, sports administrators, journalists and sports enthusiasts who were analysed through reliability analysis, descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation and regression (ANOVA). The Cronbach's α values of all the measurement scales were within the acceptable range of 0.786-0.877. The results show that financial opportunities are highly correlated with financial problems (r = 0.591, p < 0.01), there is a strong relationship between the financial opportunities and new financial-management trends (F = 532.83, p < 0.001), the financial opportunities are a strong predictor of adoption of new financial resources (F = 373.35, p < 0.001), and the financial opportunities are a significant predictor of exploration of new opportunities and problems (F = 247.03, p < 0.001). The study finds that diversifying sources of revenue, use of FinTech and Data-driven decision making and public–private partnerships are essential for the financial sustainability of Indian sport in the long run.

title: Financial Determinants and Beliefs About Gambling Control: A Cross-National Structural Model of Problem Gambling Severity
abstract: Gambling-related harm is increasingly recognized as a public health concern, yet the role of financial factors in problem gambling remains insufficiently understood. This study examined the associations of financial knowledge, risk-oriented financial behaviour, prudent financial attitudes, and financial anxiety with problem gambling severity. A focused Health Belief Model-informed framework was used to investigate whether perceived benefits of reducing gambling, perceived barriers to gambling reduction, and gambling-related self-efficacy statistically accounted for indirect associations between financial variables and Problem Gambling Severity Index scores. Data were collected from 2,000 adults who had gambled during the previous 12 months in Italy and the United Kingdom. The measurement structure was evaluated through exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses and cross-country measurement invariance testing. Direct, indirect, and total associations were subsequently examined using multi-group structural equation modelling. Financial anxiety was positively associated with problem gambling severity in both countries, whereas financial knowledge and prudent financial attitudes showed inverse associations. Risk-oriented financial behaviour showed a positive direct association with gambling severity in Italy but not in the United Kingdom. Perceived barriers emerged as the strongest HBM-related correlate of gambling severity and accounted for the principal supported indirect associations involving financial anxiety, financial knowledge, and prudent financial attitudes. Perceived benefits and self-efficacy were not independently associated with gambling severity. These findings suggest that gambling-related harm is associated not only with financial competence and vulnerability, but also with the perceived difficulty of reducing gambling. Prevention may therefore benefit from combining financial education with measures that reduce practical, cognitive, and emotional barriers to gambling control.

title: Apostas e jogos online no brasil: desafios normativos e impactos sociais Online betting and gaming in Brazil: regulatory challenges and social impacts
abstract: Com a crescente expansão das apostas e dos jogos online, o presente artigo analisou a necessidade e os desafios da regulamentação desse setor no Brasil, destacando as lacunas existentes no atual arcabouço jurídico e os riscos decorrentes da ausência de normas consistentes. A pesquisa teve como objetivo examinar criticamente as propostas legislativas e os modelos regulatórios em comparação com a realidade do mercado nacional, considerando também a influência da publicidade e a proteção dos consumidores. Para tanto, adotou-se uma abordagem bibliográfica e documental, baseada na análise de doutrinas, legislações, artigos científicos e estudos de caso. Os resultados evidenciam que, embora o país avance com normas recentes, ainda persistem fragilidades quanto à fiscalização, à prevenção da ludopatia e à ética publicitária. Conclui-se que uma regulamentação mais clara e integrada é essencial para garantir segurança jurídica, promover práticas responsáveis e equilibrar os interesses econômicos e sociais envolvidos.

title: Apostas esportivas online e a recente regulamentação no Brasil: enquadramento e implicações da relação jurídica - Online sports betting and recent regulation in Brazil: framework and implications of the legal relationship
abstract: Objetivo: analisar em que medida a relação jurídica entre plataformas digitais de apostas esportivas e seus usuários pode ser qualificada como relação de consumo, à luz do ordenamento jurídico brasileiro e das diretrizes do Código de Defesa do Consumidor, considerando a expansão das apostas online no Brasil e as lacunas regulatórias existentes quanto à proteção jurídica do usuário. Método: adotou-se o método dedutivo, com abordagem qualitativa, de caráter bibliográfico, documental e jurisprudencial, fundamentada na análise de legislação vigente, doutrina especializada e dados informativos pertinentes ao tema. Resultados: a análise evidenciou que a relação entre apostador e plataforma reúne os elementos característicos da relação de consumo, destacando-se a vulnerabilidade do consumidor digital frente às assimetrias informacionais, bem como os riscos comportamentais e econômicos associados às apostas esportivas online. Considerações finais: conclui-se que o reconhecimento da natureza consumerista dessa relação impõe às plataformas digitais deveres ampliados de transparência, informação e responsabilidade civil, além de demandar uma atuação regulatória mais efetiva do Estado, com vistas à proteção do consumidor e à mitigação dos impactos sociais decorrentes da atividade.

title: Professionals’ Perspectives On the Role of Advanced Technologies in Responsible Gambling
abstract: Problematic gambling is associated with substantial individual and societal harms, which may be intensified by the accessibility, anonymity, and captivating design of online gambling products. In this domain, advanced technologies (e.g., artificial intelligence and data analytics) are increasingly recommended for prevention, early detection, and harm reduction. This study aimed to examine the current and potential uses of advanced technologies in gambling. Forty-five semi-structured interviews were conducted with social/legal science (n = 24) and technology (n = 21) experts. Data were analysed using thematic analysis, beginning with a deductive approach followed by an inductive analysis. A total of 182 codes were identified from social/legal science professionals, and 228 from technology experts. Four overarching themes were identified: (i) characterisation of contemporary gambling; (ii) applications and implications of advanced technologies; (iii) regulatory frameworks and challenges; and (iv) recommendations and solutions. Profit-driven design practices, heightened vulnerabilities in online gambling environments, regulatory gaps, and concerns regarding algorithmic opacity and data use were highlighted. Advanced technologies were viewed as having a dual role, with potential both to exacerbate gambling-related harm and to enable earlier identification of risky behaviours and targeted interventions. Findings indicate that responsible gambling cannot rely solely on technological solutions (e.g., behavioural monitoring and limit-setting) and should be instead integrated with community-level strategies, public education, and robust regulatory oversight. Leveraging technological innovation alongside user protection is essential, requiring interdisciplinary collaboration, a public health-oriented approach, and transparent, evidence-based and ethically governed frameworks. Implications, limitations, and future directions are discussed.

Betting on health: gambling disorder, psychological comorbidity, and the neglect of oral self-care in the post-PASPA United States
abstract: In the United States, the Supreme Court’s 2018 decision in Murphy v. National Collegiate Athletic Association struck down the federal ban on sports wagering, triggering rapid state-by-state legalization; by 2025, legal sports betting was available in 38 states and the District of Columbia, generating nearly $17 billion in commercial revenue on an estimated $167 billion in total wagers. National data indicate that roughly one in five American adults placed a legal sports bet in 2025, and helpline records show a marked rise in financial distress, depression, and relationship harm among callers who identify sports betting as their primary problem. Gambling disorder (GD), reclassified by the DSM-5 as a behavioral addiction within the same diagnostic category as substance-related disorders, carries this heavy psychiatric and financial burden, yet its oral health consequences remain almost entirely unexamined in the dental literature. This narrative review synthesizes international and United States-specific evidence on the psychological consequences of gambling disorder and proposes behavioral and physiological pathways linking this addiction to oral disease and self-neglect. The literature shows psychiatric comorbidity exceeding 80% among individuals with GD, disproportionate sleep disruption compatible with nocturnal bruxism, and an established caries and periodontal disease burden among individuals with other addictive disorders that plausibly extends to problem gamblers. We argue that gambling disorder compromises oral health primarily through the erosion of self-care rather than through direct toxic exposure, a mechanism compounded in the United States by a dental care system that remains structurally separate from general medical coverage and heavily dependent on out-of-pocket payment.

title: Markets Without Pause Regulating Online Gambling in an Era of Velocity, Revenue, and Risk
abstract: <p>Online sports betting has become structurally embedded in the American economy. Since the Supreme Court’s decision in <i>Murphy v. NCAA</i> (2018), legal sports wagering has expanded to most U.S. states, generating more than $120 billion in annual handle and over $10 billion in gross gaming revenue (American Gaming Association, 2024). State governments now rely on gambling-related receipts for education funding, infrastructure support, and budget stabilization.</p> <p>The scale of the market makes prohibition implausible. Gambling is no longer peripheral; it is fiscally and culturally integrated.</p> <p>Yet the contemporary gambling environment differs fundamentally from its twentieth-century predecessor. Digital platforms have eliminated friction between impulse and wager. In-play betting multiplies the number of wagering events per hour. Payment systems allow instantaneous deposits and rapid redeposit following losses. Algorithmic personalization calibrates promotional intensity to individual behavior.</p> <p>These structural changes alter the distribution of risk.</p> <p>Across mature gambling markets, revenue is not evenly distributed. A relatively small minority of high-intensity users typically generate a majority of operator revenue (UK Gambling Commission, 2022; Productivity Commission, 2010). This concentration has fiscal and political implications. Reducing high-intensity losses may reduce tax receipts; failing to moderate concentration may increase volatility and backlash risk.</p> <p>International evidence suggests that regulatory architecture — not legalization alone — determines stability. Jurisdictions that introduced centralized self-exclusion, default deposit limits, and data transparency early have generally experienced less political instability than those that expanded rapidly without structural guardrails.</p> <p>This paper argues that the United States stands at a transitional moment. The market is large but not yet politically destabilized. Concentration patterns are observable but not yet widely reported. Youth exposure is rising but not yet driving crisis legislation.</p> <p>Reform undertaken during stability can be calibrated and incremental. Reform undertaken after scandal tends to be blunt and disruptive.</p> <p>The policy objective is not prohibition. It is structural sustainability: reducing loss velocity and concentration while preserving legal channelization and fiscal realism.</p>

title: PSYTURK
abstract: # PSY-TURK Study 1: Substance-Related and Behavioral Addiction-Risk Indicators Among University Students in Türkiye ## Project Overview This repository contains the materials associated with PSY-TURK Study 1, a cross-sectional investigation of substance-related and behavioral addiction-risk indicators among university students in Türkiye. The study examined alcohol- and drug-related risk using the CAGE-AID and assessed addiction-related burden across ten behavioral domains, including compulsive shopping, problematic social media use, food-related addictive behavior, gaming, sex/pornography, gambling, sports betting, exercise, cryptocurrency investment, and internet broadcasting/live streaming. The project aimed to estimate prevalence, examine demographic correlates, evaluate overlap between substance-related and behavioral risk indicators, and assess the robustness of findings across alternative behavioral-threshold systems. ## Repository Contents This repository includes: * Analysis scripts used to prepare, score, and analyze the data. * Variable definitions and scoring procedures. * Behavioral-threshold specifications. * Supplementary analysis materials and documentation. * Reproducibility files necessary to recreate the reported analyses. ## Data Availability The original dataset contains sensitive information regarding mental health, substance use, addictive behaviors, and related personal experiences. To protect participant confidentiality and comply with ethical obligations, the raw dataset is not publicly available. A de-identified analytic dataset may be made available upon reasonable request, subject to applicable ethical, legal, and institutional requirements. Shared datasets will exclude direct identifiers and may include additional recoding or aggregation of potentially identifying variables. ## Code Availability All analysis scripts required to reproduce the primary and supplementary analyses are available in this repository. The code is provided for transparency, reproducibility, and secondary methodological evaluation. ## Citation If you use materials from this repository, please cite the corresponding publication: Batmaz, S., et al. (in preparation). Substance-related and behavioral addiction-risk indicators among university students in Türkiye: Overlap, correlates, and threshold sensitivity. ## Contact For questions regarding the project, data access, or reproducibility materials, please contact the corresponding author.

title: Statewide Mobile Sports Betting and Suicidal Ideation Among U.S. College Students
abstract: This preregistered study will examine whether the introduction of statewide legal mobile sports betting is associated with changes in past-year serious suicidal ideation among U.S. college students ages 18-24. Using Healthy Minds Study data from 2015-2025 and staggered state adoption of mobile sports betting, the primary analysis will estimate the event +2 treatment effect using a pairwise-balanced cohort-specific difference-in-differences design. A prespecified secondary analysis will test whether associations are stronger among students legally eligible to wager.

Exploring the Influence of Financial Misconduct Due to Online Gambling on the Learning Behavior of College Students
abstract: Online gambling has become a major global issue, increasingly linked to financial problems and poor academic performance among college students. This qualitative study investigated how financial misconduct arising from online gambling affects students' learning behavior. Focusing on the real-life experiences of eleven students at Isabela State University, Cauayan Campus, during the 2025–2026 academic year, the research explored how debt, borrowing, and chasing losses influenced their daily learning, academic focus, and overall well-being. Data were gathered through in-depth interviews and examined using thematic analysis. The study found that social media exposure, peer influence, curiosity, financial struggles, and gambling promotions are the primary catalysts for online betting. Financial misconduct led to severe consequences, including cognitive impairment in learning processes, the erosion of academic engagement and responsibility, and a sharp decline in academic performance, particularly in major subjects. Furthermore, students experienced debt as a survival tool, poor financial management, behavioral addiction, compulsion, deceptive behaviors, and significant threats to educational continuity, alongside emotional dysregulation and physical health deterioration. To cope, affected students utilized self-regulation, sought institutional help, and relied on external support systems. Ultimately, these findings underscore the critical need for universities to design comprehensive prevention and support programs. Such initiatives must address both the psychological and financial dimensions of student gambling to safeguard academic success and student well-being.

title: The Sweepstakes Casino "Loophole" and the Case for State Regulation
abstract: <div> Ever since the advent of the internet, Americans have been seeking ways to gamble online. The Supreme Court helped spur growth in this way through its decision in Murphy v. NCAA, which opened the door to legalizing sports betting. Since then, seven states have legalized online gaming, allowing individuals to play slots, blackjack, roulette, and more on their phones. However, there are platforms that offer these exact activities and operate in most states, even though iGaming is only legal in a select few. These platforms call themselves sweepstakes casinos, claiming they fall under sweepstakes regulations rather than traditional gambling laws because they lack the consideration element required to fall under traditional gambling laws, thanks to their unique dual-currency system. Because they self-classify as a sweepstakes, they argue that their platforms operate within a legal loophole and cannot be regulated through usual methods. </div> <div> &nbsp;<span> </span>Yet, looking deeper, these platforms seemingly offer nothing more than an easily accessible form of unregulated gambling. States have begun to take action against sweepstakes casinos; however, it has become increasingly clear that the only definite solution is to ban these platforms outright. If states are unwilling to classify sweepstakes casinos as unregulated gambling platforms under their existing regulatory scheme, they should pass statutes that provide a more precise definition of gambling within their borders. Further, courts faced with cases involving sweepstakes casinos should expand the gambling element of consideration to cover indirect forms of consideration, thereby eliminating the existing loophole these platforms exploit. A combined approach to these two solutions would not only solve this problem but also end the cat-and-mouse game that has plagued online gambling since its inception by strengthening gambling laws and limiting opportunities for future exploitation of regulatory loopholes. </div>

title: The Stranger at Home: Lived Experiences of Online Gambling Within the Family in Siirt, Türkiye
Social media advertising by sports betting companies and its influence on consumer behavior
abstract: Advertising for sports betting platforms on digital platforms has experienced exponential growth in recent years, capturing the attention of young people in particular through social media platforms such as X (formerly Twitter), TikTok, and YouTube. The overall objective of this study was to analyze the influence of digital sports betting advertising on the consumption behavior of young users in Ecuador, particularly in terms of their exposure to and decision-making regarding these platforms. The study employed a quantitative methodological approach supplemented by qualitative interviews, using a structured survey with a Likert scale and open-ended questions administered to users of betting platforms. The results show a high frequency of exposure to sports betting advertisements, a growing interest driven by promotions, and a widespread perception of betting as an acceptable form of entertainment, even though many users acknowledge the risks. It is concluded that advertising has a significant impact on the decision to bet, especially when it presents betting as safe and lucrative. It is recommended that clear regulatory frameworks, awareness campaigns, and critical digital literacy initiatives be implemented to mitigate the impact of advertising on vulnerable audiences.

title: Socioeconomic Impact of Sports Betting and Youth Perspectives on Regulatory Solutions in Mwanza City, Tanzania
abstract: Sports betting has expanded rapidly across Tanzanian cities, raising concerns about its financial and social effects on youth. This study examined betting behavior and its socioeconomic consequences among youth in Mwanza City, Tanzania. A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 200 respondents aged 18 years and above who had previously engaged in sports betting. Participants were recruited from betting shops, mobile money outlets, and public gathering points across six wards. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, and binary logistic regression. The findings revealed that betting was common, with 36.5% of respondents betting occasionally, 31.0% weekly, and 22.0% daily. Financial difficulties were widespread: 62.0% reported financial challenges, 55.5% experienced reduced savings, and 52.0% had borrowed money to continue betting. The most common economic consequence was difficulty meeting basic needs such as food and transport (34.0%). Social impacts were also evident, including family conflicts (54.0%) and social isolation (53.5%). These findings indicate that sports betting contributes to significant financial and social vulnerabilities among urban youth, highlighting the need for stronger regulation, public awareness campaigns, and accessible support services.

Influence of Digital Deviancy on the Learning of Behaviour the Boy-Child in Public Secondary Schools in Bayelsa State
abstract: This study investigated influence of digital deviancy on the learning behaviour of the boy-child in public secondary schools in Bayelsa State, Nigeria. It was motivated by the increasing concerns that activities such as cyber fraud and online betting divert boys from their academic pursuits. Two research questions and null hypotheses guided the study, which employed a descriptive survey design. The population comprised all male senior secondary school students across 207 public secondary schools in the state, from which a sample of 248 students was drawn. Data were collected using a structured instrument titled the Influence of Digital Deviancy and Learning Behaviour Questionnaire (DDLBQ). Mean and standard deviation were used to address the research questions, while Pearson Product Moment Correlation (PPMC) was applied to test the hypotheses at a 0.05 level of significance. Findings indicated that involvement in cyber fraud (“Yahoo-Yahoo”) and online gambling both exert a strong negative influence on students' learning behaviour, with significant correlations observed in each case. The study concluded that digital deviancy constitutes a substantial counterforce to formal education among male students. It recommended that the Bayelsa State Ministry of Education adopt comprehensive digital citizenship programmes alongside targeted, gender- responsive interventions to mitigate these challenges.

title: Is Access to Online Casino Gaming Responsible for Estimated Impacts of Online Sports Betting?
abstract: The recent spread of online sports betting in the United States has led to a rapidly expanding literature which estimates impacts of this access on a wide variety of outcomes. We show, however, that much of the variation in access to online sports betting is confounded with access to online casino gaming. Additionally, a majority of industry revenues across important subsets of treated states come from casino gaming rather than sports betting. We then replicate one early published study estimating the impacts of access to mobile sports betting on self-reported mental health, and illustrate the degree to which their results are robust to the exclusion of states with legalized casino gaming. Given the data used in other studies, as well as when impacts are most pronounced relative to legalization and COVID-induced sports shutdowns in 2020, this observation calls into question whether the estimated impacts should properly be attributed to legalized sports betting.

title: Daily Bookmaker Margin Index 2026: average bookmaker margins for 38 competitions and six market types
abstract: A daily index of the margin (overround) that bookmakers build into their prices. Each row is one day, one competition and one market type, with the number of markets measured, the number of bookmakers, and the mean, median, minimum and maximum margin in percent. This release holds 5,395 rows for 88 days (2026-07-01 to 2026-09-26), 38 competitions in 10 sport families and six market types. The file contains summary statistics only: no odds, no prices and no bookmaker names. It is intended for teaching descriptive statistics and time series, and for research on market pricing and consumer costs in wagering. The daily-updated file and codebook are at the Bet Better margin index page; method notes are at bookmaker margins: method and measurement; the same figures are served as JSON by a free API with no key. title: Market Calibration Dataset: De-Vigged Betting Probabilities vs Real Outcomes, 36,476 Observations
abstract: # Market Calibration Dataset — de-vigged betting probabilities vs real outcomes **36,476 outcome observations (both sides of 18,238 settled two-outcome betting markets)** across five sports: each row is a vig-free market-implied probability and whether the outcome happened. A modern, multi-sport dataset for studying market calibration and the favourite–longshot bias — a literature that still leans heavily on decades-old horse-racing data. | | | |---|---| | **Rows** | 36,476 (both sides of every market — the dataset nets to 0.500/0.500 by construction) | | **Markets** | 18,238 settled two-outcome markets | | **Sports** | 5 (soccer, baseball, basketball, ice hockey, Australian rules) | | **Period** | November 2024 – July 2026 (month granularity) | | **Licence** | CC BY 4.0 | ## Columns | Column | Meaning | |---|---| | `event_month` | Month the event was played (YYYY-MM) | | `sport` | Sport key | | `market_family` | `game line` (match-level markets) or `player prop` | | `market_implied_probability` | The outcome's **de-vigged** market-implied probability (vig removed across the market's outcomes), rounded to 3 dp | | `outcome` | 1 if the outcome occurred, 0 otherwise | ## Construction — read before analysing - **Both sides of every market are included.** For every observed outcome at probability *p*, its complement appears at *1−p* with the opposite result. The dataset therefore nets to exactly 0.500/0.500 overall, and calibration deviations appear as an antisymmetric curve. This is the standard construction for bias analysis and means the dataset carries **no information about any bettor's or model's selections** — only about the market itself. - **Probabilities are de-vigged**, not raw. Raw implied probabilities contain the bookmaker's margin; these have had it removed across the market's outcomes. Note that de-vig method choice affects how margin is allocated across the probability range — a caveat relevant to interpreting tail behaviour, and itself a research-worthy question the data supports. - **Sampling:** markets are those covered by an analytics pipeline across five sports; within a market, inclusion of both sides is complete by construction. Rows carry no event, team, player, bookmaker or exact-date identifiers and cannot be mapped to any individual market or price. ## Headline findings - **Betting markets are impressively well calibrated**: across every probability decile, real outcome frequencies track de-vigged implied probabilities within about ±2 percentage points. - **A small, systematic tilt survives vig removal**: outcomes priced below ~50% slightly *overperform* their vig-free probabilities (+1 to +2 points) while favourites slightly underperform — consistent with bookmakers loading their margin most heavily onto longshot prices. In raw (vigged) prices this manifests as the classic favourite–longshot bias. - Player-prop markets show a larger tilt than match-level markets, peaking around the 30–40% / 60–70% probability bands (±5 points). ## Licence and citation CC BY 4.0 — free to use, including commercially, with attribution. > Bet Better (2026). *Market Calibration Dataset: de-vigged betting probabilities vs outcomes, > 36,476 observations.* https://betbetter.world/studies/market-calibration Maintained by [Bet Better](https://betbetter.world), which also publishes the [Bookmaker Margin Panel](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21755380), a [free sports model API](https://betbetter.world/api/) and an [open AFL dataset](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21612783). > No odds, prices, bookmaker identities or wagering data are included. 18+. title: NBA Player Proposition Markets: A Two-Tier Machine Learning System with Five-Month Out-of-Sample Validation
abstract: This paper presents a validated two-tier betting system for NBA player proposition markets, developed using XGBoost, Random Forest and GLMNet models trained independently per market. A five-month walk-forward out-of-sample test across 13 markets confirmed both tiers independently profitable every month. Tier 1 (model probability >= 0.80) achieved 16.0% average monthly ROI from a $2,000 starting bankroll, reaching $12,290. Tier 2 value bets (probability 0.60-0.79) achieved 28.2% average monthly ROI, reaching $23,321. Kelly criterion sizing with per-bet and daily caps is detailed. Markets with negative out-of-sample performance were permanently excluded. Three-gate validation criteria ensured zero selection bias and zero data leakage. The system is implemented at betbetter.world.

title: Jogos instantâneos online: o que são e como funcionam em 2026
abstract: Jogos instantâneos online: o que são e como funcionam em 2026 Os jogos instantâneos online são a categoria que mais cresce no mercado brasileiro de entretenimento digital: a rodada começa e termina em segundos, sem download, sem espera pelo apito final de um jogo e sem acompanhar animações longas de rolos. Você escolhe o título, define o valor, confirma e vê o desfecho quase imediatamente. Neste guia explicamos o que são esses jogos, como funcionam por dentro, quais formatos existem hoje, por que ganharam tanto espaço no Brasil e quais cuidados separam diversão de prejuízo. O que exatamente é um jogo instantâneo Um jogo instantâneo é um formato em que o resultado é definido por um gerador de números aleatórios (RNG) e revelado em poucos segundos. Diferente dos slots tradicionais, não há uma "esteira" visual longa de símbolos; diferente das apostas esportivas, não existe um evento externo cujo desfecho precise acontecer. A rodada é autossuficiente: começa, resolve e fecha no mesmo instante. Essa característica muda a experiência de três formas. Primeiro, o ritmo: em vez de uma rodada a cada trinta segundos, o jogador pode fazer várias por minuto. Segundo, a leitura do resultado, que é binária e imediata — ganhou ou não ganhou. Terceiro, o controle de orçamento, que passa a depender inteiramente da disciplina do usuário, porque a velocidade não dá tempo para pensar entre uma rodada e outra. Como funcionam por dentro Todo jogo instantâneo sério roda sobre três pilares técnicos. 1. Gerador de números aleatórios (RNG). O resultado de cada rodada é sorteado por software auditado. Em plataformas reguladas, o RNG é testado por laboratórios independentes para garantir que os resultados sejam imprevisíveis e que a margem declarada seja a real. 2. Retorno ao jogador (RTP). O RTP indica quanto, em média, volta ao jogador ao longo de milhões de rodadas. Um RTP de 96% significa que a plataforma retém 4% no longo prazo. É uma média estatística, não uma promessa para a sua sessão. 3. Volatilidade. Diz o quão raros e quão grandes são os prêmios. Baixa volatilidade paga pouco e com frequência; alta volatilidade paga raramente e em valores maiores. Dois jogos com o mesmo RTP podem ter sensações completamente diferentes por causa disso. Quais formatos existem Crash e multiplicadores: um valor sobe e o jogador precisa sacar antes de ele "estourar". Simples de entender e extremamente rápido. Dados e roletas instantâneas: variantes curtas que resolvem em uma única rodada. Minijogos estilo "conquista" e "aviator": curvas visuais curtas com ponto de saída definido pelo usuário. Sorteios numéricos: o usuário escolhe um intervalo e o resultado sai na hora. Todos compartilham a mesma lógica: decisão rápida, resultado imediato, rodada curta. Por que cresceram tanto no Brasil Três fatores explicam a popularidade. A penetração do celular tornou o formato acessível em qualquer lugar. O Pix reduziu o atrito de depósito e saque a poucos toques. E o próprio formato casa bem com sessões curtas de lazer — a pessoa joga cinco minutos no intervalo, não precisa reservar uma hora. O resultado é uma categoria que reúne a simplicidade dos slots com a sensação de controle das apostas de evento, mas sem a espera de nenhum dos dois. Como escolher onde jogar Antes de qualquer rodada, vale verificar quatro pontos objetivos: Regulamentação e licença da operadora. RTP e volatilidade declarados de cada jogo. Limites de depósito, perda e tempo definidos por você, não pela plataforma. Velocidade e transparência do saque, especialmente em Pix. Quem faz essa checagem antes joga com informação; quem pula direto para a rodada joga no escuro. Se você quer ver como esses formatos aparecem na prática, com regras explicadas e exemplos de rodada passo a passo, temos um material dedicado em https://betaobetcasino.online/jogos-instantaneos/ — com a mecânica descrita em detalhe, sem promessa de ganho fácil. Bônus, limites e jogo responsável Bônus têm condições: exigência de aposta, prazo de validade, teto de saque e exclusões. Um bônus só vale a pena quando as condições cabem no seu jeito de jogar — não o contrário. E o ponto mais importante de todos: jogo instantâneo é entretenimento, não fonte de renda. Defina um orçamento fixo antes de começar, nunca persiga perdas, faça pausas e use as ferramentas de autoexclusão se sentir que a linha foi ultrapassada. Se o jogo deixar de ser diversão, ele deixou de fazer sentido. Perguntas frequentes Jogo instantâneo é confiável? Quando a plataforma é licenciada e o RNG é auditado por terceiros, sim — a imprevisibilidade e o RTP podem ser verificados. Dá para ganhar dinheiro de forma consistente? Não como rotina. É entretenimento com resultado aleatório: existem ganhos e existem perdas, e o RTP garante que a casa fica com uma margem no longo prazo. Qual é a diferença para os slots? A velocidade e a apresentação. Nos instantâneos a rodada resolve em segundos e não há esteira de símbolos; nos slots, a animação é parte da experiência. Preciso baixar aplicativo? Não. Os formatos instantâneos são feitos para rodar direto no navegador do celular. Como controlar o orçamento? Definindo um limite antes de jogar, separando o dinheiro de lazer e ignorando a tentativa de "recuperar" perdas. A velocidade do formato é justamente o que torna esse limite obrigatório. title: Optimal Online Bookmaking for Binary Games
abstract: In online betting, the bookmaker can update the payoffs it offers on a particular event many times before the event takes place, and the updated payoffs may depend on the bets accumulated thus far. We study the problem of bookmaking with the goal of maximizing the return in the worst-case, with respect to the gamblers’ behavior and the event’s outcome. We formalize this problem as the Optimal Online Bookmaking game, and provide the exact solution for the binary case. To this end, we develop the optimal bookmaking strategy, which relies on a new technique called bi-balancing trees, that assures that the house loss is the same for all decisive betting sequences, where the gambler bets all its money on a single outcome in each round.

title: Représentations sociales et enjeux de santé publique autour des jeux de hasard dans les villes de Cotonou, Dassa-Zoumè et Parakou au Bénin
abstract: Les jeux de hasard occupent une place croissante dans les activités récréatives et économiques au Bénin, notamment à Cotonou, Dassa-Zoumè et Parakou. Leur expansion, portée par les paris sportifs, les jeux en ligne, la loterie et les machines à sous, s’accompagne d’un intérêt accru des populations mais aussi de préoccupations de santé publique. Malgré cette popularité, les perceptions sociales qui façonnent les pratiques et influencent les comportements demeurent peu documentées. Cette étude qualitative analyse les représentations, attitudes et motivations liées aux jeux de hasard dans trois communes du pays. La collecte repose sur des entretiens semi-directifs, des focus groups et des observations de terrain, permettant de saisir la diversité des discours et des contextes. Les résultats révèlent des perceptions contrastées : le jeu est perçu à la fois comme une opportunité économique, une source de divertissement et un espace de sociabilité, mais aussi comme une activité risquée susceptible d’entraîner des pertes financières, de la dépendance et des tensions familiales. Ces perceptions influencent fortement les comportements individuels et collectifs, notamment chez les jeunes. Les données soulignent la nécessité de renforcer les actions de prévention, de sensibilisation et de régulation, afin de limiter les risques sanitaires et sociaux associés aux jeux de hasard. Gambling has become increasingly prominent within recreational and economic activities in Benin, particularly in Cotonou, Dassa-Zoumè, and Parakou. Its expansion, driven by sports betting, online gambling, lottery games, and slot machines, has sparked growing public interest, but also significant public health concerns. Despite this rise in popularity, the social perceptions that shape gambling practices and influence behavioral patterns remain poorly documented. This qualitative study explores representations, attitudes, and motivations related to gambling across three municipalities in the country. Data collection relied on semi‑structured interviews, focus group discussions, and field observations, allowing for a nuanced understanding of the diversity of discourses and contexts. The findings reveal contrasting perceptions: gambling is viewed simultaneously as an economic opportunity, a source of entertainment, and a social space, but also as a risky activity that can lead to financial loss, addiction, and family tensions. These perceptions strongly influence both individual and collective behaviors, particularly among young people. The evidence highlights the need to strengthen prevention, awareness‑raising, and regulatory measures in order to mitigate the health and social risks associated with gambling.
venue: Revue Africaine des Sciences Sociales et de la Santé Publique
