title: Celebrity Endorsements and Brand Awareness of Betking in Abak Metropolis, Nigeria
abstract: The increasing competition within Nigeria's sports betting industry has compelled operators to adopt innovative marketing communication strategies capable of strengthening brand awareness and attracting consumers. Among these strategies, celebrity endorsement has become increasingly prominent; however, empirical evidence regarding its effectiveness within the betting industry remains limited, particularly in Akwa Ibom State. This study examined the effect of celebrity endorsements on the brand awareness of BetKing in Abak metropolis. Specifically, the study investigated the influence of celebrity popularity, celebrity credibility and endorsement frequency on brand awareness. The study adopted a survey research design. The population comprised 181,717 registered BetKing customers in Abak metropolis, from which a sample of 399 respondents was determined using Taro Yamane's formula. Convenience sampling technique was employed in selecting respondents, while data were collected using structured questionnaires. A total of 397 valid questionnaires were analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression analysis with the aid of SPSS version 25. The findings revealed that celebrity popularity significantly enhanced brand awareness (β = 0.292, p 0.05). The study concluded that celebrity popularity and repeated endorsement exposure constitute the major celebrity endorsement dimensions influencing BetKing's brand awareness. The study recommended that BetKing should continue engaging highly recognised celebrities and increase the frequency of endorsement campaigns across multiple communication channels in order to strengthen consumer awareness and brand recall.

title: Local Fiscal Consequences of State Sports-Betting Tax Policy
abstract: Thirty-eight states have legalized sports betting since 2018, yet policy debates ignore local governments. We ask whether state sports betting policy affects local fiscal health. Using municipal bond yields (2018-2024) and Census of Governments data (2017-2022), we estimate an imputation difference-indifferences model exploiting staggered legalization and cross-sectional variation in tax rates. Legalization improves local fiscal conditions, but higher state tax rates diminish these gains. Across all legalizing states, bond yields fall by approximately 10 basis points and municipal sales tax revenue rises by roughly $44,000 per municipality. At the median tax rate (15%), the yield reduction is approximately 14 basis points and the revenue gain is roughly $36,000. Each percentage point increase in the state tax rate erodes these benefits. We find no extensive-margin effect on intergovernmental transfers, suggesting effects flow through consumer spending rather than revenue-sharing.

Code de la sécurité intérieure, art.L. 321-8.Le marché s'est structuré de manière inégale entre les Etats.Tandis que la France dispose d'un premier cadre, encore incomplet, l'Italie reste dans une situation plus incertaine, malgré une reconnaissance institutionnelle progressive du phénomène.Ainsi, cette différence est importante, car les deux pays appartiennent à une tradition juridique proche.Elle invite donc à s'interroger sur la manière dont deux droits répondent à un même phénomène économique.Avant d'analyser cette réponse juridique, il faut toutefois définir l'objet étudié.Le terme « e-sport » est la contraction de l'expression anglaise electronic sport, que l'on traduit généralement par « sport électronique ».Cette expression pose déjà une première difficulté, en rapprochant le jeu vidéo du sport, alors même que cette assimilation demeure discutée.Le sport renvoie traditionnellement à une activité physique, organisée autour de fédérations, de compétitions et de règles disciplinaires.L'e-sport, lui, repose sur un jeu vidéo.Ce jeu est un objet numérique.Il appartient à un éditeur privé.Il est protégé par le droit de la propriété intellectuelle.Cette spécificité distingue profondément l'e-sport du sport traditionnel.Matériellement, l'e-sport peut être défini comme la pratique compétitive et organisée du jeu vidéo, à un niveau amateur ou professionnel, il doit donc être distingué du gaming et du jeu d'argent, en effet :-Le gaming désigne la pratique de jeu vidéo à titre de loisir, dès lors il peut être occasionnel et individuel, tandis que l'esport suppose une confrontation organisée.-Autre distinction vis à vis du jeu d'argent, le joueur esport ne recherche pas l'aléa propre au pari ou à la loterie, il cherche a réaliser une performance, renvoyant à la performance sportive.Le droit français a préféré la notion de « compétition de jeux vidéos » au terme « e-sport », en effet, l'article L. 321-8 du Code de la sécurité intérieure dispose dans son deuxième alinéa « Une compétition de jeux vidéo confronte, à partir d'un jeu vidéo, au moins deux joueurs ou équipes de joueurs pour un score ou une victoire ».Le même texte écarte l'obligation d'une prise de paris sportifs préalable au déroulement de l'évènement.Cette définition, bien qu'elle pose un cadre, demeure limitée puisqu'elle vise surtout un affrontement direct entre joueurs ou équipes.Quid de certaines pratiques telles que le « speedrun » dans lequel le joueur doit finir un jeu le plus vite possible, se confrontant donc à un record et non à un joueur de manière directe.L'association française d'esport, nommée France Esports, donne une autre définition de ce phénomène en le qualifiant comme l'ensemble des pratiques permettant à des joueurs de se confronter, par l'intermédiaire d'un support électronique, principalement le jeu vidéo, de manière synchronique (en même temps) ou asynchronique (en décalé).6 6 France Esports, « Esport : pratiques et disciplines », 19 avr.2018.En revanche, si la carrière est courte, la reconversion devient nécessairement un enjeu majeur, alors même que le droit n'offre que très rarement au joueur e-sportif les mêmes garanties qu'au sportif professionnel traditionnel.La seconde spécificité tient à la transversalité qui existe entre le joueur et le créateur de contenu.Dans l'e-sport, la performance compétitive n'est pas toujours la seule source de valeur car un joueur peut également tirer des revenus du streaming, des réseaux sociaux, des partenariats commerciaux ou de la création de contenus.Cette situation brouille les frontières, un même individu pouvant être à la fois compétiteur, salarié, indépendant, influenceur, ambassadeur de marque et producteur de contenus, de sorte que la distinction entre sport, divertissement et activité commerciale devient de moins en moins nette.Cette porosité annonce déjà les difficultés de qualification qui seront abordées plus loin : le joueur est-il d'abord un sportif, un salarié, un prestataire, un artiste numérique, un influenceur, ou une figure hybride que le droit peine encore à cerner ?Autour du joueur se trouve ensuite la structure e-sportive, équivalent fonctionnel du club sportif.Son rôle est opérationnel puisqu'elle recrute les joueurs, constitue les équipes, organise les entraînements, négocie les contrats, assure la logistique et représente les joueurs dans les compétitions.Il serait donc erroné d'y voir de simples groupes amateurs de jeux vidéos : les structures les plus avancées disposent d'un encadrement étoffé, composé d'entraîneurs, d'analystes, de managers, de préparateurs, de responsables de communication, parfois même de psychologues ou de spécialistes de la performance.Certaines organisent des bootcamps, c'est-à-dire des périodes intensives de préparation, ou mettent à disposition des lieux de vie et d'entraînement inspirés des gaming houses, une même structure pouvant par ailleurs être présente sur plusieurs jeux, avec des rosters distincts selon les disciplines.Cette organisation confirme que l'e-sport s'est véritablement professionnalisé.La structure ne se limite pas à inscrire des joueurs à des compétitions : elle gère une activité économique à part entière, qui suppose de construire à la fois une stratégie sportive et une stratégie commerciale.Elle cherche évidemment à gagner, mais elle cherche tout autant à exister médiatiquement, ces deux objectifs se révélant indissociables l'un de l'autre.La Karmine Corp, de son côté, a construit un modèle communautaire d'une grande puissance, capable de mobiliser massivement son public, y compris dans des enceintes traditionnellement réservées au spectacle ou au sport.L'organisation d'événements tels que le KCX, notamment à l'Accor Arena, illustre bien cette capacité à transformer une simple équipe e-sportive en un véritable phénomène communautaire, dépassant le cadre strict de la compétition.LDLC OL constitue

title: Gambling behavior among adolescent and young recreational athletes: the role of gender, gambling modality, and sport characteristics.
abstract: Adolescence and youth are periods of increased vulnerability to risk behaviors, including gambling, particularly among athletes. The present study aimed to examine 1) the prevalence and severity of gambling, 2) gender differences in gambling-related behaviors, and 3) associations between sport modality, betting on one's own sport, and engagement in specific gambling activities with gambling severity and motives among recreational athletes. The sample consisted of 244 athletes aged 15 to 35 years ( M = 20.58, SD = 4.58), of whom 68% were male. Gambling severity and motives were assessed, along with sport type, involvement in different modalities of gambling activities, and betting on the sport they practiced. Results indicated that 73% of the participants had gambled in their lifetime, and 16.3% presented at-risk or problem gambling behaviors. Males showed higher involvement in strategic and online gambling, higher gambling severity, and stronger gambling motives than females. Regression analyses indicated that online gambling, card games, and sports betting were associated with higher gambling severity. Furthermore, betting on own's sport and participation in specific gambling types (particularly slot machines) were related to higher enhancement, social, coping, and financial motives. Early identification of at-risk athletes, with attention to gender differences in gambling behaviors and motives, may help in developing tailored educational and preventive strategies within recreational sports environments.

title: Implications of Legalized Sports Betting for Family Well-Being and Tax Policy
abstract: Sports betting has expanded rapidly in the United States since the 2018 Supreme Court decision in Murphy v. National Collegiate Athletic Association, which allowed states to legalize it. Since then, 38 states have legalized sports betting and 30 allow online sports betting. Recent work has documented negative effects of access to sports betting on household financial health and stability, but the downstream effects on the families and children of bettors are largely unknown. This project studies the causal effects of access to legal sports betting on family formation and well-being — including marriage, fertility, home ownership, earnings, and education. The identifying variation is the staggered rollout of sports-betting legalization (brick-and-mortar and online) across states beginning around 2018. A secondary, exploratory component examines compliance with tax-reporting requirements for gambling winnings and estimates the associated forgone tax revenue.

title: Betting on Tomorrow: Prediction Markets and the Tax Treatment of Event Contracts&nbsp;&nbsp;
abstract: Prediction markets purport to reveal the future. Yet they also present a more <br> immediate legal question: when an individual purchases a contract paying one <br> dollar if a candidate wins an election, is that individual investing or wagering? <br> The distinction matters because federal income tax law treats investment and <br> gambling quite differently. <br> Event-contract markets permit participants to wager on elections, inflation <br> reports, public-health developments, and numerous other contingencies. Artificial <br> intelligence and frictionless platform design can personalize wagering <br> opportunities, accelerate trading, and cause bets to resemble conventional <br> investments. Although many event contracts resemble recreational wagering in <br> their design, participation, and expected returns, their regulation under financial- <br> market statutes confers an investment-like identity. Tax law may therefore impose <br> different consequences on economically equivalent wagers merely because one <br> occurs through a sportsbook and another through a regulated exchange. <br> This Article examines that incongruity. It considers whether event contracts <br> should qualify as capital assets or instead fall within the tax rules applicable to <br> gambling. Drawing upon economic-substance principles and theories of tax <br> equity, the Article argues that most retail event-contract activity is better <br> understood as consumption-oriented wagering than as profit-motivated <br> investment. Capital treatment, it demonstrates, elevates form over substance, <br> undermines horizontal equity, and permits platforms and participants to exploit <br> regulatory classifications for tax advantage. <br> The Article then proposes a practical framework for harmonizing the taxation of <br> event contracts with existing gambling rules while preserving investment <br> treatment for bona fide commercial hedging. More broadly, it demonstrates how <br> tax law should respond when technological innovation erodes established <br> boundaries among finance, entertainment, and wagering.

title: Electronic gambling engagement and psychosocial outcomes among students at the University of Ibadan, Nigeria: a theory of planned behavior perspective.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The proliferation of electronic gambling in Nigeria presents a significant public health concern among youths facing economic adversity. This study applied the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to investigate the socio-cognitive drivers and self-reported psychosocial consequences of electronic gambling engagement among students at the University of Ibadan. Electronic gambling is defined here as any gambling activity conducted through electronic devices, including mobile phones, laptops, and computers, encompassing mobile sports betting applications, web-based casino platforms, and online poker. METHODS: A descriptive cross-sectional survey design was employed. Data were collected from 403 undergraduate and postgraduate students at the University of Ibadan using stratified random sampling and a structured self-administered questionnaire adapted from validated instruments. Analyses included descriptive statistics, scale reliability assessment, and binary logistic regression. RESULTS: The lifetime prevalence of electronic gambling was 49.6%. Positive attitudes toward gambling, subjective norms involving peer approval, and perceived behavioral control were all significant predictors of gambling engagement (p < .001). Economic hardship was the strongest predictor in the model (OR = 3.06). Among participants who reported gambling, 50.9% reported increased stress and anxiety, 48.6% reported financial strain, and 42.6% reported negative academic consequences. PRACTICAL IMPLICATIONS: University health and counseling services should integrate validated gambling screening tools into routine student health assessments. Interventions should address both the economic motivations and the cognitive distortions sustaining gambling engagement. Prevention campaigns should target the specific TPB constructs validated in this study. Institutional policy must also address the structural driver of economic hardship through expanded work-study programs and student financial support initiatives.

title: More frequent use of live sports-betting features is associated with increased risk of gambling harm: Evidence from a case-control design.
abstract: BackgroundMany theories of gambling harm propose that interactive design features of sports-betting platforms confer risk of harm by enabling cyclical patterns of repeated gambling engagement. This exploratory study investigated whether such features were used more frequently by people at higher risk of gambling harm relative to a demographically matched lower-risk control group.MethodsThis study used a case-control design to compare a group of 85 people at higher risk of gambling harm (PGSI 5+) with an age- and gender-matched control group at lower risk of harm (n = 84, PGSI 0-4). We compared the frequency with which groups self-reported using in-play betting, instant cash-out, multi and micro bets, social betting, and viewing live-streamed events within a betting app.ResultsThe higher-risk group reported more frequent use of in-play betting and instant cash-out and were more likely to report streaming live sporting events within a betting app. Higher-risk participants were also more likely to make an immediate deposit to qualify for a marketing offer, and both groups reported being more likely to make risky bets when using bonus funds. We observed no group differences in the frequency of use of multis, micro-bets, or social betting.ConclusionsOur findings were broadly consistent with the theory that design features of modern betting platforms contribute to gambling harm by facilitating continuous engagement. A notable finding was that in-app streaming of live events was more common among people at higher risk of gambling harm, consistent with a novel prediction made by the motivating theory.

title: Testing the Probabilistic Calibration of NBA Trade Markets
abstract: This paper tests whether NBA “Next Team” sportsbook markets are probabilistically calibrated at the trade deadline. Using an archival dataset of destination-specific player trade markets, this paper reconstructs 38 player-events across five pooled seasons from 2020–21 through 2025–26. Each event matches a sportsbook-implied probability for a player to join a specific team with the realized transaction outcome. Market efficiency is evaluated using the Brier Score, baseline forecast comparisons, and a calibration curve. The pooled Brier Score is 0.1825, compared to 0.1330 for a naïve base-rate forecast, yielding a Brier Skill Score of -0.373. The market therefore performs worse than a forecaster who assigns the same base-rate probability to every event. The calibration curve shows over-prediction in every probability bin, with the largest errors at higher quoted probabilities. These findings do not support the hypothesis that NBA trade markets are well calibrated.

abstract: Esta investigación analiza comparativamente la publicidad de las apuestas deportivas privadas y de las loterías estatales en España, y su impacto en la percepción ciudadana. Mediante un diseño cualitativo que combina entrevistas semiestructuradas y análisis de contenido de cuatro spots emblemáticos, se observa una clara asimetría simbólica: las loterías se enmarcan como tradición afectiva y solidaridad, mientras las apuestas deportivas se asocian a riesgo, adicción y vicio. Los resultados muestran cómo la comunicación contribuye a normalizar el juego público y a estigmatizar el privado, tensionando los objetivos de protección al consumidor y recaudación estatal.

title: Brazil&#39;s Ban On Online Betting And The Income That Does Not Return To The Market
abstract: On 25 September 2026, Provisional Measure No. 1,394 prohibited the exploitation, offering and advertising of fixed-odds betting in Brazil, ending a regulated market that had operated since January 2025. This essay sets aside the polarised debate between economic freedom and public health to ask a prior, economic question: what happens to household income when it stops circulating through commerce, industry and services and begins to flow to betting platforms? Drawing on official data from the Central Bank of Brazil and the Ministry of Finance, and on estimates by the Celso Furtado Centre, the University of São Paulo's Made research centre, the National Confederation of Commerce and the Institute for Health Policy Studies, it distinguishes gross wagers from households' net loss, places that loss between a floor of roughly R$ 35 billion and a ceiling of R$ 62.5 billion for 2025, and traces where the retained revenue goes: modest tax collection, negligible formal employment, and profits that may be remitted abroad. It then confronts the classic 'mere transfer' objection of gambling economics and argues that, given the asymmetry of multipliers, the compromised nature of the bettor's choice and the externalities borne by third parties, the transfer is not neutral. The essay closes by examining the legal risks of the ban, including migration to illegal markets, compensation claims and the constitutional regime of provisional measures, and concludes that the measure's success will depend less on its text than on the State's capacity to prevent that income from merely changing address.

title: Digital Surveillance, Athlete Rights and Contractual Restrictions in High-Performance Sports: A Human Rights-Based Analysis
abstract: Amaç: Bu çalışmanın temel amacı, küresel bir endüstriye dönüşen yüksek performans sporunda, matbu sözleşmelerle profesyonel sporcuların sivil otonomileri ve serbest dolaşım hakları üzerinde kurulan kurumsal hegemonyanın (asimetrik ahlak hükümleri, transfer kısıtlamaları ve siber-fiziksel gözetim) ulusal normlar (TBK, KVKK) ve uluslararası insan hakları (AİHS, GDPR, AB Hukuku) bağlamındaki hukuki meşruiyetini incelemektir.Yöntem: Disiplinlerarası nitel araştırma desenlerinden geleneksel (narratif) derleme yöntemine dayanan bu araştırmada; güncel ampirik çalışmalar (2024-2026), ulusal spor regülasyonları ile Avrupa İnsan Hakları Mahkemesi (AİHM), Avrupa Adalet Divanı (CJEU) ve Uluslararası Spor Tahkim Mahkemesi (CAS) içtihatları analiz edilmiştir.Bulgular: Araştırma sonucunda, karşılıklılık ilkesinden yoksun ahlak hükümlerinin sporcuların sivil ifade özgürlüğünü daralttığı ve FIFA'nın transfer regülasyonlarının sporcuların serbest dolaşım hakkını ihlal ettiği saptanmıştır. Ayrıca, biyometrik veri izninin asimetrik güç dengesi nedeniyle hukuken sakat bir katılım ön şartına dönüştüğü, bu verilerin spor bahisleri sektörüyle kesişmesinin ciddi mahremiyet riskleri doğurduğu ve kesintisiz siber gözetimin sporcularda klinik düzeyde teknostres yarattığı doğrulanmıştır. AİHM'in Temmuz 2025 tarihli Semenya v. Switzerland Büyük Daire kararı ve CJEU'nun Ekim 2024 tarihli Lassana Diarra kararıyla Lex Sportiva'nın mutlak özerkliğinin kırılarak, insan hakları ve AB hukukunun spor yönetiminde zorunlu bir denetim standardı hâline geldiği belirlenmiştir.Sonuç: Sonuç itibarıyla, modern spor sözleşmelerindeki asimetrik hükümlerin ve dijital gözetimin sporcunun temel haklarını ölçüsüzce ihlal ettiği değerlendirilmiş olup; adil bir ekosistem için sporcu veri egemenliğinin tanınması, dağıtık veri sistemlerinin kullanılması ve fesih ile transferlerde hukuki karşılıklılığın tesisi gereklilik arz etmektedir.

title: Peripheral Mending at the Edges of Sports Journalism: Metajournalistic Discourse of the Terry Rozier Sports Gambling Arrest
abstract: This study looks at opinion articles and sports columns in the aftermath of Terry Rozier’s illegal gambling arrest. Rozier was arrested for allegedly conspiring with organized crime rings and was accused of taking himself out of games to manipulate prop bets. The aftermath of the incident prompted a barrage of metajournalistic discourse, where writers attempted to paradigm repair sports media and the leagues relationships with sports betting corporations. Using textual analysis, this study analyzed 36 articles that wrote about sports gambling’s influence on the NBA and sports media. The findings suggest that journalists invoked paradigm repair tactics to defend the field of sports journalism from perceptions of illegitimacy but also attempted to repair the image of the NBA as an object of journalistic coverage. We dub this tactic peripheral mending , which demonstrates how mutualistic relationships further blur journalisms’ professional boundaries.

title: Prevalence, Patterns, and Sociodemographic Determinants of Gambling Participation Among Community Adults in Urban Nigeria: A Cross-Sectional Study from Obio-Akpor, Rivers State
abstract: Abstract Background Nigeria has experienced rapid expansion of mobile sports betting, yet community-level data on gambling prevalence, patterns, and sociodemographic determinants in the South-South geopolitical zone are entirely absent. This study examined gambling participation, primary gambling type, frequency, expenditure, and their sociodemographic correlates among adults in Obio-Akpor Local Government Area (LGA), Rivers State. Methods A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted in six wards of Obio-Akpor LGA using multistage sampling. A total of 468 adults participated (response rate 93.2%). Gambling prevalence, type, frequency, and weekly expenditure were assessed via structured questionnaire. Chi-square tests examined sociodemographic associations; binary logistic regression identified independent predictors of gambling participation. Ethics approval: UPH/CEREMAD/REC/MM118/087. Results Twelve-month gambling prevalence was 31.2% (n = 144/461). Sports betting predominated (49.6%), followed by online applications (34.8%). Daily gambling was reported by 40.3% of gamblers; 29.4% spent ₦10,000–19,999 weekly, representing 57–114% of weekly income for the lowest earners. Gender (χ²=36.815, p < 0.001), educational attainment (χ²=7.369, p = 0.025), and monthly income (χ²=10.019, p = 0.018) were significantly associated with gambling participation. After adjustment, male gender was the sole independent predictor (AOR = 3.76; 95% CI: 2.36–6.01; p < 0.001). Conclusion Gambling is prevalent and financially intensive in Obio-Akpor, disproportionately affecting educated young men. Findings support urgent regulatory reform, targeted digital prevention, and integration of gambling screening into primary care in Rivers State.

title: Online sports betting in Brazil: regulation, socioeconomic impacts, and the protection of vulnerable consumers
abstract: Online sports betting has established itself as one of the fastest-growing economic and social phenomena in Brazil in recent years, especially after the legalization of fixed-odds betting by Law No. 13.756/2018 and the effective regulation promoted by Law No. 14.790/2023. This study analyzes the regulatory framework for online betting in Brazil, the social impacts resulting from the expansion of digital platforms, and the legal challenges related to the protection of vulnerable consumers. The research is characterized as applied, exploratory, and descriptive, using a mixed-methods approach (qualitative and quantitative), with analysis of legislation, judicial decisions, regulatory norms, and official statistical data. The results demonstrate that regulation represented an important advance for the organization of the sector; however, challenges related to oversight, abusive advertising, protection of highly vulnerable consumers, prevention of gambling addiction, and combating illegal operators persist. The jurisprudential analysis identified a trend towards applying the strict liability foreseen in the Consumer Protection Code to platforms that fail to implement effective responsible gambling mechanisms. A high incidence of debt among bettors, market concentration in economically vulnerable groups, and an increase in cases related to gambling disorder were also observed. It is concluded that the effectiveness of the Brazilian regulatory model depends on the adoption of integrated public policies, continuous oversight, and the strengthening of consumer protection mechanisms.

title: Long-distance yardage: the socioemotional functionality of fantasy football among American men
abstract: Over 50 million people in the United States are active fantasy sports players, with Fantasy Football (FF) being the most popular. The present study examined potential social predictors of FF participation, with an emphasis on social inclusion – which was assessed by measuring one’s need to belong, fear of rejection, loneliness and depression. We hypothesised that these social variables would positively correlate with other motivators for playing FF. Two dependent measures were created to assess FF participation – Involvement and Time Commitment. Involvement was positively correlated with one’s sensitivity to rejection. Time Commitment was not significantly predicted by any of the above. Participants who have a greater sensitivity to rejection may be playing FF as a means of staying connected to friends, while not devoting significant amounts of time to ensuring their FF team(s) perform(s) well. Both FF Involvement and Time Commitment positively correlated with Dwyer and Kim’s (2011) Motivational Scale for FF Participation (MSFFP). Specifically, Involvement positively correlated with the MSFFP Competition subscale, and Time Commitment positively correlated with the Social Interaction and Entertainment/Escape subscales. Although loneliness did not correlate with FF Involvement and Time Commitment, loneliness positively correlated with the Social Interaction subscale, and negatively correlated with the Entertainment/Escape subscale.

title: Profiles of service use among patients with gambling disorders
abstract: Background and aims: Service use data among patients with gambling disorder (GD) remains scarce. This exploratory study aimed to identify the service use profiles associated with social and health conditions, gambling games or chronicity (≥ 5 years), and subsequent adverse outcomes. Methods: In 2012-2013, 2,311 patients (72% men, 45 years [SD: 13.60]) were recruited from addiction treatment centers in Quebec (Canada); their administrative data were merged with provincial health and education data (1979-2022). Latent class analysis identified profiles related to GD treatment received (2009-2021) and other service use in the 12 months before index date (last GD records). Multiple multinomial logistic and Cox regressions examined associations with patient conditions and subsequent outcomes over 12 months (acute care, suicidal behaviors, death). Results: Profile 2 patients (35% of sample) exhibited the most chronic GD, and high use of GD and other services. Profile 4 (20%) reported the worst social and health conditions, received no GD treatment, and showed moderate use of other services. Profile 1 (15%) included patients with the best conditions, but moderate GD treatment and low use of other services. Mostly composed of patients aged 35+ years, Profile 3 (30%) received low GD treatment but high general practitioner care. Patients in Profiles 4 and 2 reported the worst conditions and highest rates of adverse outcomes - although Profile 2 received the best care overall. Conclusion: GD treatment and other care may be strengthened and better coordinated. Screening, motivational interventions, and referrals to care could be consolidated. Profiles 4 and 2 may benefit from more long-term care.

title: Supervising the Omnipresent Casino: Evaluating the Role of State and Local Regulation in Stemming Youth Addiction to Sports Gambling
abstract: Since 2018, state legalization of sports betting and the industry’s corresponding proliferation has driven an epidemic of youth addiction. Current state legislation and regulations do little to combat youth addiction. Many legal scholars emphasize the value that a federal regulatory regime would provide to reign in youth sports betting. This Note explores the value that state and local government can have in the sports gambling space. To illustrate the unique importance of state and local legislation and regulation of sports betting, this Note analogizes to another addictive product with a history of youth addiction: nicotine. Nicotine has been a regulatory target of states and localities for decades. By investigating the analogous histories of the nicotine and sports betting industries, this Note highlights three main advantages to allowing states and localities to regulate an addictive product: speed, proximity to constituents, and the ability to experiment with policy innovation. At bottom, this Note asserts that regardless of the prospect of federal sports betting legislation, state and local governments must remain empowered to legislate and regulate sports betting.

title: Internet Habits, Problematic Internet Use, and Online Risk Practices Among Adolescents With ADHD in Spain
abstract: BACKGROUND: In recent years, there has been growing scientific concern about digital habits, online risk practices and problematic internet use (PIU) among adolescents with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). This exploratory study aims to compare: (1) internet use habits; (2) PIU; and (3) online risk practices (i.e., active and passive sexting, sextortion, pornography consumption, online gambling, and contact with strangers) among adolescents with and without ADHD. METHOD: = 1.79; 51.1% girls; 5.9% ADHD) was assessed (intentional sampling). RESULTS: The results indicated that adolescents with ADHD had different Internet and video game use habits, as well as a significantly higher rate of PIU compared to their peers without ADHD (25.8% vs. 18%). They also had a higher rate of sextortion, online gambling, and pornography use. In addition, significant gender differences of particular interest were observed. CONCLUSIONS: These findings underline the need to address the particularities of adolescents with ADHD and their environment in order to promote safer use of the technology.

title: Emergency Department Visits for Gambling Disorders After the Legalization of Single-Event Sports Betting and Rapid Expansion of Online Gambling.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Online gambling and single-event sports betting have been legalized and expanded in North America. Although these changes have raised concerns over increased gambling-related harms, the impacts of gambling expansion are not well understood. This study examined changes in gambling-related emergency department visits after the legalization of single-event sports betting and privatized online gambling in Ontario, Canada. METHODS: This was a population-based study of all individuals in Ontario, Canada, aged ≥10 years, who were eligible for universal health coverage (N=17,353,640) between January 2012 and June 2025. An interrupted time series design estimated changes in the rates of emergency department visits for gambling disorders after online gambling liberalization in April 2022, overall and by age and sex. RESULTS: Over 14 years, there were 952 emergency department visits for gambling disorders from 757 unique individuals (mean [SD] age=41.8 [14.9] years; 72.0% male). The mean quarterly rates of emergency department visits for gambling disorders were 31.3% higher during the period after liberalization than before (1.28-1.68 per 1,000,000 individuals), with increases observed in males (1.81-2.63 per 1,000,000) but not in females (0.77-0.74 per 1,000,000). Visits were stable before liberalization, showed no immediate change on implementation, but began to increase by 7% per quarter (incidence rate ratio=1.07, 95% CI=1.04, 1.10). By the end of the study period (in April-June 2025), the rate of emergency department visits for gambling disorders was estimated to be 99.0% (incidence rate ratio=1.99, 95% CI=1.48, 2.67) higher overall and 154.0% (incidence rate ratio=2.54, 95% CI=1.15, 5.63) and 116.0% (incidence rate ratio=2.16, 95% CI=1.18, 3.95) higher in males aged 10-29 years and 30-44 years, respectively, than the expected rates without gambling market liberalization. CONCLUSIONS: Online gambling expansion with legal single-event sports betting was associated with a doubling of the rates of severe cases of gambling disorders, with increases occurring only in young men. Although such visits were rare, they may reflect broader population increases in gambling harms.

title: Help-seeking for gambling problems following expansion of Ontario's online gambling market and legalization of single-event sports betting.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Online gambling and sports betting have recently been legalized and expanded in North America. We aimed to evaluate long-term changes in the frequency of gambling-related helpline contacts in the province of Ontario following the launch of a government-operated online gambling platform (PlayOLG) in January 2015 and the expansion of private online gambling, including single-event sports betting, in April 2022. METHODS: We conducted an interrupted time-series analysis of contacts with Ontario's free 24-hour mental health and addictions helpline (ConnexOntario) between January 2012 and September 2025. We used segmented linear regression to compare immediate, gradual, and overall changes in monthly rates of gambling-related contacts after gambling expansion in January 2015 and April 2022 overall and by age and gender subgroups. RESULTS: Over 13 years, ConnexOntario received 745 716 contacts, including 37 087 (5.0%, mean age 39 yr, 68.2% men) related to gambling. The mean monthly rate of gambling-related contacts per 1 000 000 individuals aged 15 years and older was stable over time before the launch of PlayOLG (13.4); the rate increased after Play-OLG's launch (17.0) and further increased following privatization (26.2). Compared with the scenario in which PlayOLG never launched, the estimated effect was 9.3 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.04 to 17.5) additional monthly contacts per million individuals aged 15 years and older in February 2022 (an approximately 80.7% increase). Compared with the scenario in which neither PlayOLG nor private online gambling was allowed, the estimated effect was 20.8 (95% CI 8.5 to 33.2) additional monthly contacts per million individuals aged 15 years and older in September 2025 (an approximately 198.3% increase). Increases in gambling-related contacts occurred almost exclusively in adolescent boys and men aged 15 to 44 years. Compared with no private online gambling, and no private online gambling or PlayOLG, gambling-related contacts in adolescent boys and men aged 15 to 24 years were estimated to have increased by 144% and 337.8%, respectively. INTERPRETATION: The introduction of online gambling and subsequent privatization with single-event sports betting were each associated with substantial increases in gambling-related helpline contacts, specifically in adolescent boys and young men, suggesting increased gambling problems, care-seeking, or both. This underscores the need to strengthen preventive measures and treatment access.

title: Public health implications of the deregulation and privatization of online and sports gambling in Canada.
abstract: Recent legislative changes have allowed the rapid expansion of online and sports gambling in Ontario. These changes include the privatization of the online and sports gambling market and the legalization of marketing practices for private operators, leading to an unprecedented growth in opportunities and inducements to gamble. While the stated objectives of these reforms centre on economic growth, consumer choice, and consumer protections, the potential public health implications of this policy shift demand urgent attention. This commentary argues for the necessity of applying a public health lens to understand the wide range of potential harms associated with Ontario's gambling policy changes, particularly as other jurisdictions in Canada and across the Americas consider adopting similar approaches. It advocates for targeted research that reframes policy debates around gambling, moving away from a narrow focus on individual responsibility and towards a broader understanding informed by environmental, social, and commercial determinants of health. The public health community must step up to provide the public and decision-makers with the evidence needed to mitigate harm, protect vulnerable populations, and advance equitable health outcomes.

title: The NCAA’s campaign to “draw the line” against gamblers harassing student-athletes
abstract: College student-athletes have increasingly become targets of abusive messages from fans who lost money gambling on their games. The National Collegiate Athletic Association’s (NCAA) concern about student-athlete mental health and well-being led it to launch the “Draw the Line” campaign in 2024 to address harassment stemming from sports gambling. This article evaluates the NCAA’s Draw the Line campaign through public health communication and agenda-setting theoretical frameworks. Public health communication campaigns must address the audience resistance barriers to behavior change, specifically the applicability to self and the efficacy of treatment recommendations. Agenda-setting addresses each of these audience resistance barriers through issue exposure and the facts emphasized in the messaging influencing public salience. The NCAA hopes that greater awareness and the proper information about sports gambling and abusive messages being sent to student-athletes will curtail this harassment behavior.

title: Analyzing Media Conversations Around Sports Gambling Within the Context of Vulnerable AudiencesTrevor Fox
abstract: This study examines how newspaper coverage of sports betting (2023–2024) shapes public discourse around gambling. Through mixed-methods content analysis of 105 randomly sampled articles, guided by agenda-setting, framing, and cultivation theories, findings reveal that coverage prioritizes regulation and scandals over vulnerable populations, frames betting positively at the macro level but negatively at the individual level, and largely omits the academic evidence base on gambling harms.

title: Apuestas online, sobreendeudamiento y gobiernos locales: el rol del municipio frente a las nuevas vulnerabilidades digitales
abstract: La expansión de las plataformas digitales de apuestas deportivas y el crecimiento de los mecanismos de crédito inmediato han configurado nuevas formas de vulnerabilidad social que desafían los modelos tradicionales de intervención estatal.La masificación de las apuestas online durante eventos deportivos de alcance global, como la Copa Mundial de Fútbol, ha incrementado la exposición de niños, niñas, adolescentes y jóvenes adultos a prácticas potencialmente adictivas, mientras que la disponibilidad de financiamiento digital favorece procesos de sobreendeudamiento que afectan la economía familiar.Ambos fenómenos comparten características que los profundizan:-Ausencia de regulación del Estado nacional (en el caso de las apuestas online cuenta con media sanción un proyecto de ley que regula su publicidad).-Sobreexposición mediática de la publicidad sobre los beneficios que poseen dichas actividades.-Sensación de inmediatez y casi nula dificultad para el acceso de absolutamente todas las personas a través de las plataformas (en el caso de los créditos es menos sencillo para menores, pero no imposible a través de billeteras digitales).

title: 1XBET addiction at general Lansana conte university of Sonfonia-Conakry: Scope of analysis of university results
abstract: This study aims to identify the factors explaining 1xbet addiction among students at the General Lansana Conté University of Sonfonia, Conakry, and to analyze the effects of 1xbet addiction on their academic performance. To this end, a quantitative survey was conducted with 325 student gamblers at the General Lansana Conté University of Sonfonia, Conakry. To better define the scope of this study, we used the Sharpe and Tarrier model (1993). We were thus able to show that the hope of quick profits, the pursuit of easy money, social influence, aggressive advertising from betting platforms, bonus offers, and financial incentives are the factors that explain 1xbet addiction among students at the General Lansana Conté University of Sonfonia, Conakry. Furthermore, this game has enormous consequences for these students on a social level (social isolation, sleep disorders, delinquency, theft, etc.); a financial level (financial ruin, debt, even over-indebtedness, etc.); and an academic level, as they devote most of their time to placing bets at the expense of their studies; this is the root cause of the failures observed in university settings. To better guide them regarding the risks associated with online sports betting addiction, several suggestions have been made, the most essential of which are: organizing awareness sessions on the risks associated with sports betting; integrating financial education programs into students' curricula; encouraging the practice of sports, cultural, or artistic activities to entertain students and offer them healthy alternatives to sports betting; and controlling access to online betting platforms.

title: Proceedings of ADVANCE 2026 - 13th International Workshop on ADVANCEs in ICT Infrastructures and Services
abstract: Complete proceedings of ADVANCE 2026, the 13th International Workshop on ADVANCEs in ICT Infrastructures and Services, held in Florianópolis, Brazil. The volume gathers the 20 contributions presented during the six technical sessions of the workshop (12 full papers and 8 short papers), together with the foreword, the keynote lecture by Prof. Jonice Oliveira (Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil) and the invited talk by Prof. Antônio Mauro Barbosa de Oliveira (IFCE, Brazil). The ADVANCE workshop series, launched in 2012, is an international forum where researchers, practitioners and engineers from academia and industry discuss emerging trends in ICT infrastructures, networking and distributed services.

title: Online sports gambling and financial wellbeing in the United States
abstract: Abstract Online sports gambling expanded rapidly in the United States since 2018. This article uses a nationally representative sample survey in early 2025 to measure who is gambling, how much, and online sports gambling’s association with financial wellbeing and decision-making. Gambling in a casino was still more common than online sports gambling in early 2025, but the populations appear distinct, suggesting that sports gambling rapidly expanded the gambling population. Three-quarters of online sports gamblers were male. They were typically younger and had higher incomes than either non-gamblers or casino gamblers. Sports gambling was not statistically associated with lower financial wellbeing or a higher likelihood of difficulty paying bills but was associated with higher rates of revolving credit card debt and did cause some financial distress. One-third of sports gamblers engaged in high-intensity gambling which could indicate problems. Sports gamblers rated their ability to make complex financial decisions higher than non-gamblers, yet they were more impatient and more likely to be overconfident.
venue: Journal of Financial Literacy and Wellbeing

title: Ludopatia e crescimento das apostas esportivas: epidemiologia e desafios para o Sistema Único de Saúde
abstract: Objetivo: Analisar a prevalência da ludopatia associada às apostas esportivas no Brasil e discutir seus impactos sobre o Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS), à luz do crescimento do mercado de apostas após sua liberação em 2018. Métodos: Trata-se de uma revisão bibliográfica qualitativa, realizada a partir da análise de artigos indexados no PubMed entre 2018 e 2025, nos idiomas português, espanhol e inglês, gratuitos na íntegra e alinhados aos objetivos da revisão. Para contextualizar o cenário brasileiro, também foram incorporados dados provenientes de instituições oficiais e fontes jornalísticas. Resultados: Estima-se que 1,4 milhão de brasileiros apresentem ludopatia diagnosticada, enquanto cerca de 11 milhões exibem comportamento de risco. O perfil predominante é composto por homens jovens, com ensino médio completo e baixa renda. A ludopatia mostrou associação com ansiedade, depressão, uso de substâncias, endividamento, isolamento social e aumento do risco de suicídio, especialmente entre adolescentes. Observou-se aumento superior a 200% na procura por atendimentos relacionados ao transtorno; entretanto, apenas cerca de 1.200 casos foram oficialmente registrados no SUS em 2024, sugerindo importante subnotificação e sobrecarga assistencial. Conclusão: O transtorno do jogo relacionado às apostas esportivas configura-se como um problema de saúde pública já consolidado no Brasil, com impactos significativos na saúde mental e no funcionamento do SUS. Os achados reforçam a urgência de medidas regulatórias sobre a publicidade de apostas, da implementação de estratégias preventivas e da ampliação do acesso à rede de atenção psicossocial, especialmente para populações vulneráveis.

title: Educação financeira como estratégia de prevenção ao comportamento de risco em apostas entre jovens
abstract: A educação financeira pode desempenhar um papel fundamental na prevenção do vício em apostas entre jovens ao proporcionar o desenvolvimento de habilidades de gestão financeira, autocontrole e tomada de decisões responsáveis. O objetivo desse trabalho é analisar de que forma a educação financeira influencia na prevenção ao comportamento de risco em apostas entre jovens. Esse trabalho tem como metodologia uma revisão bibliográfica e evidências documentais, este estudo oferece uma visão geral da história dos jogos de azar, desde suas origens até a recente regulamentação da indústria de jogos de azar no Brasil, com foco nos impactos sociais e econômicos dessa prática. O estudo explora o papel fundamental da educação financeira como ferramenta para aprimorar a cognição e o controle, auxiliando jovens a desenvolver habilidades de gestão financeira, identificar riscos e evitar comportamentos impulsivos. A análise indica que a expansão das apostas esportivas, impulsionada pela tecnologia e pela flexibilidade legal, apresenta novos desafios para a sociedade brasileira, especialmente para os jovens. Embora o setor tenha potencial econômico, os riscos sociais e psicológicos associados ao vício em jogos de azar exigem medidas preventivas e educacionais.

title: TRANSTORNO DE JOGO: RELATO DE CASO E REVISÃO DE ASPECTOS CLÍNICOS E PSICOSSOCIAIS
abstract: Introdução: Os jogos de azar são definidos como atividades que envolvem a aposta de um valor financeiro na tentativa de prever o resultado de um evento futuro, cujo desfecho é, em grande parte, independente das ações do apostador. Entre as formas mais populares dessa prática, destacam-se os jogos de cassino, loterias e jogos de azar na Internet, incluindo pôquer e apostas esportivas. O transtorno de jogo é o termo adotado pela quinta edição do Manual Diagnóstico e Estatístico de Transtornos Mentais (DSM-5) para descrever um padrão persistente e recorrente de comportamento de jogo associado a sofrimento significativo ou a prejuízo substancial em diversas esferas da vida. A prevalência é de 1% ao longo da vida, sendo o terceiro comportamento mais comum após tabaco e álcool. O tratamento é complexo, com ênfase em intervenções psicossociais. Objetivo: Relatar um caso de uma paciente encaminhada ao serviço de psiquiatria pela atenção primária de sua cidade de origem, devido ao comportamento disfuncional relacionado a jogos de apostas em diversas plataformas digitais e discutir as intervenções terapêuticas adotadas, considerando os principais aspectos clínicos, sociais e psicopatológicos associados à condição e discutindo as dificuldades enfrentadas no manejo multidisciplinar do transtorno de jogo. Metodologia: Trata-se de relato de caso clínico, complementado por revisão narrativa da literatura, a partir de análise retrospectiva do prontuário eletrônico de uma paciente atendida no Ambulatório de Psiquiatria do Hospital de Base da Faculdade de Medicina de São José do Rio Preto, vinculado ao Departamento de Ciências Neurológicas, Psiquiatria e Psicologia Médica da FAMERP. Resultados: Paciente do sexo feminino, 24 anos, com comportamento persistente e desadaptativo de apostas online, associado a prejuízos financeiros, sociais e emocionais significativos. O tratamento inicial incluiu psicofármacos (fluoxetina, naltrexona, valproato e risperidona), bloqueio das contas em plataformas digitais e encaminhamento para psicoterapia, resultando em melhora parcial. Entretanto, a paciente não teve acesso efetivo à psicoterapia ao longo do acompanhamento, o que contribuiu para a evolução com recaídas, abandono do acompanhamento e manutenção dos prejuízos funcionais. Conclusão: O manejo do transtorno de jogo requer uma abordagem multidisciplinar, combinando intervenções psicossociais, farmacológicas e suporte contínuo, com atenção às comorbidades psiquiátricas. A dificuldade de acesso a terapias especializadas, a alta taxa de recaídas e os impactos psicossociais do comportamento de jogo destacam a necessidade de políticas públicas mais eficazes, além de estratégias terapêuticas individualizadas para promover reabilitação integral e prevenir novos episódios.

title: What Bettors Don't Know About Their Own Betting: A Programme of Research Using Matched Behavioural and Self-Report Data to Examine the Limits of Informed Decision-Making in Online Sports Wagering
abstract: Informed decision-making is a foundational assumption of consumer protection frameworks for online gambling, yet the conditions required to support it are rarely examined empirically. This talk presents a programme of research investigating the cognitive, behavioural, and socioeconomic factors that systematically undermine awareness and decision-making in online sports wagering. Drawing on a series of studies that uniquely combine transaction-level behavioural account data with matched self-report measures, we examine how bettors estimate their own expenditure, respond to wins, losses, and liquidity shocks, and differ in self-control awareness across problem gambling severity levels and socioeconomic groups. Findings demonstrate systematic and predictable failures of financial self-awareness that are most pronounced among those at greatest risk of harm. We also present an evaluation of government-mandated strategies designed to enhance spending awareness, assessing their impact on both self-reported and objectively measured behaviour. Implications for the design of harm minimisation frameworks are discussed, with attention to the structural conditions under which informed decision-making can be meaningfully supported rather than assumed.
venue: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)

title: A Two-Stage Framework for Sports Betting Asset Construction: Probabilistic Prediction and Risk-Aware Portfolio Allocation
abstract: This manuscript presents a two-stage framework that treats sports betting markets as an alternative asset class, coupling probabilistic prediction with risk-aware portfolio allocation. The first stage produces calibrated probabilistic forecasts of match outcomes using heterogeneous learners trained on team-strength features, rolling form, and bookmaker odds. The second stage transforms these probabilities into a portfolio allocation problem under Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) constraints, comparing multiple staking strategies including flat staking, fractional Kelly, mean-variance, and risk parity. The framework is empirically evaluated on multi-league, multi-season European football data (2015–2025) covering the top five leagues, using a strict rolling-origin protocol that eliminates temporal leakage. Evaluation combines machine learning metrics (log-loss, Brier score, ranked probability score) with financial metrics (return on investment, Sharpe ratio, maximum drawdown, probability of ruin), providing a joint assessment absent from most prior work in this domain. This work operationalizes the theoretical foundations introduced in our companion preprint on integrated uncertainty-aware decision-making, and extends our previous work on sports betting as an alternative asset class (Galekwa et al., IEEE Access 2026). It contributes to the doctoral research program of the first author on robust decision-making under model uncertainty at the Institute of Smart Systems Technologies, University of Klagenfurt.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Machine Learning for Soccer Betting: A Scoping Review
abstract: Soccer betting is a high-uncertainty predictive market in which machine learning (ML) is increasingly used to estimate outcome probabilities, spot value bets, and stake sizes. However, the field remains fragmented: prediction, probability calibration, uncertainty quantification, and betting decisions are typically tackled in isolation, with little cross-pollination between the ML and decision-theoretic communities. Reported under the PRISMA extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR), we mapped the evidence of ML applied to soccer betting from January 2010 to March 2026. We searched the IEEE Xplore, Springer Link, ScienceDirect, MDPI, arXiv, and Google Scholar databases for relevant studies. Of the 612 records screened, 38 primary studies met the eligibility criteria, complemented by 29 foundational methodological and review works charted as background anchors (67 charted sources in total). All coverage statistics were computed for the 38 primary studies. Prediction dominates the literature on this topic. Explicit probability calibration appeared in only 21\% of primary studies, explicit uncertainty quantification in 29\%, and an explicit betting-decision rule in 55\%. Only a single peer-reviewed study couples calibration, uncertainty, and a decision rule in one pipeline, and even that study uses fixed-stake value betting rather than an uncertainty-modulated stake. Financial risk metrics (Sharpe, CVaR, drawdown, and probability of ruin) are severely under-reported relative to ROI. We synthesize this evidence into three outputs: (i)~a two-stage architecture (event prediction and staking decision) bridged by calibration and uncertainty quantification, which together supply the confidence signal the decision stage requires; (ii)~a cross-cutting map of datasets, features, and metrics; and (iii)~a structured catalog of eleven research gaps. This review makes a methodological case for integrated, uncertainty-aware ensemble frameworks and provides a reference point for future benchmarks in ML-driven sports predictive markets.
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: Neurocomputational Modeling of Cognitive Biases in Sports Betting: A Machine Learning Approach
abstract: In recent years, studies on sports betting have emphasized the use of statistical models and rational choice frameworks. They prioritize prediction accuracy and profitability while often neglecting cognitive biases. Few studies have integrated specific biases into the computational models. Furthermore, existing machine learning approaches mainly detect outcomes rather than model decision processes. This study proposes a neurocomputational framework. It combines cognitive bias theory and deep learning to predict bias-driven betting actions. We designed an LSTM with attention to the capture temporal dependencies. These dependencies are shaped by the hot-hand fallacy, loss chasing, and confirmation biases. The experimental results showed that the standard evaluation yielded an F1-score of 0.462. However, optimizing the decision threshold significantly improved the performance to an F1-score of 0.636 (AUC = 0.692). This highlights the sensitivity of the bias detection. The proposed model demonstrated superior ranking capabilities compared to the optimized baselines. Moreover, the attention weights provide interpretable insights into the distinct memory horizons of different biases. This framework offers a novel tool for forecasting biased-betting behavior. It has applications in responsible gambling analytics and risk predictions.

title: Risk Parity vs. Kelly Criterion: An Empirical Evaluation of Bankroll Allocation Strategies in Football Value Betting
Toward Sports Betting as a Financial Asset: An Investigative Analysis of Risk, Investment Potential, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Sports betting has grown into a large, data-intensive market; however, research on prediction and capital allocation remains fragmented. Most forecasting studies overlook leverage and path-dependent portfolio dynamics, whereas Kelly based frameworks assume frictionless markets and perfectly known probabilities. These gaps have contributed to the failure of several betting funds that developed accurate predictive models but lacked a robust risk-management discipline. To this end, we develop an integrated framework that embeds forecasting, stake sizing, and leverage control into a single portfolio management architecture. First, we model recursive leverage dynamics that generate superlinear growth under favorable outcomes and convex collapse during adverse sequences. Second, we introduce an uncertainty-adjusted Kelly criterion that uses the Kullback–Leibler divergence to penalize model misspecification and reduce stake sizes. Third, we embed them in a three-tier architecture: bet sizing, portfolio CVaR limits and leverage caps. Controlled simulations demonstrate that uncertainty-adjusted staking reduces the ruin probability from 78% to below 2% while preserving 85% of the growth potential, and that VaR-based leverage limits prevent extreme drawdowns (92% vs. 41%). The empirical validation of real-world data collected from the English Premier League confirms that uncertainty quantification improves risk-adjusted performance (Sharpe ratio gains of 30%) and enhances diversification benefits. All results can be reproduced by following the code available at https://github.com/Zabat/betting-risk-management.

title: Apuestas deportivas online: desplazamientos de sentidos de lo deportivo : ¿El deporte como inversión?
abstract: La presente investigación analiza cómo las plataformas de apuestas deportivas online legales en Argentina construyen nuevas significaciones en torno al deporte. El estudio se centra en seis plataformas de curso legal: Bet365, Betano, Bplay, Codere, Betsson y Betwarrior, con el objetivo de indagar de qué manera transforman el sentido del deporte —asociado al juego y al azar— en una retórica vinculada a la inversión, el cálculo y la rentabilidad. Desde una perspectiva comunicacional y cultural, se adoptó un enfoque cualitativo basado en el análisis interpretativo y multimodal del discurso. Se relevaron contenidos, estética visual, iconografía, narrativas, recursos multimediales y perfiles de usuario, junto con el análisis complementario de algunas piezas publicitarias. Los resultados evidencian un desplazamiento simbólico: el deporte es presentado como un fenómeno previsible y gestionable mediante datos y estadísticas, promoviendo una lógica de racionalización del azar que tensiona su dimensión lúdica e inscribe la práctica deportiva en dinámicas de mercantilización y financiarización.
venue: El Servicio de Difusión de la Creación Intelectual (National University of La Plata)

title: The Interpretive Limits of Expected Goals: Model Dependence, Realization Variability, and Decision-Making Under Uncertainty
abstract: Abstract Expected Goals (xG) models provide conditional probability estimates of scoring based on a finite modelled information set. Contemporary implementations can incorporate rich contextual, defensive, goalkeeper, sequential and tracking information; this is a genuine methodological advance, but it does not remove the conditionality of the resulting estimate with respect to the represented information, model specification and reference data. Their outputs are therefore probabilistic, model-dependent representations rather than deterministic statements about what an individual football event or match should produce. This distinction is relevant both to post-match statistical interpretation and to live betting, where a precise numerical display can become a decision cue. This paper combines a methodological framework with a preliminary retrospective screening of 154 xG-complete matches from the first four rounds of the 2026/27 Premier League, Serie A, La Liga and Bundesliga, yielding 308 team-match observations. Cumulative xG was mapped to integer goal regions separated by half-goal boundaries (0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5, ...). These cutpoints were selected because half-goal lines create unambiguous win/loss settlement boundaries in football goal markets, including team-total markets that correspond directly to the team-match unit analysed here. The transformation is analytical; it is neither a bookmaker pricing model nor a native output of the underlying xG models. Realized-goal divergence was defined as ΔG = Gactual − B(xG). Exact correspondence with the half-goal-threshold xG analytical band occurred in 35.7% of observations; 83.4% were within one goal and 16.6% were at least two goals away. Mean absolute band divergence was 0.834 goals, while signed mean divergence was only +0.055, showing that aggregate cancellation can coexist with substantial individual realization dispersion. A didactic Poisson reference with λ = xG produces an expected exact-band rate of approximately 34.2%. This reference is used only to show that a low exact-realization rate can arise naturally in a probabilistic count process; it is not a calibration test or generative model for the provider xG values. Sensitivity analyses excluding observations close to half-goal cutpoints produced materially similar results. A secondary two-sided threshold screen showed material variation by both line and side, with marked class imbalance at the higher thresholds. The second part proposes a stratified prospective experiment crossing three participant strata—football experts, regular bettors/football fans and novices—with three randomized information environments within each stratum: match visible without analytical statistics, match visible with statistics overlaid, and statistics-only from bookmaker/provider sources. Three distinct decision tasks are studied: final-match Over/Under 2.5 at 15 minutes, full-time 1X2 at half-time, and next-goal prediction at 60 minutes. A separate out-of-sample modelling benchmark estimates the incremental predictive contribution of xG to each target. The central claim is not that xG is inaccurate or simplistic, but that even a sophisticated xG estimate remains a conditional statistical representation rather than an observed realized outcome or a direct probability of a future betting target. The decision impact of statistical information must therefore be evaluated within the environment in which it is used.

title: Effects of Lottery Games on Students' University Education in Arusha Region, Tanzania
abstract: This study investigated the effects of lottery games on students' university education in Arusha region. Objectives were to: examine the extent to which lottery games affect university students’ education and find out possible measures to minimize the effects of lottery games on University Students' education. Entertainment Utility Theory and convergent mixed method design guided the study. The target population included 5 deans of students and 1002 students from 5 universities in Arusha region. The sample size of 205 comprised of 200 students and 5 deans of students. Questionnaires and interview guide were used to collect data. Simple random sampling was employed to sample students while the deans of students were selected purposively. Validity was established through expert review while reliability was determined using Cronbach’s Alpha and the coefficient value was r=0.67. While the trustworthiness of instrument for collecting qualitative data was done through peer debriefing. The data from quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics in SPSS version 23 and presented in tables. Qualitative data was presented in themes alongside research questions. The results show that participating in lottery games such as aviator, sports betting and casino games negatively affects students’ university education. In conclusion, students who are addicted to lottery games participation are likely to be distracted from their educational goals. The study recommends that self-awareness, provision of education on effects of lottery games, regulations and limits of purchasing lottery tickets by the gaming boards is useful to reduce the risks associated with lottery games.
venue: Journal of Research Innovation and Implications in Education

title: A responsabilidade civil dos influenciadores digitais na divulgação de jogos de azar e apostas online
abstract: O presente artigo analisa a responsabilidade civil dos influenciadores digitais na divulgação de jogos de azar e plataformas de apostas online no Brasil, especialmente diante da crescente expansão do marketing digital e da popularização das chamadas “bets”. Inicialmente, aborda-se a evolução dos influenciadores digitais como agentes de publicidade e sua relevância no ambiente virtual, bem como a regulamentação ética promovida pelo CONAR quanto à transparência das publicidades em redes sociais. Em seguida, examina-se o histórico dos jogos de azar no Brasil e o processo de regulamentação das apostas esportivas e plataformas digitais, com enfoque nas Leis nº 13.756/2018 e nº 14.790/2023. Por fim, discute-se a responsabilidade civil dos influenciadores digitais à luz do Código de Defesa do Consumidor, especialmente quanto à possibilidade de enquadramento desses agentes como fornecedores por equiparação, sujeitos à responsabilidade objetiva e solidária pelos danos causados aos consumidores. Ademais, ao final a pesquisa também analisa o entendimento dos tribunais brasileiros em casos envolvendo publicidade enganosa de jogos de azar, evidenciando a tendência jurisprudencial de responsabilização dos influenciadores quando sua atuação contribui para prejuízos suportados pelos consumidores. Dessa forma, o presente trabalho foi estruturado em cinco capítulos, com o objetivo de analisar a responsabilidade civil dos influenciadores digitais diante do contexto apresentado e adotou-se o método hipotético-dedutivo, com abordagem qualitativa, utilizando-se como procedimentos metodológicos a revisão bibliográfica de artigos científicos, obras doutrinárias, legislação aplicável e análise de entendimentos jurisprudenciais.

title: Non-Substance Addictive Behaviors Among People with Intellectual Disability: A Systematic Review
abstract: Abstract Non-substance addictive behaviors in individuals with intellectual disability (ID) constitute a relevant field of study, particularly given that this population has been historically underserved. This systematic review examined prevalence, risk and protective factors, and interventions related to non-substance addictive behaviors—specifically problematic gambling, gaming, use of internet, mobile phones, and pornography—among people with ID. A systematic search in Web of Science and PsycINFO found ten studies meeting the inclusion criteria (four case studies, three cross-sectional, two qualitative, and one longitudinal design). Five studies focused on gambling, two on mobile phone use, one on internet use, one on both internet and mobile phone use, and one addressed gaming, internet, and pornography. This systematic review highlights the limited evidence regarding different non-substance addictive behaviours among individuals with ID, identifies nuanced gaps and variability within the existing literature, and underscores the need for future research to strengthen and expand current knowledge.
venue: International Journal of Mental Health and Addiction

title: Identifying the Socio-Emotional and Mental Health Correlates of Online Sports Betting Among Late Adolescent Boys.
abstract: ABSTRACT Introduction Online sports betting is emerging as a novel form of gambling, particularly popular among late adolescent boys, ages 18–25. While the socioemotional determinants of traditional forms of gambling are generally understood, less is known about how these correlate with online sports betting behavior and whether online sports betting recency relate to mental health outcomes. Methods Online questionnaires were used to assess late adolescent boys' social lives, emotional functioning, mental health, and online sports betting behavior. Results Path analysis reveal that college enrollment, participation in social gaming, and higher life satisfaction were related to more recent online sports betting. Online sports betting recency was not related but depression or anxiety symptoms. Conclusions With nearly half (47%) having participated, online sports betting was highly prevalent. Several key social and emotion factors are related to online sports betting recency among late adolescent boys. Contrary to expectations, there were no links with depression or anxiety.
