title: APOSTAS ESPORTIVAS ONLINE E SAÚDE MENTAL EM JOVENS ADULTOS: UMA REVISÃO INTEGRATIVA DA LITERATURA
abstract: As apostas esportivas online expandem-se com a digitalização, a disponibilidade contínua das plataformas e sua crescente integração às práticas esportivas, suscitando preocupações acerca da saúde mental de jovens adultos. Este estudo analisa as evidências científicas sobre as relações entre apostas esportivas online, comportamento problemático e indicadores de saúde mental nessa população. Realizou-se uma revisão integrativa da literatura, de natureza bibliográfica e com síntese predominantemente qualitativa, mediante buscas nas bases SciELO, Scopus e Web of Science, considerando publicações de 2022 a 2026. Após a triagem, a retirada das duplicidades, a aplicação dos critérios de elegibilidade e a leitura integral, 12 artigos compuseram o corpus. Os dados foram submetidos à análise descritiva e comparativa e organizados em eixos temáticos. Os resultados indicam que a maior gravidade do comportamento problemático se associa de maneira mais consistente a sintomas de ansiedade, depressão, estresse e sofrimento psicológico. A participação ou a frequência das apostas, quando avaliadas sem medidas específicas de gravidade, não apresenta associação uniforme com esses desfechos. Fatores individuais, sociais, comerciais e tecnológicos também se relacionam a padrões de maior risco. As evidências não permitem estabelecer causalidade nem determinar a direção temporal dessas relações, permanecendo necessária a realização de estudos longitudinais direcionados aos jovens adultos e ao contexto brasileiro.

title: Stay updated on changes in sports‐betting restrictions for student‐athletes, staff, coaches
abstract: The sports‐betting world underwent significant transformation just over seven years ago when the U.S. Supreme Court decided ( Murphy v. NCAA , 584 U.S. 453 (2018)) to strike down as unconstitutional the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act of 1992. A total of 39 states, in addition to Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico, now allow some form of legalized online or in‐person sports betting, with Missouri becoming the most recent as of Dec. 1, 2025 ( see www.legalsportsreport.com/sports-betting-states/ ). In states with legalized betting, anyone meeting the age requirement (21 in most of the states) can place bets on professional and college games with the caveat that there are restrictions regarding sharing insider information or betting on games within the conference that a student‐athlete's school participates. In addition, many state laws include language that restricts bets on game outcomes, bets on in‐state teams, and proposition bets (frequently referred to as “prop bets,” which are bets placed on specific events or individual performances within a game that aren’t directly tied to the final score or outcome of who wins or loses).

title: The Art of Winning an Unfair Game: Modelling Strategies in the NHL Betting Market using Machine Learning
abstract: This thesis develops and evaluates a profit-oriented machine-learning modelfor betting on regular-season National Hockey League (NHL) games, with thegoal of overcoming the bookmaker margin and achieving a positive return oninvestment (ROI). Game statistics from Natural Stat Trick are combined with moneyline odds fromThe Odds API and converted to decimal odds. Rolling "form windows" producehome-minus-away feature vectors, which feed logistic-regression, XGBoost, andsupport-vector-classifier models combined into a Sharpe-weighted ensemble.Value bets are identified and staked using two schemes (Flat and To-Win),evaluated over a holdout period (season 2024/25 and the ongoing 2025/26)across 15 random-seed Monte-Carlo runs. The model is benchmarked against three reference strategies (favorite,team-loyalty, and random betting) and against the S&P 500 and SMI indices.Financial risk metrics (ROI, maximum drawdown, Sharpe, Calmar, andrisk-reward ratio) are reported throughout. Under To-Win staking the modelreaches a modestly positive ROI (+1.47% and +1.51% in the two holdoutperiods), while a critical discussion addresses statistical significance,sample size, and the practical limits of the approach. This is the English translation of a German-language Maturaarbeit(Swiss upper-secondary thesis). The translation was produced with AIassistance; the German original is authoritative.

title: Darf die Polizei den Sportwetten-Sheriff vom Stadion fernhalten?
Why Courts and Congress Should but Won’t Outlaw Prediction Markets
abstract: The current confusion over prediction markets, mainly trading in futures on sports events, starts with society’s historic antipathy toward gambling. State legislatures passed statutes outlawing everything that looked like gambling. Following the Industrial Revolution this created conflicts with certain commercial activities, which actually served valuable public purposes. Among these were insurance, auctions and trading in securities and commodities. Courts struggled with these state restrictions until the Depression forced Congress to act. Beginning in 1933, federal statutes expressly exempted trades on nationally regulated markets from state anti-gambling laws. However, the items must meet specified criteria. Courts are now faced with the question of whether prediction markets meet those criteria. Even who should decide – courts or federal regulatory agencies – is in dispute. Courts should rule them illegal not only because they are, but also to protect states like Utah from being forced to have sports betting and states like Nevada being forced to have unregulated sports betting. But the wild card is the Trump tie-in, including naming Kalshi insiders as federal regulators. Not until Trump is gone will the right of states to make their own decisions about gambling once again prevail.
venue: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)

title: Changes in gambling behaviors among young adults in Rhode Island, 2022-2024.
abstract: Background The rapid expansion of legalized sports betting and mobile gambling in the U.S. has transformed how gambling is accessed and experienced. Young adults are particularly vulnerable to these changes; however, limited research has examined how gambling behaviors are shifting across multiple modalities during periods of expanding gambling availability. Methods We analyzed repeated cross-sectional data from the Rhode Island Young Adult Survey (RIYAS) collected in 2022 (n = 1,022) and 2024 (n = 1,008) among individuals aged 18-25 years. Outcomes included past-year participation in specific gambling behaviors, positive BBGS (Brief Biosocial Gambling Screen) screens, and overall gambling involvement measured as the number of gambling types endorsed. Multivariable logistic regression models estimated adjusted odds ratios for differences in individual gambling behaviors between survey waves, and Poisson/zero-inflated Poisson models estimated differences in gambling involvement. Results Gambling participation did not differ significantly between 2022 and 2024. However, among individuals reporting gambling, participation increased in several activities, including lottery tickets (AOR = 1.36, 95 % CI: 1.01-1.83), raffle gambling (AOR = 1.40, 95 % CI: 1.05-1.88), sports betting (AOR = 1.65, 95 % CI: 1.07-2.56), casino slot machines (AOR = 2.99, 95 % CI: 2.10-4.27), other slot machines (AOR = 2.30, 95 % CI: 1.23-4.33), and app-based gambling (AOR = 2.14, 95 % CI: 1.38-3.32). The number of gambling types endorsed increased (IRR = 1.28, 95 % CI: 1.16-1.41). Positive BBGS screens were more common in 2024 but not statistically significant after adjustment. Conclusions Findings suggest while overall gambling participation remained stable, engagement across multiple and mobile-based gambling activities increased between survey waves, potentially signaling emerging risk. Increasing diversification and digitalization of gambling behaviors requires continued surveillance and public health strategies addressing emerging gambling environments.

title: ESTRATEGIAS DE MARKETING EN LAS APUESTAS DEPORTIVAS: ANÁLISIS DE SU INFLUENCIA EN EL COMPORTAMIENTO Y FIDELIZACIÓN DE LOS JÓVENES
abstract: Trabajo Fin de Grado leído en la Universidad Rey Juan Carlos en el curso académico 2025/2026. Directores/as: Jesús Anguita Grajales

title: Giocare per il denaro o giocare con il denaro? Una rassegna della letteratura economica sul valore edonistico delle scommesse sportive.
abstract: La rassegna della letteratura economica suggerisce una duplice definizione delle scommesse sportive: attività finanziaria e/o bene di consumo. Infatti, l’ipotesi che l’obiettivo delle scommesse sportive sia unicamente il profitto contrasta con l’osservazione che il loro rendimento atteso è negativo. La partecipazione a lotterie da parte di agenti razionali è giustificabile allentando (almeno localmente) l’ipotesi di una loro avversione al rischio. Questa propensione al rischio può derivare dall’attribuire al gioco d’azzardo non solo una finalità finanziaria, ma anche un valore edonistico. L’ipotesi che scommettere sia divertente è sostenuta da varie osservazioni e studi empirici. In particolare, la domanda di scommesse sportive pare dipendere dalle stesse variabili che determinano la domanda di intrattenimento sportivo, suggerendo l’ipotesi di una complementarità tra scommesse e visione (dal vivo o televisiva) delle competizioni sportive. Sport bets are “state contingent assets”, with a negative expected return. Therefore, a rational agent who buys these lotteries behaves as a risk-lover. The rationality of bettors may be supported by the evidence on the informational efficiency of the sport betting market. While, theoretically, their (local) risk-loving behavior may be explained by adding a (small) utility of gambling in a bettors’ generally concave (risk-averse) utility function. If gambling is amusing, then the gamblers are consumers rather than investors, and the money that they spend on gambling should not be considered as a financial loss, but as the price paid for the pleasure of gambling. Actually, the empirical evidence suggests that the demand for sports entertainment includes sports betting. In particular, betting and watching a game appear to be strong complements, as if betting on the game watched on a media would make attending the game more exciting.
venue: IRIS Research product catalog (Sapienza University of Rome)

title: Inteligencia sensible y apuestas deportivas: una lectura pedagógica sobre adolescentes y cultura digital
abstract: Este ensayo conceptual analiza cómo las apuestas deportivas online configuran sensibilidades adolescentes y que implicancias pedagógicas se derivan para la educación del cuerpo y el ámbito escolar. A partir de una revisión crítica de literatura nacional e internacional (2010-2024) y del diálogo con las nociones de habitus emocional, reparto de lo sensible e inteligencia motriz, se propone la categoría inteligencia sensible para pensar como la percepción, emoción y acción se relacionan en prácticas de apuesta. El artículo discute la estetización del riesgo, la naturalización de la apuesta en contextos escolares y plantea propuestas pedagógicas orientadas a la alfabetización digital crítica y la educación emocional y corporal. Concluye que exceder el marco psicopatologizante abre posibilidades de intervención educativa que reconozcan aprendizajes y regulan riesgos.
venue: Revista Tempos e Espaços em Educação

title: Criminal Responsibility in Individuals with Gambling Disorder in Brazil
THE MOST IMPORTANT LEGAL BATTLE IN THE HISTORY of GAMBLING
abstract: Prediction markets have quickly become the biggest legal issue in the gambling world since Murphy versus NCAA, the multi-year case that eventually resulted in the repeal of the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act (PASPA), paving the way for legalized sports betting and unbeknownst at the time, the rise of sports contracts on prediction markets. As of April 4, 2026, there are 10 active prediction market bills, and Kalshi alone is involved in 13 legal battles with various states.

title: Diseño y análisis psicométrico de un instrumento para determinar apuestas deportivas en universitarios
abstract: El presente proyecto de investigación tuvo como propósito diseñar y analizar psicométricamente un instrumento para determinar las influencias que presentan las apuestas deportivas en estudiantes universitarios. La investigación se realizó ante el crecimiento de las plataformas digitales de apuestas deportivas y la necesidad de contar con herramientas que permitan identificar y caracterizar su presencia e influencia en la población universitaria. El estudio se elaboró con un enfoque exploratorio, mediante un muestreo no probabilístico de participación voluntaria, con una muestra de 40 estudiantes de la Facultad de Ciencias de la Salud de la Universidad de Ciencias Aplicadas y Ambientales (U.D.C.A.), pertenecientes a los programas de Ciencias del Deporte y Medicina Humana. Para la recolección de información se diseñó un instrumento metodológico tipo cuestionario, organizado en diferentes secciones relacionadas con las características sociodemográficas, el conocimiento y exposición a las plataformas de apuestas deportivas, la participación en estas actividades, las motivaciones y el gasto asociado, así como el impacto y la percepción de sus posibles efectos en la vida cotidiana de los estudiantes. El proceso de validación del instrumento se realizó mediante el Coeficiente de Validez de Contenido (CVC), considerando la valoración de los criterios en términos de suficiencia, claridad, relevancia y coherencia. Como resultado, se obtuvo un CVC global de 0,85, lo que corresponde a una buena validez y concordancia del instrumento. Los resultados permitieron identificar la participación de los estudiantes en diferentes plataformas de apuestas deportivas, destacándose BetPlay como una de las plataformas con mayor utilización. Asimismo, se evidenciaron diferentes motivaciones, niveles de participación y percepciones relacionadas con esta actividad. Entre los aspectos evaluados, la situación económica presentó el mayor porcentaje de impacto positivo percibido por los participantes. En conclusión, el instrumento diseñado presentó propiedades de validez de contenido favorables, por lo que constituye una herramienta pertinente para la identificación y caracterización de las influencias asociadas a las apuestas deportivas en estudiantes universitarios y puede servir como base para futuras investigaciones en esta población.
venue: Repositorio - Universidad de Ciencias Aplicadas y Ambientales UDCA.

title: Data-Driven Decision-Making in Fantasy Premier League : Correlations, predictions and optimization strategies
abstract: The increased amount of available information has, over the past decades, spread through every industry, and the world of sports has been no exception. Today, various statistics are available almost in real time and for nearly every event. This is naturally also the case with the world’s most popular football league, the English Premier League. This available information is utilized not only within teams themselves, but also widely for other purposes such as betting and fantasy games. Fantasy Premier League (FPL), which focuses on the English Premier League, and the statistics related to it, are at the center of this thesis. FPL provides an ideal environment for applying the principles of data-driven management within the constraints of limited resources. The research question of this thesis is: How can data-driven decision-making enhance performance in Fantasy Premier League (FPL) through correlation analysis, predictive modeling, and optimization strategies? The theoretical section of the thesis focuses on explaining the principles of data-driven management, predictive analytics, and optimization, particularly from the perspective of fantasy sports games. The methodology section describes the data analysis techniques used, presents the underlying mathematical formulas, and explains how the data was collected. The data used in this thesis is numerical, and the research method is quantitative. The empirical section of the thesis consists of a test created using the Python programming language. The first objective was to identify the factors that correlate most strongly with FPL points and recorded match events. After this, the mean absolute error and the root mean squared error were determined to evaluate the effectiveness of the predictive regression models. Finally, a simulation utilizing optimization was carried out, in which the created optimization model selected an FPL team and competed against a team representing a human minded, heuristic model. The results of the thesis indicate that data-driven management can also be applied in the world of fantasy sports. The created model did not outperform the human-like team in every individual round, but overall, it accumulated more points. In addition, it utilized the available budget considerably more efficiently. It should be remembered that FPL is a complex game, and this thesis alone cannot account for all variables, meaning that some simplifications had to be made. The observation period was also too short to draw broader conclusions. Nevertheless, it can be concluded that data-driven management and various forms of data analytics have become a permanent part of the lives of FPL managers going forward.

title: A Study on Gambling Effect on Youths and Their Lifestyle In Tumkuru District
abstract: Abstract The rapid growth of online and offline gambling activities has become a major social concern among young people in recent years. This study focuses on analyzing the effects of gambling on the lifestyle, behavior, financial condition, and social relationships of youths in Tumakuru. The research aims to understand the reasons behind the increasing involvement of youths in gambling activities and to examine how such habits influence their daily lives and future well-being. The study is based on both primary and secondary data. Primary data were collected through questionnaires and direct interaction with selected respondents from different areas of Tumakuru. Secondary information was gathered from journals, articles, reports, and online sources related to gambling behavior among youths. The findings indicate that factors such as peer influence, easy access to online betting platforms, stress, unemployment, and the desire for quick money are major reasons for youth participation in gambling activities. The research further reveals that excessive gambling negatively affects academic performance, mental health, family relationships, financial stability, and social behavior. Many respondents reported experiencing anxiety, loss of concentration, debt, and reduced productivity due to gambling habits. The study also highlights that continuous exposure to gambling can lead to addiction and unhealthy lifestyle patterns among youths. The paper concludes that awareness programs, parental guidance, educational support, and stricter regulation of gambling platforms are necessary to reduce the harmful effects of gambling on young individuals. Creating employment opportunities and promoting healthy recreational activities can also help youths avoid gambling-related risks and develop a more balanced lifestyle .
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

title: IPL Analysis Using Machine Learning
abstract: The Indian Premier League (IPL), as one of the most popular Twenty-20 cricket leagues worldwide, generates vast amounts of data related to matches, players, teams, and playing conditions, making it an ideal domain for machine learning– based analysis. This paper presents a comprehensive study on the application of machine learning techniques for analyzing IPL data with the objectives of predicting match outcomes, evaluating player performance, and supporting strategic decision-making. Using historical IPL datasets comprising match details, player statistics, team compositions, pitch conditions, and weather factors, the data is preprocessed and transformed through feature engineering to enhance predictive capability. Various supervised machine learning algorithms, including regression, classification, ensemble, and deep learning models, are employed to forecast match results and performance metrics. The study builds upon existing research that demonstrates the effectiveness of models such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machines, and deep learning architectures in sports analytics. The results highlight the potential of machine learning to uncover meaningful patterns, improve prediction accuracy, and provide actionable insights for stakeholders such as team management, analysts, fantasy sports users, and broadcasters. Overall, the proposed approach emphasizes the growing role of data-driven methods in modern cricket analytics and their contribution to enhancing competitiveness, audience engagement, and informed decision-making in the IPL ecosystem.
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology

title: Sports betting as a social phenomenon: Public attitudes and motivation for participation
abstract: This article examines bookmaking and sports betting as a social phenomenon emerging at the intersection of economic, cultural, and institutional processes. It analyzes the contradictory nature of public attitudes toward bookmaking. The theoretical basis of the study is formed by classical and modern sociological approaches to the analysis of gambling, deviant behavior, social inequality, and the rationalization of economic practices. The main focus is on the motivation for participation in sports betting, the role of the social environment, media, and digital communications in the process of involvement. Financial and non-financial incentives for participation, emotional involvement, as well as the characteristics of trust in advertising and informal sources of information are considered. The study is based on data from a sociological survey conducted in Tyumen and examines the relationships between the social context of involvement, motivation for participation, and subjective assessment of the consequences of betting. The range of social and economic consequences of participation in bookmaking practices, as well as strategies for limiting or terminating participation, are analyzed. In conclusion, the place of bookmaking in the structure of modern leisure and economic practices, its role in the reproduction of social differences and the formation of ambivalent public attitudes towards gambling are determined.
venue: Вестник Тюменского государственного университета. Социально-экономические и правовые исследования

title: Kanavointiparadoksi: panosrajoittaminen, verotus ja kokeneiden vedonlyöjien poissulkeminen Suomen 2027 rahapeliuudistuksessa
abstract: This study examines whether a 90% channelisation target is achievable for the sports bettor segment under Finland’s 2027 gambling reform and investigates the structural mechanisms that may prevent this outcome. The Finnish Gambling Act of 2026 dismantles Veikkaus's decades-long monopoly in favour of a multioperator licensing model. While the reform aims to channel players away from unlicensed offshore operators, this study argues that it creates a Channelisation Paradox for high-turnover sophisticated bettors: the licensed market is commercially inaccessible due to systematic stake limiting by recreational operators, while the unlicensed market is financially unfeasible because positive wager-level gains from unlicensed sports betting may be taxable as earned income, while losses from losing wagers cannot be offset against them. The severity of this non-deductibility principle is illustrated by the Supreme Administrative Court ruling KHO 28.5.2025/1225. The study employs a pragmatist research philosophy using heuristic inquiry and autoethnography as its primary methodology. The empirical dataset comprises a systematically maintained personal betting log covering 23 months of sports betting activity from June 2024 to April 2026, encompassing 10,194 bets, €899,916 in total turnover, and a net return on investment of 2.38% across 33 operators. Seven documented limit events, instances of operator-imposed stake restriction, provide primary empirical evidence of systematic sophisticated bettor exclusion from the regulated market, including one case of restriction propagating automatically across operator brands within the same corporate group. The comparative policy analysis draws on Swedish channelisation data, the KHO ruling, and the Finnish Gambling Act of 2026. The findings demonstrate that operator-imposed stake limiting is driven by predicted future edge rather than realised profitability, as evidenced by one restriction applied at a negative return on investment. The study concludes that the 22% GGR tax rate structurally disadvantages sharp-friendly operator models, that recreational operator dominance of the licensed pool produces systematic exclusion of sophisticated bettors, and that the resulting Asymmetric Tax Trap renders both licensed and unlicensed markets non-viable for this segment. The Swedish precedent, where an identical tax rate has produced five consecutive years of missed channelisation targets, supports the thesis that the Finnish 90% target is structurally incompatible with the current framework for sports bettors.

title: Anatomy of Corruption: Biography of One Hundred Corrupt Politicians of India
abstract: This book is a monumental scholarly investigation into the anatomy of political corruption in India. It is not a simple collection of scandalous stories or a partisan polemic. Instead it is a rigorous multidisciplinary analysis that examines the careers of one hundred politicians who held or sought public office in India and whose conduct was defined by serious corruption allegations, criminal charges, judicial condemnation, or credible documentation by independent sources. The work applies the full intellectual arsenal of criminology, criminal profiling, jurisprudence, political philosophy, and legislative inquiry to understand not only what happened but why it happened, how it was allowed to happen, and what systemic conditions made it possible. The book is organized into fifteen parts, each building on the theoretical and empirical foundations of the previous ones. Part One establishes the foundational architecture. It defines political corruption as the abuse of entrusted power for private gain and traces the historical trajectory from the colonial inheritance through the Nehruvian era, the Indira Gandhi period, the Rajiv Gandhi years, the economic liberalization of 1991, and up to the present. It explains how corruption evolved from the license raj rent seeking to the post liberalization regulatory capture that produced the 2G Spectrum scandal and the Coal Block Allocation scandal. The theoretical frameworks introduced include Merton's strain theory, Sutherland's differential association, rational choice theory, Sykes and Matza's techniques of neutralization, white collar crime theory, institutional corruption theory, and criminal profiling methodologies from the FBI and David Canter. The first part also presents the first seven profiles including Lalu Prasad Yadav and the Fodder Scam, A Raja and the 2G case, Suresh Kalmadi and the Commonwealth Games scandal, J Jayalalithaa and the disproportionate assets case, P Chidambaram and the INX Media case, Arvind Kejriwal and the Delhi Liquor Policy case, and Sukh Ram and the telecom scandal. Each profile is analyzed for criminological type, neutralization techniques used, institutional conditions that enabled the conduct, and legal outcomes. Part Two examines ideological corruption. It asks how political ideologies interact with corrupt practices. The book argues that strong ideological commitment can become a mechanism of moral disengagement, where politicians justify bending rules in service of a higher political project. The profiles in this part include B S Yediyurappa and the Karnataka mining scandal, Bangaru Laxman who was caught on camera accepting a bribe as BJP president, Madhu Koda the Jharkhand chief minister who laundered mining proceeds offshore, Dilip Singh Judeo and the cash for votes controversy, P V Narasimha Rao and the JMM bribery case, Chhagan Bhujbal and the Maharashtra money trail, Ajit Pawar and the irrigation scam, Mulayam Singh Yadav and disproportionate assets, Mayawati and the BSP political economy, and several Trinamool Congress leaders from the Narada sting operation. The part also analyzes the Coal Block Allocation scandal in depth and the defense sector corruption continuum from Bofors to Rafale. Part Three descends into the specific domain of land and mining corruption. It introduces the concept of extraction corruption, which combines financial harm with territorial dispossession and ecological degradation. The part examines the constitutional framework of the Fifth Schedule, the Forest Rights Act, and the Panchayats Extension to Scheduled Areas Act, showing how these protections have been systematically bypassed. Profiles include Hemant Soren who was arrested by the ED and then reelected as chief minister, Shibu Soren and the JMM bribery case, Ashok Chavan and the Adarsh Housing Society scam, Virbhadra Singh and the Himachal disproportionate assets case, D K Shivakumar and the cash haul controversy, Azam Khan and land grabbing in Rampur, and the criminal politicians Mukhtar Ansari and Atique Ahmed who were both killed while in custody. The part also analyzes the Muzaffarnagar riots and the political economy of communal violence. Part Four is titled Meta Corruption: the subversion of justice itself. This part argues that the most dangerous form of corruption is the corruption of the systems designed to detect and punish first order corruption. It examines investigative agency capture, prosecutorial manipulation, judicial pressure, witness management, legal process weaponization, and constitutional engineering of impunity. The profiles include P Chidambaram again but focused on his arrest and the PMLA proceedings, D K Shivakumar again for the ED investigation, Arvind Kejriwal and Manish Sisodia for the Delhi Liquor Policy case and their prolonged pre trial detention, Bhupesh Baghel and the Mahadev online betting app case, and the post mortem analysis of Mulayam Singh Yadav. The part also provides a comprehensive analysis of the Sita Soren judgment of 2024 which overruled the 1998 Narasimha Rao immunity for bribery of legislators, and the Electoral Bonds judgment of 2024 which struck down the opaque political financing scheme. Part Five examines electoral corruption. It presents the theory of electoral integrity and the democratic paradox where candidates with criminal records have a higher win rate than clean candidates. It analyzes vote buying, booth capturing, electoral violence, manipulation of electoral rolls, and the use of state resources for incumbent advantage. The quantitative data from the Association for Democratic Reforms shows that in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, candidates with declared criminal cases had a success rate of 15.3 percent compared to only 4.4 percent for clean candidates. The part profiles the bahubali politicians of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar including Mukhtar Ansari, Atiq Ahmed, Pappu Yadav, D P Yadav, Azam Khan, and Prabhunath Singh. It also examines the Election Commission of India, the Model Code of Conduct, and the Supreme Court's jurisprudence on disqualification under Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act. Comparative international analysis includes the Philippines, Mexico, and Italy. Part Six analyzes the corporate political nexus in post liberalization India. It develops the frameworks of regulatory capture, crony capitalism, state capture, and structural corruption. The part examines the 2G Spectrum case in even greater detail, the Coalgate scandal, the Commonwealth Games procurement corruption, the Electoral Bonds data analysis, and the defense procurement scandals including Bofors and Rafale. Profiles include Manmohan Singh and the question of systemic responsibility for Coalgate, Naveen Patnaik and the Odisha mining economy, Y S Jagan Mohan Reddy and the disproportionate assets case, N Chandrababu Naidu and the skill development scam, Sharad Pawar and the architecture of long term political capital, and Jayant Sinha and the Jharkhand bail controversy. The part also examines the INX Media case, the Aircel Maxis case, and the role of corporate lobbying in shaping regulatory outcomes. Part Seven confronts the most morally urgent dimension: communal violence and state crime. It develops the theory of state facilitated communal violence using the frameworks of Penny Green and Tony Ward on state crime, Paul Brass on the institutionalized riot system, and Ashutosh Varshney on civic engagement. The part examines the major episodes of communal violence in independent India: the 1984 anti Sikh violence, the 1992 93 Mumbai riots following the Babri Masjid demolition, and the 2002 Gujarat violence. The profiles include Narendra Modi and the SIT closure report on Gujarat 2002, Amit Shah and the Sohrabuddin fake encounter case, L K Advani and the Babri Masjid demolition conspiracy case, Jagdish Tytler and Sajjan Kumar for the 1984 violence, Kalyan Singh for contempt of the Supreme Court in the Babri Masjid case, Maya Kodnani who was convicted then acquitted for the Naroda Patiya massacre, and Bal Thackeray for the organized intimidation culture of the Shiv Sena. The part also examines the Srikrishna Commission report and the failure to implement its recommendations. Part Eight examines the corruption of information itself. It analyzes media capture, paid news, IT cells, troll armies, legal coercion against journalists, and the weaponization of defamation and sedition laws. The theoretical framework draws on Habermas's public sphere, Herman and Chomsky's propaganda model, and the concept of manufactured uncertainty. Profiles include Subramanian Swamy as a political litigant using lawfare, Arnab Goswami and Republic TV for hyper partisan television journalism, Kapil Sibal for internet censorship controversies, Prannoy Roy and Radhika Roy for the hostile takeover of NDTV by the Adani Group, Prabir Purkayastha for the NewsClick case under UAPA, Ravish Kumar as a counter institutional figure, Devendra Fadnavis for election affidavit disclosure issues, Rahul Gandhi for defamation conviction and disqualification, Sudhir Chaudhary for the Doordarshan appointment controversy, and the figures from the Radia tapes revealing the corporate political media triangle. The part also examines the Pegasus spyware scandal and its implications for journalist source protection. Part Nine examines the post liberalization crony capitalism system. It analyzes the mechanisms of spectrum corruption, procurement corruption, regulatory forbearance, regulatory design corruption, post hoc regularization, and evergreening of bank loans. The profiles include Suresh Kalmadi for the Commonwealth Games, A Raja for the 2G acquittal, Vijay Mallya as the fugitive economic offender, Nirav Modi and Mehul Choksi for the Punjab National Bank fraud, Yediyurappa for the Karnataka mining scandal, Madhu Koda for Jharkhand corruption, P K Bansal for railway bribery through his nephew, Robert Vadra for land deals as proximity corru

title: Mediterranean Diet Adherence and Screening Indicators of Gambling-Related Problems in a Sample of Young Adults: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Analysis of the EVA-Adic Study
abstract: Background/Objectives: Gambling disorder is recognized as a behavioral addiction, and gambling-related problems represent an important public health concern among young adults. However, evidence regarding their association with overall diet quality, particularly adherence to the Mediterranean diet (MedDiet), remains scarce. This exploratory secondary analysis examined whether screening indicators of gambling-related problems were associated with MedDiet adherence in young adults. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 496 participants aged 18–34 years from the EVA-Adic study. MedDiet adherence was assessed using the 14-item Mediterranean Diet Adherence Screener (MEDAS-14). Gambling-related indicators were assessed using the Short Pathological Gambling Questionnaire (CBJP), the Lie/Bet Questionnaire, and their six individual items. Independent multiple linear regression models were fitted for each indicator. The fully adjusted Model 2 included age, sex, alcohol consumption, sleep quality, sitting time, marital status, and educational level. Given the secondary nature of the analysis, the absence of an a priori sample-size calculation for the present research question, and the limited number of participants with positive gambling-related indicators, the analyses were considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. Results: The mean age was 26.60 ± 4.41 years; 276 participants (55.6%) were women, and 157 (31.7%) had high MedDiet adherence. In the fully adjusted Model 2, feeling guilty about gambling (Q2) was nominally associated with a lower MEDAS-14 score (B = −1.10; 95% CI, −1.97 to −0.22; p = 0.015). However, this association did not remain statistically significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction (q = 0.116), and none of the eight primary Model 2 associations met the FDR-adjusted significance threshold. Conclusions: Several gambling-related screening indicators showed nominal inverse associations with MedDiet adherence, with gambling-related guilt showing the most consistent estimate across sensitivity analyses. However, no association remained statistically significant in the fully adjusted model after correction for multiple testing, and formal interaction analyses provided no robust evidence of effect modification by sex. Given the small number of positive screens and the cross-sectional design, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

title: A psicologia do vício em apostas virtuais: uma perspectiva integrativa e existencial do fenômeno
abstract: Os jogos de sorte e o ato de apostar acompanham a trajetória cultural da humanidade, atravessando diferentes épocas e adquirindo características específicas em cada cultura. No Brasil, estima-se que a cultura das apostas tenha se consolidado a partir do século XVI, com a chegada dos jogos de cartas, expandindo-se posteriormente com o “jogo do bicho”, em 1892, e com a criação da Loteria Federal, em 1917. Mesmo após a proibição oficial dos cassinos em 1946, as apostas esportivas mantêm sua presença na sociedade brasileira. No século XXI, com o avanço do mercado de consumo capitalista e a expansão dos meios digitais, as apostas virtuais tornam-se amplamente acessíveis, favorecendo a exploração da realidade socioeconômica do país por meio de estratégias de marketing, publicidade massiva e influenciadores digitais. Nesse contexto, emergem problemas econômicos, psicossociais e comportamentais que se intensificam através de mecanismos de perpetuação do comportamento aditivo, como recompensas dopaminérgicas, estímulos sensoriais e esquemas de reforço variável. A manutenção do ciclo compulsivo, análoga aos danos multifatoriais observados no vício em apostas, evidencia também questões existenciais, como o vazio existencial e sua relação direta com comportamentos de fuga, autoentorpecimento e frustração de sentido. O presente trabalho realiza uma revisão narrativa da literatura, de caráter qualitativo, visando integrar as dimensões histórica, socioeconômica, comportamental e existencial do fenômeno, traçando um nexo causal entre o comportamento aditivo, os impactos psicossociais das casas de apostas virtuais e a dinâmica do vazio existencial à luz da Logoterapia e da análise existencial.

title: PERSUASÃO DIGITAL E APOSTA ONLINE: UM EXPERIMENTO DE CAMPO SOBRE APELOS CENTRAIS E PERIFÉRICOS EM ANÚNCIOS DE APOSTAS ESPORTIVAS

title: Winning the Wager: Lessons from U.S. Sports Betting Markets for the Economic Design of Legislation in Texas
abstract: Texas remains one of the few holdout states since Murphy v. NCAA (2018) opened the door to legalized sports betting across the country. Rather than asking whether Texas should legalize, this thesis asks how: specifically, how should the state design the economic framework for a legalized market? Through a comparative case study of six U.S. sports betting jurisdictions, it analyzes tax base design and market structure to recommend a gross gaming revenue-based, competitive multi-operator model suited to Texas's fiscal infrastructure and constitutional constraints. These findings are made more urgent by the state's existing "grey market," which already delivers functional sports betting to Texans outside any regulatory or fiscal framework, exposing the state to consumer harms without the corresponding revenue benefits. The central argument is that the form of legalization is more consequential than the fact of it: for Texas, economic design carries both fiscal and meaningful social stakes.
venue: The University of Texas at Austin

title: A RESPONSABILIDADE CIVIL DOS INFLUENCIADORES DIGITAIS NA PUBLICIDADE DE APOSTAS ESPORTIVAS À LUZ DO DIREITO DO CONSUMIDOR
abstract: O presente artigo analisa a responsabilidade civil dos influenciadores digitais na publicidade de apostas esportivas, especialmente diante da expansão das plataformas conhecidas como bets e da crescente influência desses agentes sobre as decisões de consumo. O problema de pesquisa consiste em verificar em que medida os influenciadores podem ser responsabilizados civilmente quando divulgam apostas esportivas de forma inadequada, sobretudo nos casos de publicidade enganosa, omissão de riscos ou ausência de identificação clara do conteúdo patrocinado. O objetivo geral é examinar os limites jurídicos dessa atuação à luz do Código de Defesa do Consumidor, do Código Civil, da Lei n.º 14.790/2023 e das diretrizes de autorregulamentação publicitária. A pesquisa adota metodologia bibliográfica e documental. Conclui-se que, quando atuam mediante remuneração ou vantagem econômica, os influenciadores digitais podem assumir deveres de informação, transparência e boa-fé perante os consumidores, podendo ser responsabilizados civilmente quando sua conduta contribui para induzir o público em erro, ocultar riscos relevantes ou estimular expectativas irreais de ganho.

title: Pleasure, Appetite, and the Things Christians Call Harmless
abstract: This chapter examines the moral and spiritual life of pleasure in a culture where appetite is increasingly treated as self-validating and where many practices are defended with the sentence, "It is harmless." Its governing claim is not that pleasure is evil, but that every pleasure must remain a gift under the lordship of Jesus Christ rather than becoming a master, an anesthetic, a substitute savior, or a rival source of identity. Scripture affirms wine, food, feasting, rest, music, celebration, recreation, beauty, friendship, and bodily enjoyment as creaturely goods, while also warning against drunkenness, intoxication, greed, dissipation, gluttony, sloth, occult participation, and every form of enslavement. The chapter therefore rejects both permissiveness and ascetic legalism. It refuses to call every enjoyable practice sin merely because it is pleasurable, and it refuses to call a practice safe merely because Scripture does not name its modern form explicitly. Using the biblical categories of command, principle, wisdom, conscience, liberty, stewardship, love, and mastery, the chapter evaluates alcohol, nicotine and vaping, cannabis and other recreational drugs, prescription-drug misuse, gambling and sports betting, speculative trading, gaming and streaming, artistic entertainment, occult-themed media and spiritual curiosity, celebrity culture and parasocial desire, food and fasting, sleep and leisure, and the broader problem of good gifts becoming controlling appetites. Contemporary public-health and behavioral evidence is used descriptively where it clarifies dependence, gambling harm, gaming disorder, binge-watching, parasocial engagement, obesity, sleep, and substance-related risk. Medical treatment is carefully distinguished from intoxication, necessary medication from misuse, and clinical research with psychedelics from recreational or spiritualized drug use. New Age, New Thought, manifestation, divination, entheogenic spirituality, and occult experimentation are examined where pleasure and altered consciousness are presented as routes to awakening, guidance, or divine access. The chapter argues that Christian liberty is not the right to ask how close one may live to enslavement while remaining technically permitted. Christian freedom is freedom to belong to Christ, love the neighbor, discipline appetite, receive created goods with thanksgiving, and surrender any gift that begins to rule the heart. The drunk, smoker, gambler, compulsive gamer, binge-watcher, comfort eater, celebrity-obsessed fan, exhausted workaholic, and fearful legalist are not identical cases and must not be treated with one slogan. Yet all are summoned to the same Savior. Christ alone justifies, abstinence cannot save, and pleasure cannot condemn the repentant believer who comes to Him. At the same time, grace must never be turned into permission for intoxication, bondage, waste, spiritual dullness, or idolatry. The chapter concludes by calling the reader from appetite as authority to Christ as Lord, from false reassurance to sober self-examination, and from temporary pleasure to holy joy, durable freedom, and readiness for His return.

title: A Study on Marketing Environment with Reference to Betting Apps in India
abstract: This study explores the burgeoning online betting app market in India, highlighting its rapid expansion fueled by increased smartphone usage, widespread internet access, and the integration of digital payment systems like UPI. The rise of fantasy sports and real-money gaming platforms has transformed the way Indian users engage with sports and mobile entertainment. The research delves into the intricate regulatory environment, marked by central and state-level legal complexities, evolving definitions of \\\"games of skill\\\" versus \\\"games of chance,\\\" and advertising restrictions that pose significant challenges to market Players. The study emphasizes the growing need for localization strategies, including support for regional languages, cultural relevance, and sport-specific targeting—especially cricket, which remains the dominant sport influencing user engagement. Using strategic marketing frameworks such as PESTLE and 5Cs analysis, the research examines how betting and fantasy platforms deploy aggressive promotions, influencer marketing, and intuitive app design to attract and retain users in a highly competitive environment. Through secondary data analysis, the project identifies key trends in user behavior, regulatory shifts, and market dynamics. It concludes that while the Indian betting app market holds substantial growth potential, long-term success depends on how well platforms navigate legal uncertainties, build consumer trust, and adopt responsible marketing practices tailored to the Indian audience. The findings offer valuable insights for marketers, app developers, and policy-makers interested in the evolving landscape of digital gaming and betting in India.

title: Perceived parental attitudes and gambling behavior in adults: the moderating role of resilience
abstract: Introduction Although multiple risk factors for problematic gambling have been identified, evidence regarding perceived parental attitudes and resilience remains limited, particularly among adults in Türkiye. This study investigated the associations between perceived parental attitudes and gambling behavior and the moderating role of resilience. Methods A cross-sectional online correlational study was conducted in İstanbul, Türkiye, between October 2024 and May 2025 with 389 participants recruited via convenience sampling. Data were collected using the Abbreviated Perceived Parental Attitudes–Child Form, the Brief Psychological Resilience Scale, and the South Oaks Gambling Screen–Turkish Version. Moderator analyses with bias-corrected bootstrap confidence intervals were performed. Results Maternal rejection was positively associated with gambling severity (B = 0.106, 95% CI [0.053, 0.160], p < 0.001), as was paternal rejection (B = 0.123, 95% CI [0.073, 0.174], p < 0.001). Resilience significantly moderated both associations (maternal rejection × resilience: B = −0.017, 95% CI [−0.028, −0.005], p = 0.005; paternal rejection × resilience: B = −0.016, 95% CI [−0.028, −0.003], p = 0.012). Simple slope analyses showed that the associations between parental rejection and gambling severity were significant at low (maternal: B = 0.176, p < 0.001; paternal: B = 0.189, p < 0.001) and average (maternal: B = 0.106, p < 0.001; paternal: B = 0.123, p < 0.001) levels of resilience but were not significant at high resilience (maternal: B = 0.037, p = 0.265; paternal: B = 0.058, p = 0.092). Exploratory correlation analyses additionally showed that parental emotional warmth was positively associated with resilience. Discussion These findings suggest that resilience may buffer the association between perceived parental rejection and gambling severity.

title: Bad Bets: Examining the Legality of Sports-Related Prediction Markets
abstract: Historically, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission ("CFTC") employed a strict framework in which only prediction markets for research and academic value were permitted.This framework rejected political event contracts.In September 2024, a ruling from U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit as well as recent press releases from the Trump Administration have signaled a paradigm shift in the acceptance and legitimacy of prediction markets.This industry seized the moment and began offering event contracts over a broad swath of events including sports.These commercial platforms say their ability to offer sports-related event contracts are governed by the CFTC.However, the industry's position has drawn opposition from both state and Tribal Gaming Commissions, who view sports-related event contracts as sports gambling and subject to state law.This has led to an increase in legislation initiated by state and Tribal gaming regulators.This Note argues that sports-related event contracts are gambling and that the Supreme Court's ruling in Murphy v. NCAA prevents federal law from preempting state and Tribal gaming commissions from regulating these contracts.

title: From Murphy to Monopolies: Rethinking State Online Sports Betting Regulation
abstract: Since the Supreme Court’s decision in Murphy v. NCAA invalidated the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act, states have assumed exclusive authority over the regulation of sports betting. This decentralization has produced a highly fragmented regulatory landscape, particularly in the online sports betting market, where some states permit robust competition among numerous operators while others affirmatively sanction monopolies or highly concentrated markets. These state-level choices interact with an already concentrated national market dominated by DraftKings and FanDuel, creating significant variation in consumer choice, pricing, and regulatory outcomes across jurisdictions. This Note examines the sources and consequences of market power in online sports betting, distinguishing between naturally occurring national concentration and state-created intra-state market power. It situates state-sanctioned monopolies within the broader theoretical framework of “justified monopolies,” drawing comparisons to industries such as alcohol distribution, pharmaceuticals, telecommunications, and securities markets. Although proponents argue that monopolistic regulation can generate higher tax revenues, enhance consumer protection, and promote long-term innovation, this Note contends that online sports betting does not satisfy the conditions necessary to justify such market concentration. This Note argues that competitive online sports betting markets are better suited to advancing consumer welfare and regulatory goals than state-level monopolies. It further suggests that the current patchwork of state regimes risks distorting consumer behavior, reducing effective competition, and undermining potential gains from innovation. Drawing on the regulatory logic of Regulation National Market System in U.S. securities law, the Note proposes that competition—rather than state-imposed exclusivity—offers a more effective and adaptable framework for regulating online sports betting in the post-Murphy era.

title: AI-Assisted Bettors: Analyzing AI-Driven Betting Behavior through Cluster Analysis
abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) systems in consumer-facing decision-support systems (DSS) such as predictive analytics and automated recommendation platforms is growing in popularity in numerous domains, including sports betting. The degree to which users interact with the output of automated systems, calibrate trust, and exhibit automation bias–consistent behavior is largely unknown. In this study, we investigate the behavioral segments formed by bettors using AI-powered predictive sports betting DSS based on their shifts in confidence, risk-taking behavior, and bankroll management practices. We use survey data from a sample of 200 U.S.-based bettors and SPSS TwoStep Clustering to identify three distinct behavioral profiles: Traditional Bettors, AI-Influenced Confident Bettors, and AI-Adopting Risk-Takers, each with their own unique set of interactions with and through predictive DSS. The findings show that bettors can engage in responsible adoption through strategic bankroll management practices and a tempering of AI trust, while overreliance behaviors can be mitigated or amplified, respectively, by counter or co-aligning with individual differences. Framing betting platforms as real-time, in-the-wild, and consumer-deployed DSS contributes to IS research on algorithmic decision environments, user trust, and human–computer interaction. The results advance IS theory by contributing to the discussion of how cognitive biases, human decision behaviors, and confidence amplification in and through automated systems manifest in such domains. We conclude the paper with implications for responsible DSS design and deployment as well as practical guidelines for user segmentation in predictive analytics DSS environments.
venue: Journal of the Association for Information Systems

title: Predicting and Understanding Mobile Sports Gambling with the Reasoned Action Approach.
abstract: Mobile sports betting is an increasingly popular way to wager in the United States, but few studies have examined the social cognitive predictors of engaging in this specific form of gambling. The present studies were designed to do so with the application of the Reasoned Action Approach (RAA; Fishbein & Ajzen, 2010). Study 1 was a belief elicitation study that identified the most common behavioral, normative, and control beliefs regarding mobile sports betting. Study 1 also reported an initial test of the degree to which attitude, perceived normative pressure, and perceived behavioral control predict intentions to place mobile sports bets. Study 2 examined the predictive validity of the identified beliefs and tested whether future betting behavior can be predicted from the model. The RAA significantly predicted mobile sports gambling intentions and future behavior. The most important beliefs contributing to the prediction of mobile sports gambling were the degree that participants endorsed gambling is fun and easy, leads to addiction, and results in winning money. Implications for future research and interventions are discussed.
