title: Risk Governance in Esports Gambling: Addressing Integrity and Regulation in a Rapidly Evolving Ecosystem
abstract: Esports gambling has rapidly grown into a multi-billion-dollar global industry, incorporating traditional betting and fantasy esports. While this expansion brings exciting opportunities, it also presents significant risks, including threats to competitive integrity (match-fixing, cheating), financial vulnerabilities from unregulated skin-betting and cryptocurrency transactions, and social concerns like underage participation and problem gambling. Traditional risk management, which focuses on mitigating known risks within single organizations, is inadequate in this decentralized, transnational environment with diverse stakeholders: game publishers, tournament organizers, regulators, betting operators, and players. This presentation proposes risk governance as a more holistic approach to these challenges. Unlike reactive risk management, risk governance proactively anticipates, prioritizes, and addresses risks across organizational boundaries. It emphasizes collaboration between public and private sectors to create legitimacy, transparency, and trust while fostering innovation. By examining examples such as the Counter-Strike skin-betting scandal and Riot Games' evolving gambling policies in League of Legends, this presentation demonstrates how risk governance can address esports gambling’s systemic vulnerabilities. It advocates for governance frameworks that balance rapid technological innovation with consumer protection and competitive integrity.
venue: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)

title: Football World Cup 2026 Gambling Study
abstract: The present study includes online research into betting behaviour within the real-life context of the 2026 World Cup. Variables aside from descriptives that will be investigated are sports betting consumption, gambling problems, bet amount, preferred odds, bet choice motivation, subjective probability of the real-life bets, and subjective probability of an urn-and-ball task. The manipulation will be in the verbal framing of the bet (aggregated vs. disaggregated), and the verbal and visual framing of the urn-and-ball task (aggregated vs. disaggregated). The present research will investigate whether aggregated vs. disaggregated framing of the bets will change sports betting behaviour (bet amount). Additionally, the sports betting behaviour will be investigated as a function of subjective probabilities. The overall aim is to discover whether framing can be applied as a way to increase subjective probability, to subsequently lessen the amounts bet by sports bettors. Furthermore, the present study will add to the literature on determinants of betting behaviour, to eventually be used to inform policy on how (sports) bettors can be better protected. We hypothesize that bet amounts will differ between aggregated and disaggregated bet framing conditions. Since the preparation timeline of the study is very short and dependent on the FIFA World Cup 2026, we did not have sufficient time to preregister all analyses, but we will add amendments to this pre-registration to further specify additional analyses before inspection of the data (aside from quality checks).

title: Associations Between Gambling Motives and More Severe Gambling Disorder – Does Gender Matter?
abstract: Gambling Disorder (GD) is a behavioural addiction with complex, detrimental psychological, economic, and social consequences. Previous research has examined gender differences in the prevalence of distinct gambling motives and has linked gambling motives to at-risk behaviour. Whether motives affect probabilities of transition to higher GD severity levels differently in males and females remains unclear. Using an online self-test, we assessed the prevalence distinct GD severity levels according to the DSM-5 criteria and gambling motives with items addressing domains of the "Gambling Motives Questionnaire - Financial" (GFQ-F). Associations between motives and GD severity at three transition points (no GD to mild, mild to moderate, moderate to severe GD) were analysed using age-adjusted logistic adjacent category regression models. Interaction terms (motive*gender) were examined to detect gender-specific "effects". Furthermore gender-stratified models were run. No significant gender*motive interactions emerged. In the total sample, a transition to a higher GD severity level was predicted by: "(to) Forget worries", "When depressed," and "(to) Earn money" at each transition point; "Thrill" and "Stress" at the first two points, and "Boredom" at the first point. In males, the results were nearly identical. In females only "Thrill", "Boredom", and "(to) Earn money" were predictive at the first transition point. Given the prevalence of coping motives in females and the consistent detrimental "effect" of coping and financial motives in males, these motives should be prioritized in treatment and support offers for both genders. For prevention, strategies targeting enhancement motives may be particularly effective.

title: Beat the Sportsbook: The Theory and Practice of Successful Sports Betting
abstract: Sports betting is a major sector of American Gaming economy. In 2024, Americans wagered almost $150 billion dollars in legal online and brick and mortar sportsbooks, resulting in record industry revenue of $13.7 billion. Moreover, sports betting holds a particular importance for gaming operators as it attracts younger and more affluent consumers, most of whom would be unlikely to participate in other casino games, such as slot machines. Some purists claim that betting on sports jeopardizes the integrity of competition; however that argument does not pass the test of time. As a matter of fact, historians have found that when sports emerged gambling did too. Separating the two may be impossible. Also, in many ways having sports betting operate in a regulated transparent market is superior to illegal betting and opaque rules. Despite the popularity of sports betting, public consensus holds that it is nearly impossible for bettors to overcome the vig (fee sportsbooks charge for booking a bet) and make money in the long run. While other forms of risk taking, such as investing in high-risk growth stocks, high-yield bonds, and cryptocurrencies, are viewed as daring risk taking, sports betting still has a negative social stigma. In this research we explore quantitative and qualitative strategies that allow sports bettors to overcome the inherent odds disadvantages and realize both the theoretical (expected value) and practical (actual results) positive returns on their sports wagers.
venue: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)

title: Branding Through Sport
abstract: Branding through sport encompasses the strategies of non-sport organizations to build and enhance their own brands through the vehicle of sport. The chapter explores how brands leverage fans’ existing emotional attachments toward players and teams to strengthen a given company’s/product’s brand equity. Relevant concepts are discussed including brand equity, image transfer, parasocial relationships, source credibility, and athlete endorsement. Emerging trends including artificial intelligence and sport betting are also overviewed in the context of branding through sport. The chapter closes with managerial implications for key stakeholders and an international case study exploring the strategic partnership between FC Barcelona and Spotify.

title: The Intersection of Sport Betting and Consumer Behavior: A Systematic Review
abstract: Sport betting is a popular and lucrative entertainment segment of the sport industry. As such, understanding consumer behavior across the betting experiences is critical for the many stakeholders involved. The current study is a systematic quantitative literature review which assesses the current state of literature that intersects sport betting and consumer behavior literature, specifically cognitive, affective, conative, and consumption behavior of the sport bettors. The purpose of the systematic review is to (1) identify the most recent sport betting consumer behavior research, (2) compile and examine theoretical frameworks guiding sport gambling consumer research, (3) provide a descriptive summary of findings from previous sports betting consumer behavior research, and (4) provide an agenda for future research on the topic, identifying theoretical and practical implications for additional inquiry. This systematic quantitative literature review on 49 sports betting consumer behavior studies found no consistent application of theory, a bias toward quantitative research designs, and inconsistent scale usage to measure common sport betting related constructs. Future work should aim to publish more consistently in sport management or gambling studies journals, to employ scales to measure key constructs like sport betting behavior and diversify research design approaches.

title: The Effects of Game-Related Experiences on Delinquent Behavior among Adolescents: The Mediating Roles of Gambling Problem Perception and Gambling Experience.
abstract: This study aims to examine the effect of adolescents’ game-related experiences on deviant behavior and to analyze whether problem gambling perception and gambling experience serve as mediating variables in this relationship. In recent years, digital gaming environments have become a primary leisure space for adolescents. However, concerns have been raised as these environments increasingly incorporate gambling-like features, such as loot boxes, virtual item trading, and sports betting-related elements, which may lead to gambling behaviors and subsequent deviant activities. This study goes beyond examining direct effects by structurally testing a parallel mediation model in which problem gambling perception and gambling experience function as key mediators between game-related experiences and deviant behavior. The analysis utilized data from the “2022 National Survey on Youth Gambling Problems” conducted by the Korea Center on Gambling Problems, with a total sample of 18,944 adolescents, including both in-school and out-of-school youth. The results indicate that game-related experiences have a significant positive effect on deviant behavior. In addition, game-related experiences were found to negatively influence problem gambling perception while positively affecting gambling experience. The mediation analysis revealed that game-related experiences influence deviant behavior through both a cognitive pathway, which weakens problem gambling perception, and a behavioral pathway, which increases gambling experience. These findings suggest that adolescents’ gaming experiences extend beyond mere leisure activities and may contribute to deviant behavior through gambling-related perceptions and behaviors. This study highlights the need for preventive policy approaches that move beyond reactive control strategies. Specifically, it emphasizes the importance of proactively managing gambling-like elements within gaming environments and enhancing adolescents’ awareness of gambling risks as part of comprehensive prevention efforts.
venue: The Korean Society of Private Security

title: Introduction
abstract: This introduction traces a personal and intellectual journey rooted in childhood play, situating games as a foundational force in identity formation, creativity, and lifelong learning. Drawing on memories of growing up in a small village in upstate New York, the narrative explores informal, imaginative play – ranging from backyard sports and solitary role-playing to tabletop and early fantasy sports games – as a formative medium for social connection, emotional expression, and creative experimentation. These early experiences with play, chance, and invention are shown to anticipate later intellectual interests in game design, probability, imagination, and the pedagogical value of play. By weaving autobiography with cultural references to sport, film, literature, and philosophy, the introduction frames play not as trivial diversion but as a serious, generative activity that shapes cognition, relationships, and meaning across the lifespan. The chapter ultimately positions play as both a source of joy and a complex psychological force – capable of fostering creativity, mental health, and learning, while also carrying the potential for conflict and destruction – setting the stage for a broader psychoanalytic and educational exploration of play in the chapters that follow.

title: Corporate Political Strategies and Discursive Frames of the Gambling Industry in Finland's Gambling Policy Reform
abstract: Aims Finnish gambling policy, long based on a state-controlled monopoly, is set to shift to a license-based regime in 2027. The study investigates the Corporate Political Activity (CPA) strategies and discursive frames used by gambling industry actors, comparing their application among actors and phases of the legislative process in the context of Finland's gambling policy reform. Methods In total, 36 formal statements were analyzed, including submissions to the public consultation ( n = 19) and parliamentary hearings ( n = 17). A deductive content analysis was conducted, based on the previous CPA frameworks. Results The results indicate that gambling industry actors proposed alternative policies and sought to prevent certain parts of the legislation from being enacted. Discursive framings shifted throughout the legislative process: legal rights dominated consultations, while unintended effects, especially increased unlicensed gambling, became more salient in parliamentary hearings. Clear differences emerged among actors. International actors prioritized policy substitution and framed the proposed legislation as excessive and harmful to their legal rights, whereas the state monopoly operator did not prevent enactment of regulations. A further difference concerned proposals to replace some harm-reduction measures with more restrictive alternatives. Conclusions The growing influence of the gambling industry may risk deprioritizing the prevention and reduction of gambling harm in future gambling policy.
venue: Nordic Studies on Alcohol and Drugs

title: How Indian Law Can Take On Prediction Market Giants
abstract: <p><span>Indian gaming has been the lifeblood for many tribes. In 2024, tribal gaming brought in $43.9 billion in gross revenue. But online sports betting poses “an existential threat to Tribal sovereignty and economies.” Prediction markets like Kalshi operate as “designated contract market[s]” accessible in anywhere in the country. These platforms tout themselves as “CFTC regulated” exchanges that allow users to “trad[e] on the outcome of future events.” Users can trade on sports events like NBA matches (and can even get a $10 trading bonus if they use a Kalshi promo code). With billions at stake, states and tribes have gone to court. There are at least nineteen pending federal lawsuits involving online prediction markets. Recently, the Third Circuit ruled in favor of Kalshi. Meanwhile, the Ninth Circuit just heard oral arguments, and observers there noted the bench’s skepticism towards the prediction markets. Tribes and tribal gaming associations have submitted amici urging courts to rule against these platforms. California tribes have sued Kalshi specifically for IGRA violations, and are currently appealing a district court’s decision.</span></p> <p><span>&nbsp;</span></p> <p><span>This paper argues that an IGRA-centered interpretation can resolve whether prediction markets’ sports-related contracts are “gaming” as it relates to tribal lands. By using traditional statutory interpretation principles to grapple with IGRA’s text, the law points to one conclusion: that Kalshi’s sports-related operations is class III gaming under IGRA. Therefore, absent a Tribal-State compact authorizing its operation, Kalshi’s operations on Indian lands violates the Unlawful Internet Gambling Enforcement Act (UIGEA). This paper does not substantively focus on whether sports-related events contracts are “swaps” under the Commodities Exchange Act (CEA). This paper does argue that even if they could be considered “swaps” under federal law, Indian pre-emption doctrine would preclude CEA to render IGRA surplusage. This paper also proposes that tribal-state compacting offers a solution. Of course, a statutory fix could resolve this problem in a broad stroke. But the “hub-and-spoke” tribal-state compact model could serve as a desirable solution for both states and tribes. As online prediction giants unlawfully threaten tribal gaming, courts need not look further than IGRA itself to resolve this dispute.</span></p>

title: A qualitative investigation of the retrospective lived experiences and emotional trajectories of Australian gamblers
abstract: PURPOSE: The current study sought to understand and explore how gamblers retrospectively characterise the shifts in their emotional valence across a gambling session, and how they interpret changes in their emotional arousal as a gambling session unfolds. METHODS: A total of 20 Australian gamblers, aged between 20 and 63 years (Mage = 34.9, SDage = 10.23), participated in retrospective semi-structured interviews. Participants were asked to reconstruct and narrate the emotional shifts experienced across gambling sessions and elucidate how they interpreted and understood the changes in their emotions as a gambling session unfolded. Data was analysed via reflexive thematic analysis using an interpretivist epistemological framework. RESULTS: Five key themes were constructed from the data: (1) Affective Recovery: Feelings of Pride and Competence Through Mastery; (2) Affective Shift: Isolation to Feelings of Belonging; (3) Navigating Experiences of Negative Valence; (4) Anticipatory Excitement to In-Game Arousal; and (5) Escalating Affective Intensity and Emotional Urgency. CONCLUSION: This study challenges traditional paradigms by demonstrating that both positive and negative emotions act as highly fluid drivers during and after a gambling session. These insights may prompt further research into investigating emotional mechanisms that drive and maintain an individual's gambling.
venue: International Journal of Qualitative Studies on Health and Well-Being

title: Beyond cognitive distortions: the mediating role of passion between erroneous cognitions and gambling severity
abstract: Objective: While erroneous gambling cognitions and gambling passion (harmonious and obsessive) are recognised as key factors underpinning an individual's gambling, limited research has examined whether passion explains how cognitive distortions relate to gambling severity. Method: = 11.52). . Results: Controlling for gambling preference, frequency, and social desirability, predictive control exhibited a significant negative indirect path to gambling severity via harmonious passion, whereas obsessive passion positively mediated the relationship between illusion of control, interpretive bias, and gambling severity. Furthermore, obsessive passion significantly (negatively) moderated the relationship between interpretive bias and gambling severity. Conclusion: Findings suggest that when individuals overestimate predictive control, they may cognitively minimise risks associated with their gambling. Additionally, internal pressure from obsessive passion could inflate perceived control over random outcomes and heighten the tendency to attribute outcomes to skill. Moderation results indicated obsessive passion may exert a stronger influence on gambling severity than interpretive bias. Overall, findings highlight the need to target both gambling cognitions and passion when addressing an individual's gambling severity.

title: Harmonious and obsessive gambling passion: a comparative analysis of non-problem to problem gamblers
abstract: While researchers have investigated the link between gambling and passion, there is currently a paucity of literature detailing the precise relationship between harmonious and obsessive passion across the full spectrum of this behavior. The current study aimed to investigate the association between these passion constructs and empirically established levels of gambling severity: non-problem, low-risk, moderately at-risk, and problem gamblers. A total of (n = 630) gamblers aged between 18 and 73 (Mage = 38.56, SDage = 11.52) recruited via the general community and through Prolific.co, completed an online survey consisting of the Gambling Passion Scale (GPS), Problem Gambling Severity Index (PGSI) and the Short-Marlowe-Crowne Social Desirability Scale (S-MCSDS). Partial correlations revealed a significant weak negative correlation between harmonious passion and PGSI scores, and a strong positive partial correlation between obsessive passion and PGSI scores. Results from one-way ANOVAs showed that problem gamblers scored significantly higher on both harmonious and obsessive passion compared to the non-problem, low-risk and moderately at-risk gamblers. Findings from the current study provide insights into the role of passion in problem gambling and suggest that both may be salient toward an individual’s gambling behavior. Given these results, clinicians should consider focusing on the construct of passion when assessing and classifying a gambler’s risk profile. Focusing on passion may also elucidate a more holistic understanding of individuals’ perception of their own gambling behavior, which, in turn, could facilitate the development of more refined, personalized intervention strategies.

title: Going for Broke: The Impact of Gambling Legalization on Larceny
abstract: Since the Supreme Court overturned PASPA in 2018, many states have legalized sports betting while others have not. This has created an opportunity to study whether legalized sports betting is associated with changes in crime. While much of the existing research focuses on gambling addiction and financial hardship, fewer studies have examined whether legalization is related to changes in crimes. This project compares states with and without legalized sports betting, including North Carolina, South Carolina, Alabama, Mississippi, Wisconsin, Minnesota, and Pennsylvania. Annual data from 2011 through 2024 are being collected from sources such as the FBI Crime Data Explorer, the U.S. Census Bureau, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and the Federal Reserve Economic Data database. In addition to crime, the analysis includes poverty, unemployment, educational attainment, population density, government safety net programs, and drug and alcohol use so that the effect of sports betting can be examined while accounting for other factors that influence crime. The goal of this research is to determine whether sports betting legalization has an independent relationship with crime after controlling for these economic and demographic variables. The findings may provide a better understanding of the broader social impacts of legalized sports betting and contribute to future policy discussions surrounding gambling expansion.

title: NORMATIVE INFLUENCE ON SPORTS BETTING AMONG YOUNG MEN IN GHANA
abstract: Sports betting has become an increasingly visible feature of everyday sport culture in Ghana, yet theory-driven communication research explaining how betting becomes socially normalized among young men remains limited. Drawing on the theory of normative social behavior and its communication-centered reconceptualization, this dissertation used an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design to examine how interpersonal communication, observation, and media exposure shape perceived norms, and how those norms relate to sports betting and its associated harms. Study One used semi-structured interviews with ten young Ghanaian men who bet on sports. Participants described a filtered communication environment in which wins circulate widely, losses are minimized or withheld, and audiences are carefully selected. Betting appeared ordinary because young men encountered it through friends, betting shops, phones, advertisements, sports media, and public debate. At the same time, participants described avoiding the people most likely to object, including parents, partners, religious figures, and non-betting peers. The qualitative findings showed that betting was widely normalized as participation, but not uniformly approved, and that help-seeking was constrained because admitting a desire to stop also meant admitting that betting was no longer working. Study Two tested the proposed communication-centered normative pathway in a survey of 314 young Ghanaian men who bet on sports. The results showed a consistent distinction between descriptive and injunctive norms. Perceived descriptive norms were predicted by observation of referent others, media exposure, and communication frequency, and were associated with betting frequency. Perceived injunctive norms were predicted only by positive and excitatory betting talk and were associated with PGSI-SB severity. Indirect-association models showed that descriptive norms accounted for pathways from communication frequency, observation, and media exposure to betting frequency, while injunctive norms accounted for the pathway from positive betting talk to PGSI-SB severity. Outcome expectations and pro-betting attitudes strengthened the association between injunctive norms and PGSI-SB severity. Together, the findings show that communication does more than accompany sports betting. It helps make betting visible, frames what is worth sharing, signals what appears common or approved, and shapes the conditions under which young men can disclose harm or seek support. Findings distinguish the normative processes associated with how often young men bet from those associated with how much harm they experience. The findings clarify communication mechanisms relevant to harm reduction, including the potential value of correcting one-directional information environments and of addressing the disclosure barriers that discourage help-seeking.

TRADING ATHLETES: THE UNREGULATED MARKET of INDIAN FANTASY PLAYER STOCKS
abstract: This article examines the regulatory challenges posed by Fantasy Player Stock Trading (FPST) platforms in India, which uniquely blend gaming and financial market mechanics. Unlike traditional fantasy sports, FPST platforms utilize sophisticated trading features, including algorithmic pricing, leveraged positions, and market-driven price discovery. This analysis demonstrates that current gaming regulations and self-regulatory mechanisms are inadequate to address the inherent complexities of FPSTs, which operate like unregulated securities markets. Although FPST tokens do not neatly fit the legal definition of “securities,” their functional equivalence with financial markets, coupled with their addictive design and systemic vulnerabilities, necessitates a bespoke regulatory framework and oversight. This article underlines the necessity of immediate regulatory attention to protect gamers, advocating for a new regulatory approach beyond existing gambling or gaming parameters.

title: At the Crossroads: Sports Betting in Missouri and Proposals for Regulations
abstract: Sports betting is a rapidly growing industry nationwide, and Missouri became the 39th state to legalize the practice. Although states hope to reap the benefits of a regulated sports gambling market, the activity carries significant mental, physical, and socioeconomic risks due to its inherently addictive nature. The hyper-accessibility of modern platforms, particularly those enabling unlimited micro betting, magnifies longstanding concerns in a new digital context. Compounding these risks, the absence of federal standards for minimum wagering ages and the aggressive marketing strategies employed by sportsbooks draw in young adults. This article proposes a coordinated federal and state regulatory framework that would establish a minimum wagering age, constrain sportsbooks’ marketing practices, and limit micro-betting options to better protect consumers in Missouri.

title: ANALYZING THE DETERMINANTS, PSYCHOLOGICAL CORRELATES, AND INTERVENTION STRATEGIES FOR ONLINE GAMING ADDICTION AMONG AVIATOR BET USERS IN NAIROBI COUNTY, KENYA
abstract: The rapid proliferation of digital gaming and betting platforms has fundamentally transformed patterns of leisure, economic participation, and behavioral health across the globe, with particularly acute implications for emerging digital economies in sub-Saharan Africa. The small but growing niche occupied by hybridal types of gaming-gambling games, like the Aviator Bet service, has combined real-time wagering systems with the high frequency nature of gaming in ways that increase the susceptibility to compulsive and addictive behavior. The overlap of efforts to provide a mobile financial infrastructure, most prominently M-Pesa, and a greater Sony number of more advanced online betting technologies has provided a space in which younger adult online gambling addicts are uniquely predisposed to form behavioral addiction patterns. The paper explores the predictors, mental factors, and treatment consequences of online gaming addiction between the users of Aviator Bet in the Nairobi County, Kenya with the two-fold aim of defining the extent of the issue, and analyzing evidence-based interventions.To obtain convergent qualitative and quantitative data, a parallel mixed-methods approach was used that combined quantitative survey data that was gathered on 248 participants who are adults and qualitative information obtained via the in-depth interview. The study sample was selected using stratified sampling in the different sub-counties in Nairobi, which is a diverse city and peri-urban area. The high prevalence of moderate to severe online gaming addiction was found as quantitative results, where 62.5% of the participants fit the criteria of engaging in a way that was considered to be clinically significant. Regression analysis proved the severity of addiction as a significant predictor of psychological distress (0.48, p <.001) and significant positive correlation was identified between addiction severity and anxiety (r =.52), depression (r =.49) and perceived stress (r =.46). Social outcomes were also evident with high addiction levels showing the existence of financial strain ( 0.41, p <.01), interpersonal conflict ( ${-0.37, p <.01).It is the qualitative data that complemented these quantitative trends by pointing to cognitive distortions such as illusions of control and gamblertype fallacy thinking, maladaptive coping styles, vulnerability of socioeconomic status and peer normalization as primary psychosocial influences in perpetuating and maintaining compulsive involvement.
venue: International Journal of Social Sciences and Management Review

title: WHEN LEGALIZATION PRECEDES REGULATION: REGULATORY TIMING AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF SPORTS BETTING MARKETS
abstract: Governments increasingly face the challenge of regulating newly legalized markets while simultaneously protecting consumers and mitigating social harms. While existing research has focused primarily on the design of regulatory instruments, comparatively little attention has been devoted to the consequences of delaying regulation after legalization. This article develops a regulatory sequencing perspective to examine how the timing of regulation may influence market development and consumer behavior. Drawing on the legalization of fixed-odds sports betting in Brazil, where a comprehensive regulatory framework was implemented several years after legalization, this article argues that delayed regulation shaped the market environment policymakers inherited. It identifies three mechanisms through which this occurred: the normalization of betting and the diffusion of consumer beliefs before the implementation of effective consumer protection measures; the widespread adoption of high-engagement product and platform design features in the absence of regulatory constraints; and the reduced capacity of regulatory institutions to influence market dynamics after commercial practices and industry structures had become established. Rather than treating regulatory timing as a procedural detail, this article argues that it constitutes an important determinant of policy effectiveness in newly legalized markets. Beyond the Brazilian case, the analysis contributes to broader debates on gambling regulation by highlighting how the sequencing of legalization and regulation can shape both market trajectories and the effectiveness of subsequent regulatory intervention.

title: Understanding the Socio-Demographic Profiles and Motivations behind Youth Participation in Sports Betting: A case study of Dar es Salaam City, Tanzania
abstract: This study examines the socio-demographic profiles and motivations of youth sports bettors in Dar es Salaam city, Tanzania. The study employed a cross-sectional design; data were collected from 205 participants across five wards through mixed-methods analysis. Both primary and secondary data were used in this study, while the data analysis involved SPSS. The study is anchored in Rational Choice Theory, Social Learning Theory and Sustainable Livelihood Frameworks; challenging the "idleness" myth, and suggesting that sports betting is a rational, albeit high-risk, adaptive strategy to structural economic constraints and urban income instability. Findings reveal that betting participation is not limited only to marginalized youth. While economic gain serves as the primary driver; social environments play a critical role in sustaining betting practices. The study concludes that social learning in urban hubs (vijiwe) sustains participation beyond initial entry. Recommendations include implementing stricter zoning regulations for betting outlets near residential areas and developing community-based programs that offer more stable financial growth than speculative gambling. This research emphasizes shifting policy from moralistic discouragement toward evidence-based structural interventions beyond Dar es Salaam context.

title: Implementing Lower Latency, Fast Startup and Switching for low-latency low-delay (L3D) DASH
abstract: Low-latency video streaming is essential for interactive applications such as sports betting and live concerts. The sixth edition of the MPEG DASH specification introduces new features enabling the L3D-DASH (Low Latency, Low Delay DASH) approach, which aims to minimize startup times and playback latencies. This paper presents an overview of L3D-DASH and details its implementation on the encoder and packager side, as well as on the client-side. We describe the encoding and packaging pipeline optimized for ultra-low-latency, including parallel video streams with distinct IDR placement strategies and the use of the Live Media Ingest protocol for efficient media delivery. On the client side, we discuss the implementation in dash.js and the challenges of L3D-DASH, such as adaptive bitrate switching and precise playback start and seeking. We then compare the performance of L3D DASH against classic non low latency DASH content. Initial results demonstrate that L3D-DASH achieves faster startup and a more stable low latency playback compared to classic DASH content. These findings highlight the potential of L3D-DASH to advance the state of low-latency streaming and improve user experience in latency-sensitive scenarios.

title: A REGULAMENTAÇÃO DAS APOSTAS ESPORTIVAS E O RISCO DE MANIPULAÇÃO DE PARTIDAS DE FUTEBOL NO BRASIL
abstract: A significativa ampliação do número de apostas esportivas no Brasil, ocasionada pelas plataformas digitais, tem revelado riscos à integridade das competições e à segurança da atividade. A possibilidade de manipulação em partidas de futebol e a atuação de organizações criminosas expõem fragilidades no atual modelo regulatório. Portanto, este estudo tem por objetivo analisar os desafios jurídicos e institucionais atinentes à regulação da atividade de apostas esportivas no Brasil, considerando, sobretudo, os riscos concretos de manipulação de resultados e corrupção desportiva. A metodologia adotada é de natureza qualitativa, exploratória e teórico-dogmática, com base em análise bibliográfica. Os resultados indicam a existência de um arcabouço normativo incipiente, marcado pela ausência de tipificação penal específica, pela fragilidade institucional na fiscalização das casas de apostas e pela carência de integração entre os órgãos reguladores. Verificou-se que os mecanismos atuais de repressão são insuficientes para enfrentar supostos esquemas de manipulação de resultados, exigindo um modelo de governança mais estruturado, preventivo e aparelhado. Também foi possível constatar a necessidade de adoção de medidas como educação preventiva, auditorias, compliance esportivo e cooperação internacional. Conclui-se que a regulamentação das apostas esportivas depende da articulação entre legislação, fiscalização e políticas públicas integradas, a fim de proteger a integridade do esporte e a confiança da sociedade no sistema.

title: A RELAÇÃO ENTRE AS APOSTAS ESPORTIVAS DIGITAIS E A FRAGILIDADE DA EDUCAÇÃO FINANCEIRA NO BRASIL
abstract: O crescimento das apostas esportivas digitais no Brasil tem chamado cada vez mais a atenção devido aos seus impactos econômicos e comportamentais, especialmente entre jovens e pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade financeira. Nesse contexto, este estudo analisa a relação entre a expansão das apostas esportivas, a educação financeira e as condições socioeconômicas da população brasileira. Para isso, foi realizada uma pesquisa qualitativa de caráter bibliográfico e documental, baseada na análise de artigos científicos, relatórios institucionais e dados oficiais publicados entre 2020 e 2025. Os resultados indicam que a popularização das apostas está relacionada à facilidade de acesso às plataformas digitais, à intensa exposição publicitária e à busca por ganhos imediatos. Também foi observado que estados com menor renda média e maior dependência de programas de auxílio governamental de renda apresentam maior participação em apostas esportivas, sugerindo relação entre vulnerabilidade econômica e comportamentos financeiros de risco. Conclui-se que o avanço das apostas esportivas digitais está associado a fatores econômicos, sociais e comportamentais, reforçando a importância da educação financeira e de políticas públicas voltadas à conscientização e à prevenção do endividamento. Além disso, o tema demanda atenção crescente por parte da sociedade e da comunidade acadêmica. Para pesquisas futuras, recomenda-se a realização de estudos empíricos sobre os impactos das apostas nas finanças pessoais, na saúde mental e no comportamento dos indivíduos.

title: CENTRAL DE REGULAÇÃO DE VAGAS E RESPONSABILIDADE SISTÊMICA: UMA CRÍTICA À TRANSFERÊNCIA DO ÔNUS ESTRUTURAL DA SUPERLOTAÇÃO PRISIONAL AO PODER JUDICIÁRIO
abstract: O artigo analisa criticamente a Central de Regulação de Vagas (CRV), metodologia desenvolvida pelo Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) para enfrentar a superlotação do sistema prisional brasileiro. Sustenta-se que a CRV incorre em equívoco estrutural ao atribuir ao Judiciário o encargo de compensar omissões historicamente imputáveis ao Poder Legislativo — pelo progressivo endurecimento da política criminal sem correspondente provisão de vagas, tendência intensificada no biênio 2025-2026 — e ao Poder Executivo — pela insuficiência crônica de investimento em infraestrutura penitenciária e pelo redirecionamento de recursos das apostas esportivas para finalidades alheias à criação de vagas. O artigo reconhece a parcela de responsabilidade do Judiciário — especialmente pela manutenção de prisões preventivas além do prazo razoável e pelo represamento de progressões de regime — e aponta as contradições internas do próprio Poder Judiciário, que cobra da magistratura ordinária o combate à superlotação enquanto profere decisões com impacto expansivo sobre a população carcerária. O Amazonas é apresentado como estudo de caso paradigmático: estado com a segunda menor taxa de aprisionamento do país (166,10 por 100 mil habitantes), não por eficiência do sistema, mas por ausência estrutural de vagas, assolado por disputas faccionais desde 2016 e palco de dois massacres em unidades superlotadas (2017 e 2019). O fenômeno resultante é denominado ativismo judicial compulsório por omissão alheia: o juiz é responsabilizado por gerir o que décadas de inação executiva e legislativa não construíram. Ao final, propõem-se soluções de distribuição constitucionalmente adequada de responsabilidades entre os três Poderes.

title: Mulheres nas apostas esportivas no Brasil: crescimento, perfil e fatores determinantes em 2025
abstract: O presente estudo analisa o crescimento da participação feminina no mercado de apostas esportivas no Brasil, que atingiu 37% em 2025. O objetivo é compreender os fatores que impulsionam esse aumento, bem como identificar diferenças comportamentais em relação ao público masculino. A metodologia adotada foi de caráter exploratório, com base em dados secundários provenientes de relatórios de mercado e pesquisas setoriais. Os resultados indicam que o avanço da participação feminina está relacionado à maior inserção das mulheres no universo esportivo, à influência das redes sociais e ao fortalecimento da presença das apostas no cotidiano cultural. Além disso, observa-se que as mulheres tendem a adotar comportamentos mais cautelosos em relação ao risco. Conclui-se que o mercado está em processo de amadurecimento e que a compreensão desse público é importante para estratégias mais eficientes de marketing e desenvolvimento de produtos.

title: O papel dos influenciadores digitais na promoção de jogos de apostas online: uma análise sobre as práticas publicitárias e a proteção do consumidor The role of digital influencers in promoting online betting games: an analysis of advertising practices and consumer protection
abstract: Este artigo analisa a responsabilidade dos influenciadores digitais na promoção de jogos de azar online, focando nas implicações jurídicas relacionadas à publicidade enganosa e abusiva. O objetivo principal é investigar até que ponto os influenciadores podem ser responsabilizados pelas campanhas publicitárias de jogos de azar, considerando a legislação brasileira, como o Código de Defesa do Consumidor. A pesquisa foi conduzida por meio de uma revisão bibliográfica, com base em estudos sobre regulamentações nacionais e internacionais, além da análise de casos judiciais envolvendo influenciadores e plataformas de jogos de azar. O estudo também abordou conceitos como publicidade enganosa, abusiva e a responsabilidade dos influenciadores digitais nas redes sociais. Os resultados evidenciam que, apesar da legislação brasileira prever mecanismos aptos à proteção dos consumidores, existem lacunas na regulamentação que dificultam a aplicação eficiente das leis no ambiente digital. Foi identificado que muitos influenciadores promovem jogos de azar sem esclarecimentos adequados sobre os riscos financeiros, o que permite a caracterização de práticas vedadas pelo ordenamento. Conclui-se pela necessidade de aprimoramento normativo no que diz respeito à possibilidade de responsabilização dos influenciadores envolvidos em campanhas publicitárias de jogos de azar. A pesquisa aponta para a importância da criação de normas mais específicas que regulamentem essas práticas no ambiente digital, visando à proteção dos consumidores. Ademais, destaca-se a relevância de que estudos futuros aprofundem a análise dos impactos dessas campanhas sobre os indivíduos e da efetividade das regulamentações atualmente vigentes.

title: Operational non-invariance: event definition and temporal resolution determine the sign of the transactional contrast in gambling payment data
abstract: This project contains the complete reproduction package for the article "Operational non-invariance: event definition and temporal resolution determine the sign of the transactional contrast in gambling payment data." The central objective of this research is to investigate how the operational definition of a gambling event and the temporal resolution of observation shape the behavioral and financial conclusions drawn from transactional gambling data. The study starts from a metrological observation: research comparing player behavior using different event definitions — for example, an endogenous session-based definition (D0) versus fixed time windows (≤1h, ≤6h, ≤24h) — often produces opposite signs for the same phenomenon. Our work shows that this conflict is not a sampling artifact but a systematic property of the observation channel × estimator pair. We use three data sources: (i) public online sports betting and casino datasets from the literature (Mendeley, Transparency Project); (ii) anonymized Brazilian cooperative banking data on payments and transfers linked to gambling operators; and (iii) simulations of self-exciting point processes with negative-control calibration. The methodology combines non-parametric statistics (account-level bootstrap, risk-set matching, placebo reallocations), Hawkes intensity estimation across multiple temporal resolutions, and negative-control tests to validate conclusions. The expected and obtained results are: Proven operational non-invariance: at sub-daily resolution (exact, 15-minute, 1-hour), the endogenous D0 definition produces a positive contrast, while short fixed windows produce a negative contrast, with non-overlapping confidence intervals. This shows that the sign of "chasing" depends on how the event is defined. Collapse under aggregated resolution: when analysis is performed at daily or weekly resolution, intraday information is lost, fixed-window contrasts degenerate to zero, and D0 saturates at values determined by the discretization grid. This implies that aggregated-data studies cannot distinguish mechanism from measurement artifact. Failure of balance control as an isolated identifier: the available proxy for player cash flow (deposit minus withdrawal) is not identifiable in the dataset, limiting interpretations about "loss chasing driven by liquidity." Negative control and gate rejection: the research incorporates a pre-registration of calibration gates (G4/G5) that failed validation. The results confirm that Hawkes self-excitation can be confounded with persistent dispersion or seasonality, reinforcing that clinical interpretation of η̂ (estimated contagion intensity) requires intraday resolution and negative-control validation. The final output is a manuscript ready for submission to an international scientific journal, accompanied by a complete reproduction package (scripts, results, hashes, data provenance) allowing external auditing of all figures and tables. The project is a collaboration between SAVE Tecnologia em Saúde Mental, which develops predictive infrastructure for detecting risk-related behaviors in financial portfolios, and applied researchers in statistics, data science, and mental health. Expected impact We expect this work to: (a) establish a metrological vocabulary for behavioral gambling research using transactional data; (b) define minimum identifiability conditions for inferences about "chasing" and "loss chasing"; (c) guide intraday data collection by financial institutions and credit cooperatives monitoring client risk; and (d) provide a methodological foundation for future studies with validated clinical outcomes.

title: Os impactos das apostas online de quota fixa na sociedade
abstract: O presente artigo visa a esclarecer tópicos relevantes sobre as apostas online (bets) no âmbito do Direito Desportivo e na sociedade, tendo em vista que a disponibilização de apostas esportivas, no Brasil, vem desencadeando o endividamento das famílias, o que leva parte significativa da sociedade a um comportamento financeiro de altíssimo risco, prejudica consideravelmente a economia doméstica, o comércio varejista e o desenvolvimento social, diante do fato de que essa prática reiterada poderá evoluir para um comportamento compulsivo por parte de alguns indivíduos (transtorno do jogo patológico), o que, consequentemente, implicará o aumento no endividamento das famílias brasileiras, principalmente entre aqueles que veem neste tipo de aposta uma forma de solução rápida para suas dificuldades financeiras. Importante salientar que as bets têm como objeto principal o futebol, já que este esporte coletivo é o mais popular do mundo e, de acordo com os dados da Federação Internacional de Futebol (FIFA), cerca de 270 milhões de pessoas atuam em atividades diretamente relacionadas ao esporte. O mercado de apostas esportivas tem gerado bastante interesse dos setores ligados ao esporte profissional, sobretudo o futebol. Em 2022, dos vinte clubes da Série A do Campeonato Brasileiro de Futebol, apenas o Palmeiras não era patrocinado por alguma casa de apostas esportivas (Brito, 2022, n.p.). Desta forma, as bets uniram o útil ao agradável, ou seja, uniu a paixão que os brasileiros têm pelo futebol e a tentativa imediata de rápida solução para as suas dificuldades financeiras, o que cria, assim, um comportamento compulsivo perigoso por parte de alguns indivíduos. Estudos recentes, realizados após o advento da Lei n.º 14.790/2023 (Lei das Bets), vêm estabelecendo uma ligação forte e direta entre a prática descontrolada de apostas (facilitada pela ausência de regras mais efetivas de limitação ao jogo compulsivo) e o agravamento do nível de endividamento das famílias brasileiras (Charchat & Medeiros, 2024, n.p.).Esse assunto é um tema recente e desconhecido por grande parte dos doutores da lei; como a bibliografia a respeito é escassa, sua discussão depende de artigos, colunas, e da interpretação das próprias leis.
venue: Revista de Gestão e Negócios do Esporte

title: The Attention Factor: The Speculative Risk You May Already Own
abstract: Cryptocurrency and equity markets have become linked-and the linkage is intensifying. Bitcoin now shares roughly a quarter of its return variation with world equities during periods of elevated speculative participation, while gold shares near zero. An asset with no shared business fundamentals-cash flows, earnings, or production linkages has developed meaningful co-movement with equity markets. For allocators, understanding this linkage is not a crypto question-it is a portfolio risk question. We therefore test whether the linkage is entirely explained by shared exposure to economy-wide conditions-global market returns and risk appetite shifts. It is not. After removing these systematic channels, a residual connectedness survives-but not uniformly. The residual is largest for firms whose revenues depend mechanically on speculative participation (DraftKings, Robinhood, Coinbase) and for sentiment-driven strategies (BUZZ Social Sentiment ETF). For institutionally priced benchmarks like the Nasdaq-100 and AI stocks, residual connectedness drops to the level explained by shared market exposure alone-despite their popularity. This pattern suggests a common cause. Our hypothesis: the linkage transmits through shared marginal investors. A speculative cohort-retail traders active across crypto exchanges, zero-day options, sports betting, and commission-free brokerages-sets prices in multiple markets simultaneously. When this cohort's sentiment shifts, it creates correlated movements across every venue they participate in. Crypto, having no fundamental equity linkage, serves as the cleanest signal of this transmission. We interpret this transmission as an Attention factor-capital-backed collective conviction expressed by a speculative cohort active across multiple markets. The key finding is not binary. Every equity investor carries some speculative sentiment exposure through the market itself-crypto co-moves with world equities broadly, meaning this channel is already embedded in market returns. What varies is how much additional connectedness specific equities carry beyond this market-level dose. Thematic growth funds, small-cap indices, and social-sentiment strategies concentrate it. The relevant question for allocators is not whether to add crypto, but how much speculative sentiment exposure already exists in the portfolio-and where on the spectrum their holdings sit.

title: The Underground World of Influencer Trading Card Gambling or "Breaking"
abstract: This research explores the emerging phenomenon of "breaking", a practice whereby people, often influencers or card shop owners, open trading card packs in front of a live audience, selling randomized or selected packs to their viewers. Using a netnographic approach, I investigate three major online communities "breakers" use to facilitate the breaking practice. Initial participant observation and data includes 200+ social media posts, 20+ hours of video, and significant participant observation in live channels. Preliminary findings suggest that the power of influencers combined with the gambling psychology of collectible trading cards create a highly persuasive environment where community members are socially celebrated and encouraged to continue to purchase or "gamble" in front of a large audience. Major themes include: community-seeking, peer-pressure, belonging, and parasocial relationships. These findings suggest that trading card "breaking" has some parallels with the emergence of sports betting, particularly the social aspect and involvement of influencers. The findings also suggest a glorification and valorization of consumer participation in gambling, particularly when influencers are opening packs in front of large audiences.
venue: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)

title: Cross-Cultural Adaptations of Gambling Treatments for East Asians: A Comprehensive Scoping Review and Strategic Recommendations
Gambling Advertising During the UEFA Euro Football Championship: A Frequency and Content Analysis in TV Coverage and Social Media
abstract: Abstract: Aims: According to the German State Treaty on Gambling, gambling advertising must not be excessive. However, what counts as excessive is not defined, nor are there any frameworks for classifying advertising. The present study therefore quantifies and classifies gambling advertising during a specific sports event. Methodology: 11 matches of the 2024 European Football Championship were analyzed with respect to frequency and type of gambling advertising. Besides, the social media accounts of 10 sports betting providers were examined. The Meta Ad Library was used to analyze paid-for advertisements. Results: A high volume of gambling advertising is prevalent (n = 5,914), especially during TV broadcasts, where it mostly appears on pitchside hoardings without age restrictions or warnings. On social media (n = 2,645), gambling providers mainly rely on content marketing for organic advertising (1,542), whereas paid-for advertisements (1,103) are more direct and targeted towards a younger audience. Conclusions: Due to the high advertising volume and the room for improvement regarding the implementation of social responsibility measures, it remains uncertain whether the objectives of the Treaty, aimed at protecting the population from gambling-related harm, can be fully achieved. The scope, content, and strategies of these advertisements raise concerns, particularly about the risks for children and adolescents.
venue: SUCHT - Zeitschrift für Wissenschaft und Praxis / Journal of Addiction Research and Practice

title: SPORTS BETTING: JUDICIAL INTERPRETATION AND LEGAL CHALLENGES IN INDIA
abstract: This paper explores the jurisprudential evolution of gaming and sports betting laws in India, analyzing the ongoing conflict between archaic colonial statutes and the dynamic realities of the digital economy. Historically, the Indian judiciary has served as the de facto regulator of the industry, establishing the "preponderance of skill" test to distinguish between constitutionally protected business activities under Article 19(1)(g) and prohibited games of chance (res extra commercium). Through a comprehensive analysis of landmark judgments—ranging from R.M.D. Chamarbaugwala (1957) to Varun Gumber (2017)—the research traces how the courts have consistently defended skill-based digital and physical enterprises against disproportionate and arbitrary state-level bans. However, the paper highlights a contemporary constitutional crisis triggered by the recent enactment of the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act (PROGA), 2025. By imposing a blanket prohibition on all "Online Money Games" regardless of the underlying skill element, PROGA 2025 seeks to override decades of established judicial precedent. The study critically evaluates the ongoing legal challenges to the Act, specifically focusing on the Union's legislative competence, the disruption of the federal structure, and the violation of fundamental rights. Finally, it examines the counterproductive outcomes of this prohibitionist legislative approach, notably the proliferation of a $100 billion offshore shadow market and the inadvertent criminalization of legitimate professional sports. The paper concludes that the upcoming 2026 Supreme Court hearings will be a watershed moment, determining both the survival of a multi-billion-dollar industry and the boundaries of parliamentary power over State subjects in the digital age. Keywords: Sports Betting, Games of Skill vs. Chance, PROGA 2025, Judicial Interpretation, Article 19(1)(g)

title: Fantasy Sports App Participation and Its Impact on Sports Consumption Among Indian Youth
abstract: Fantasy sports platforms have changed how young people in India consume and engage with sport, resulting in a shift from passive spectators to active participants who make choices, analyze player statistics, and compete for either monetary or social gain. This study examines the effects of fantasy sports participation on sports consumption behaviors in Indian youth aged 18-25, and how the regulatory ban on real-money fantasy contests, effective in 2025, influenced these consumption behaviors. This study follows a mixed-method explanatory sequential design, integrating quantitative survey data collected from 105 valid respondents with qualitative interviews to capture both statistical and experiential perspectives. During the quantitative phase, a within-subject pre-post design compared self-reported engagement in sport before the ban and after the ban in three areas of interest: hours of watching live matches, OTT subscriptions, and self-rated interest in sport. Analyzing for changes in the self-reported engagement metrics consisted of paired-sample t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, with regression analysis as a way to control for demographics and motivation. Results reveal a significant decline in sports consumption post-ban: average weekly viewing hours fell by 2.3, OTT subscriptions dropped by 0.28, and sports interest decreased by 2.3 points on a 7-point scale (p &lt; 0.001). Qualitative insights confirmed that the absence of monetary incentives and peer competition reduced both motivation and emotional attachment to sports. The findings suggest that fantasy sports act as a behavioral catalyst for sports engagement, amplifying consumption through informational, motivational, and social pathways. The study concludes that while the ban curbed potential gambling risks, it also weakened the broader sports consumption ecosystem. Policymakers should adopt calibrated regulation emphasizing responsible gaming and transparency rather than outright prohibition. The paper contributes empirically grounded evidence to the literature on digital fandom, gamified engagement, and regulatory policy in India's evolving sports economy.

title: A randomized double-blind sham-controlled preliminary study of a 5-week protocol of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) combined with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for gambling disorder in Indonesia
abstract: Gambling disorder (GD) has increased in prevalence particularly in Indonesia where online gambling predominates. Gambling harm may involve not only individuals with GD but also their significant others. This preliminary study aims to investigate the efficacy of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) in conjunction with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) compared to sham rTMS with CBT in treating individuals with GD. Twenty seven participants diagnosed with GD were randomly assigned to receive either active or sham rTMS over five weeks, alongside a standardized CBT program. Outcomes were assessed at multiple time points using various standardized measures. This protocol was safe and well-tolerated, with minimal adverse events (adverse event rate: 7.2%). Both groups displayed significant reductions in gambling symptoms measured by the Gambling Symptom Assessment Scale. However, no significant differences were observed between the active and sham rTMS groups. The active rTMS group demonstrated faster reductions in gambling craving [B: 2.63 (95% CI 0.55 to 4.70), p: 0.015] and gambling-related cognition, particularly in the domains of gambling expectancies [B: 1.84 (95% CI 0.98 to 2.71), p ≤ 0.001] and the perceived inability to stop gambling [B: 1.70 (95% CI 0.36 to 3.04), p: 0.014]. The results suggest that rTMS may enhance CBT outcomes in treating GD by modulating craving and cognitive biases associated with gambling. Further research is warranted to optimize intervention parameters and assess the long-term effects of rTMS in GD treatment.

title: Law of Nino: A Unified Probabilistic and Multi-Agent Framework for Predictive Modeling in Sports, Mathematics, and Physics
abstract: We present the Law of Nino / NMSM-model, a novel probabilistic multi-agent framework for predictive modeling validated over five Premier League seasons (2021/22–2025/26). Integrating δ-formula, Hybrid Core, PSS, Ω(t), Backward Seed, Möbius-8 symmetry, and Poisson processes, the model achieves a Brier-score of 0.0398 (98.4% reliability) and an average hit-rate of 82.2% across 1,530 matches. The framework is adaptable beyond sports, capable of addressing mathematical problems (Fibonacci sequences, prime numbers, combinatorial proofs) and physical phenomena (Monte Carlo simulations in particle physics, cosmology). Applications include sports betting optimization, scenario analysis, and scientific modeling.

title: Decisions at Play: Influence of Gambling Advertisements and Influencer Content during FIFA World Cup 2026 on Attitudes, Cognitions, and Gambling Initiation
abstract: This project investigates how exposure to gambling advertisements, including sports betting, and influencer gambling-related content during the 2026 FIFA World Cup is associated with gambling-related attitudes, cognitions, and behaviour among adults in Germany. Major sporting events are characterised by heightened visibility of gambling promotions across television and digital media, which may contribute to the normalisation of gambling, to the initiation or intensification of gambling behaviour as well as the reinforcement of gambling-related cognitive distortions. Data will be collected at three timepoints: before the tournament, during the tournament, and after the tournament. Participants will self-report their exposure to gambling-related content, gambling attitudes and expectancies, gambling-related cognitive distortions, motivation to gamble, gambling behaviour (including initiation, frequency, and spending), and gambling-related problems. The study further examines whether these associations are stronger among individuals with known vulnerability factors for gambling-related harm. The study aims to improve understanding of the associations between gambling-related media exposure during major sporting events and changes in gambling-related cognition and behaviour over time, with potential implications for responsible gambling and advertising policies.

title: Math, Data, and Cognitive Bias: Educating Teens to Make Informed Decisions About Gambling
abstract: This presentation introduces the Gambling Awareness Initiative (GAI), a program designed to educate teens about the risks of sports gambling using data, probability, and cognitive-bias research. While many interventions focus on stories of addiction, GAI emphasizes the math behind gambling and the ways cognitive biases—such as the illusion of control—affect decision-making. Participants will see how simple simulations, coin-flip activities, and expected-value visualizations reveal the true odds and long-term outcomes of gambling. The session demonstrates how applied statistical reasoning can empower teens to recognize and resist harmful gambling behaviors. Implications extend to educators, parents, and community advocates seeking evidence-based approaches to prevention, bridging research and practice in a highly engaging, interactive format.
venue: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)

title: Beyond the Bet: An Updated Scoping Review on Sports Gambling
abstract: ABSTRACT Background: Technological advances and changes in legislation have driven the proliferation of sports betting in recent years. Therefore, understanding who is at risk of sports betting-related consequences and how to mitigate harm is essential. Objectives: The present scoping review aimed to provide an updated examination of the correlates of sports betting and interventions for sports betting. Methods: Articles published between April 2022 and June 2025 were screened, and 60 studies were eligible for inclusion. Results: Most studies explicitly examined or included correlates of sports betting, and a small minority focused on interventions for sports betting. Across studies, sports bettors were most often younger men with higher income and education levels. Psychological factors such as impulsivity, sensation seeking, competitiveness, and cognitive distortions (eg, illusion of control) were consistently associated with more frequent and problematic betting. Social influences, including peer norms, sports fandom, and exposure to advertising, were also linked to engagement and harm. Evidence on interventions remains limited but suggests modest benefits of responsible gambling tools, including precommitment, and safer gambling messages. Conclusions: Overall, findings underscore the need for more targeted approaches to prevent and minimize potential harms associated with sports betting. Contexte: Les progrès technologiques et les changements dans la législation ont favorisé la prolifération des paris sportifs ces dernières années. Il est donc essentiel de comprendre qui est exposé aux conséquences liées aux paris sportifs et comment en atténuer les effets néfastes. Objectifs: La présente revue exploratoire visait à fournir une analyse actualisée des facteurs associés aux paris sportifs et des interventions en la matière. Méthodes: Les articles publiés entre avril 2022 et juin 2025 ont été examinés, et 60 études ont été jugées éligibles pour inclusion. Résultats: La plupart des études examinaient explicitement ou incluaient les corrélats des paris sportifs, et une petite minorité se concentrait sur les interventions en matière de paris sportifs. Dans l’ensemble des études, les parieurs sportifs étaient le plus souvent des hommes jeunes disposant de revenus et d’un niveau d'éducation plus élevés. Des facteurs psychologiques tels que l’impulsivité, la recherche de sensations fortes, la compétitivité et les distorsions cognitives (par exemple, l’illusion de contrôle) étaient systématiquement associés à des paris plus fréquents et problématiques. Les influences sociales, notamment les normes des pairs, le fanatisme sportif et l’exposition à la publicité, étaient également liées à la pratique et aux effets néfastes. Les données sur les interventions restent limitées, mais suggèrent des bénéfices modestes sur les outils de jeu responsable, notamment l’engagement préalable et les messages en faveur d’un jeu plus sûr. Conclusions: Dans l’ensemble, les résultats soulignent la nécessité d’adopter des approches plus ciblées pour prévenir et minimiser les effets néfastes potentiels associés aux paris sportifs.

title: Preventive Interventions for Safer Online Betting: A Systematic Review
abstract: A systematic review and synthesis of scientific literature on preventive interventions for safer online gambling and their effectiveness.

title: PATTERNS AND PREVALENCE OF SPORTS BETTING AMONGST UNDERGRADUATE SPORTS ENTHUSIAST
abstract: Sports betting has transformed from an ancient pastime into a multi-billion-dollar global industry, influencing economies, sports culture, and individual behaviours. This article critically examines the evolution of sports betting, its global and national trends, and its growing prevalence among Nigerian youth, particularly among university students and sports enthusiasts. While the industry generates substantial revenue, supports employment, and enhances sports engagement, it also raises concerns about addiction, financial distress, and regulatory loopholes. The accessibility of online betting platforms, coupled with aggressive marketing and celebrity endorsements, has fuelled increased participation, often at the expense of financial stability and academic performance. Additionally, this paper explores the socioeconomic impact of betting, highlighting how economic hardship and peer influence contribute to widespread gambling behaviours. With Nigeria emerging as a major betting hub in Africa, a strategic balance between economic benefits and social responsibility is crucial. Strengthening regulatory frameworks, promoting financial literacy, and implementing responsible gambling measures are imperative to mitigate associated risks. This article advocates for a holistic approach that safeguards vulnerable populations while ensuring the sustainability of the industry within ethical boundaries.
venue: Journal of the Nigeria Association of Sports Science and Medicine

title: Schema on the Inside: A Two-Phase Fine-Tuning Method for High-Efficiency Text-to-SQL at Scale
abstract: Applying large, proprietary API-based language models to text-to-SQL tasks poses a significant industry challenge: reliance on massive, schema-heavy prompts results in prohibitive per-token API costs and high latency, hindering scalable production deployment. We present a specialized, self-hosted 8B-parameter model designed for a conversational bot in CriQ, a sister app to Dream11, India's largest fantasy sports platform with over 250 million users, that answers user queries about cricket statistics. Our novel two-phase supervised fine-tuning approach enables the model to internalize the entire database schema, eliminating the need for long-context prompts. This reduces input tokens by over 99%, from a 17k-token baseline to fewer than 100, and replaces costly external API calls with efficient local inference. The resulting system achieves 98.4% execution success and 92.5% semantic accuracy, substantially outperforming a prompt-engineered baseline using Google's Gemini Flash 2.0 (95.6% execution, 89.4% semantic accuracy). These results demonstrate a practical path toward high-precision, low-latency text-to-SQL applications using domain-specialized, self-hosted language models in large-scale production environments.
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

title: Apostas on-line e saúde mental em adultos: Revisão crítica da literatura com metanálise exploratória de ansiedade e estresse
abstract: A expansão das plataformas de apostas exige distinguir participação recreativa, gravidade do jogo e sofrimento psicológico. Este artigo analisa a relação entre apostas on-line e saúde mental, com atenção às apostas esportivas, à depressão e ao risco suicida. Realizou-se revisão crítica com busca dirigida no PubMed, na BVS e no Portal de Periódicos CAPES, complementada por textos de periódicos e repositórios. A discussão reuniu 18 estudos primários e sete sínteses científicas. A síntese quantitativa exploratória reuniu dois estudos transversais em adultos, com 6.283 participantes, que informaram correlações de Spearman entre gravidade do jogo on-line e ansiedade ou estresse. Utilizaram-se transformação de Fisher, efeitos aleatórios de DerSimonian–Laird e intervalos conservadores de Hartung–Knapp modificados. As estimativas combinadas foram 0,117 para ansiedade e 0,091 para estresse; os intervalos conservadores incluíram ausência de associação. A heterogeneidade da ansiedade foi elevada, enquanto o resultado de estresse foi dominado pelo estudo maior. Depressão, ideação suicida e comparações entre modalidades foram examinadas narrativamente, por incompatibilidade das medidas. A síntese narrativa sustenta uma crítica à promoção irrestrita das apostas, com efeitos experimentais de incentivos sobre decisões e evidência de danos financeiros. A metanálise não estabelece causalidade ou risco específico de plataformas. Conclui-se pela necessidade de estudos longitudinais brasileiros, medidas por produto e avaliações clínicas que considerem perdas financeiras, controle do comportamento e comorbidades.
venue: Journal of Social Issues and Health Sciences (JSIHS)

title: APOSTAS ESPORTIVAS E A REGULAMENTAÇÃO À LUZ DO CÓDIGO DE DEFESA DO CONSUMIDOR: DESAFIOS, PERSPECTIVAS E IMPACTOS SOCIAIS NO ORDENAMENTO JURÍDICO BRASILEIRO
abstract: Introdução Nas últimas décadas, o avanço tecnológico transformou as relações de consumo, especialmente com a expansão dos serviços digitais. Nesse cenário, cresceram atividades online que envolvem riscos aos usuários, exigindo maior atenção do ordenamento jurídico. A facilidade de acesso às plataformas virtuais e a intensa divulgação nas redes sociais ampliaram o alcance dessas práticas, atingindo um público cada vez mais diverso e vulnerável. Esse contexto demonstra a necessidade de mecanismos eficazes de proteção jurídica, diante da assimetria de informações entre fornecedores e usuários. A publicidade digital, muitas vezes atrativa e persuasiva, pode induzir o consumidor a decisões precipitadas, sem plena compreensão dos riscos. Além disso, a atuação de influenciadores digitais reforça esse cenário, já que seu poder de convencimento impacta diretamente os seguidores, nem sempre observando os deveres de transparência e boa-fé. Diante disso, é essencial analisar como os princípios da responsabilidade civil e da proteção do consumidor podem ser aplicados para garantir equilíbrio nessas relações. A falta de fiscalização efetiva e a dificuldade de responsabilização dos agentes envolvidos contribuem para a insegurança jurídica e para prejuízos financeiros e sociais. Assim, o presente estudo busca examinar a efetividade dos instrumentos jurídicos disponíveis para assegurar a proteção dos consumidores no ambiente digital, diante dos desafios das novas formas de consumo e da crescente influência midiática.Objetivo: Analisar, sob uma perspectiva jurídica e social, a aplicação do Código de Defesa do Consumidor (Lei nº 8.078/1990) nas atividades de apostas esportivas e jogos online, que foram regulamentadas pela Lei nº 14.790/2023, buscando entender como o ordenamento jurídico brasileiro pode assegurar proteção efetiva e ágil aos consumidores diante de práticas abusivas e da influência exercida por plataformas e influenciadores digitais.
venue: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação

title: Critical financial education: a mathematical study on investmentsand games of chance as an instrument for awareness and citizenship inbasic education
abstract: Based on the incorporation of Financial Education as a curricular component within the basic education curriculum in the state of Paraná, as well as the significant growth of online betting and electronic gaming platforms in Brazil, this study aims to address the mathematical and probabilistic aspects of financial investments, presenting basic concepts related to real financial applications alongside those termed here as illusory investments, which have contributed to the rising indebtedness of a significant portion of the Brazilian population, compromising household income and elevating the risks associated with gambling addiction. As an educational product, we present a didactic proposal involving an online platform that encompasses three illusory investments and mathematically demonstrates their disadvantages. Through this approach, we hope to contribute to the development of critical and logical-mathematical thinking among Basic Education students regarding games of chance and electronic betting, thereby fostering greater awareness regarding promotional materials for illusory investments.
venue: Institutional Repository of the Federal Technological University of Paraná (RIUT) (Federal University of Technology – Paraná)

title: Direito, tecnologia da informação e acesso à justiça no contexto esportivo
abstract: À medida que as apostas esportivas de quota fixas entram no Brasil, o assunto continua interessante; no entanto, a regulamentação das apostas esportivas foi além de uma questão econômica e fiscal restrita, transformando-se em uma conversa mais ampla sobre questões de autenticidade esportiva, conformidade e combate à lavagem de dinheiro (AML). Este artigo destaca os desafios de responsabilidade regulatória e legal que acompanham a digitalização, agravados pelas vulnerabilidades dos atores esportivos. Este estudo fornece, subsequentemente, uma visão sobre a interação entre Direito, Tecnologia da Informação e Acesso à Justiça no ambiente esportivo. Argumenta que a implementação da integridade e a contenção da atividade criminosa, apoiadas por tecnologias de monitoramento, constituem os mecanismos decisivos que garantem a segurança jurídica e o acesso à justiça esportiva. Identifica a legislação a ser seguida, estratégias de conformidade e vulnerabilidades do sistema, como deficiências de governança e a possibilidade de o pessoal esportivo ser atraído para manipulação de resultados, e propõe a elaboração de uma política regulatória que alcance um equilíbrio entre contabilizar o ganho financeiro de tal atividade e preservar a moralidade e lealdade esportiva.
