title: Kodex zum Umgang mit der Industrie, die abhängigkeitserzeugende Produkte vertreibt (z. B. Alkohol, Cannabis, Tabak, nicht pharmazeutische Nikotinprodukte, Glücksspiele, Sportwetten)
abstract: Zusammenfassung: Hintergrund: Industrien, deren Geschäftsmodell auf der Vermarktung abhängig machender oder gesundheitsschädlicher Produkte beruht, beeinflussen Forschung, Evidenzbildung und Gesundheitspolitik. Dazu zählen Tabak- und Nikotinindustrie, Alkohol- und Cannabisunternehmen sowie Glücksspiel- und Sportwettenanbieter, deren Strategien von industriefinanzierter Forschung über Sponsoring bis zu PR-Kampagnen und Lobbying reichen. Die vorliegenden Daten zeigen, dass dadurch systematische Interessenkonflikte entstehen, die wissenschaftliche Integrität und Glaubwürdigkeit gefährden. Position: Das Positionspapier formuliert einen Kodex für wissenschaftliche Fachgesellschaften im Umgang mit diesen Industrien. Es fordert die grundsätzliche Ablehnung von Geld- und Sachzuwendungen sowie wechselseitigen Gegenleistungen, die Vermeidung von Kooperationen mit industriegestützten Personen und Organisationen und eine konsequente Offenlegung aller relevanten finanziellen und nicht-finanziellen Interessenkonflikte der vergangenen fünf Jahre. Ausgenommen sind gesetzlich oder regulatorisch vorgeschriebene klinische Prüfungen unter Bedingungen strenger Transparenz, unabhängiger Governance und uneingeschränkter Publikationsrechte. Ziel ist es, Unabhängigkeit, Qualität und Vertrauenswürdigkeit der Suchtforschung zu sichern und den Einfluss kommerzieller Interessen auf Forschung, Lehre und gesundheitspolitische Empfehlungen wirksam zu begrenzen.
venue: SUCHT - Zeitschrift für Wissenschaft und Praxis / Journal of Addiction Research and Practice

title: Betting on Belief: How perceptions of increasing sport wagering shape fan trust in game
abstract: The increased availability of legalized sport wagering across the United States has transformed the modern sport industry, redefining fan engagement practices. As betting partnerships, in-game odds integration, and gambling media content become increasingly embedded in sport broadcasts, understanding how fans interpret these changes is critical. This study examines how fans perceive the rise of sport wagering and how their perceptions influence their views of sport efficacy (i.e., integrity, authenticity, fairness, etc.). Participants will include adult sport fans, 18 or older, recruited through Murray State athletic events. Individuals recruited will be asked to voluntarily answer a four-section survey along with demographic questions. The first section will include the Sport Fandom Questionnaire (Wann, 2001), a five-item measure assessing the level of sport fandom. The next scale will be the five-item Fan Dysfunction Scale (Wakefield & Wann, 2006), designed to assess the degree to which fans are confrontational. The third scale will be the seven-item Sport Spectator Identification Scale – Revised (James, Delia, & Wann, 2019), completed to assess the level of identification with a favorite sport team. In the fourth and final section, the participants will be asked to complete a 6-item scale, assessing the level of an individual’s trust in sport following the increased availability of sport wagering.
venue: Murray State's Digital Commons (Murray State University)

title: Betting on Performance: Sports Betting Legalization and NBA Player Performance Relative to Sportsbook Expectations
abstract: This paper presents some of the first empirical work examining how the legality of sports betting markets affects the relationship between player performance and sportsbook expectations and adds to a small but growing body of research on how legal sports betting changes player behavior. To achieve this, this paper evaluates the effect legalization of mobile sports betting has on NBA player performance relative to prominent sportsbook proposition line (or “prop line”) expectations. To determine that effect and assess whether these betting expectations impact player behaviors, a player-game level dataset is used that links FanDuel closing over/under lines to real game data for 178 NBA players across five different statistical categories. The dataset spans three distinct player positions (center, guard and forward) and covers games from the 2022 to the 2025 seasons. Using a difference-in-differences model, and exploiting staggered state-level legalization timing, the results show that players in legal markets deviate more from their prop line expectations, though not in any consistent direction. The primary outcome was the absolute value of the deviation between game performance and the FanDuel closing line (AbsDev). StatDiff measured the directional difference between real game performance and the closing line. Betting legality was associated with a statistically significant increase in AbsDev across three main specifications (beta range 0.266-0.396, all p < 0.05). Player performance in legalized markets deviated further from applicable prop lines in both directions without a consistent directional bias. This effect was most pronounced in the points market (beta = 0.665, p = 0.020), specifically with centers and forwards. For example, Dennis Schroder, who was traded to five different teams from 2022-2025 in markets that both offered and did not offer legalized betting, provides additional evidence and support for the conclusions in this paper.

title: Does the consideration of market prices in model selection increase model profitability? Evidence from theory, artificial data and real-world data
abstract: It is well-acknowledged in the literature that besides accuracy, profitability (i.e. the economic value) of a forecast is crucial in domains including economics, energy, weather or sports forecasting. The present study argues that selection of profitable forecasting models benefits from consideration of market prices in-sample (i.e. when optimizing model parameters on training data). Such models can be specifically optimised for profitability instead of accuracy, as most commonly done so far. Previous literature suggests that, under specific circumstances, accuracy- and profitability-optimisation leads to equal model selection. We theoretically show that this result is contingent upon strict assumptions and does not hold anymore if relaxing any of these assumptions. Moreover, we present evidence that out-of-sample profitability (i.e. returns generated on unseen data) are actually increased for profitability-optimised models compared to accuracy-optimised models based on artificial and real-world data from the domain of sports betting. This result is explained by the ability of profitability-optimised models to implicitly detect and counter an existing market bias, provided that the model family allows to capture such biases. The present study intends to stimulate discussion on optimal model selection for profitable forecasting and to encourage researchers to consider profitability-optimisation in forecasting applications to real-world data.

title: Forecasting the Winner of a Live Tennis Match
abstract: With the rise of live sports betting in recent years, tennis forecasting has expanded from pre-match prediction to models that update win probabilities as a match unfolds. A central challenge in creating such a model is the constant need for models to adapt to score and performance changes. This study examines how pre-match and live information can be most effectively integrated into a model to produce accurate win-probability estimates. The analysis uses 8,222 Grand Slam matches containing a total of 1,505,355 points. Five models were evaluated using a chronological split, with matches from 2011-2021 used for training, 2022 for validation, and 2023-2024 for testing. Trace, a hybrid model, achieved accuracies of 76.06%, 82.15%, and 88.34% at 25%, 50%, and 75% match progress, suggesting that hybrid modeling is a practical approach to live tennis forecasting.

title: Classification-Behavior Discordance and Problem Gambling: Differential Patterns for Fantasy Sports and Loot Boxes Among College Students.
abstract: Fantasy sports and loot boxes share similarities with gambling yet remain largely unregulated as such, creating ambiguity in how individuals perceive and engage with these activities. While participation in both activities has been linked to problem gambling, whether individuals' classification of these activities as gambling is associated with differential risk has not been examined. This study introduces the concept of classification-behavior discordance, defined as the misalignment between how an individual classifies an activity and whether they participate in it. Using data from an online survey of 4,016 college students enrolled at public colleges and universities in Nevada, United States, we constructed four discordance groups for each activity based on the intersection of classification and participation: non-participants, aware participants, unaware participants, and non-participating classifiers. We conducted separate binary logistic regression models for fantasy sports and loot boxes to examine associations between discordance group membership and problem gambling. Results revealed divergent patterns across activities. For loot boxes, classifying the activity as gambling was associated with significantly elevated problem gambling risk among participants, whereas for fantasy sports, participating without classifying the activity as gambling was associated with significantly lower risk. These findings highlight the importance of considering individuals' subjective classification of gambling-like activities in problem gambling screening, prevention, and regulatory efforts.

title: Religiosity and Online Gambling Addiction: A Serial Mediation Model of Perceived Social Support and Life Satisfaction within the Framework of Conservation of Resources Theory
The Impact of NBA-Related Signals and Market Factors on the Short-Term Price Movement of DKNG Stock
abstract: This study investigates whether NBA-related signals and basic market factors can help predict the short-term behavior of DraftKings (DKNG), a major U.S. sports betting company whose business activity is closely tied to NBA games. Using daily price data, market benchmarks, technical indicators, and selected game-intensity variables, the study builds predictive models for two tasks: next-day return direction classification and next-day volatility regression. Three machine learning models—Ridge, Random Forest, and XGBoost—were trained and evaluated using time-ordered rolling validation. Results show that non-linear models significantly outperform linear baselines. Direction prediction improves only modestly, but calibration scores become more reliable. Volatility prediction shows stronger improvement, especially with technical indicators. The findings suggest that combining market information with NBA-related signals provides meaningful predictive power, especially during high-attention game periods. This work offers a foundation for future research incorporating higher-frequency betting data, injury reports, and sentiment indicators. Such extensions could enhance understanding of how sports-event dynamics interact with financial market behavior in real time.

title: Responsibility and Liability in Autonomous Vehicle Accidents
abstract: As algorithms get more advanced, they can take over and optimize human activities such as driving and sports betting. My capstone focuses on how algorithms and different data modalities can affect outcomes and accuracy in sports betting, while my STS project investigates how humans and an algorithmic system can share responsibility in case of an accident. In my technical capstone, I researched the impact that different datasets have on an algorithm’s accuracy. With the topic of NBA sports betting, I found three data modalities to train my algorithms on. The first was statistical data from box scores of games. The second combined the basic statistical data with spatial movement data from Sport VU. SportVU was a tracking system that the NBA implemented, where cameras all over the courts captured all the positions of the players and the ball at 25 frames per second. The third data was statistical data combined with textual data via a play-by-play commentary of the game. By training the same model on these three different types of data, I was able to analyze the importance of data and how it impacted the results of the model. While machine learning algorithms and models may produce better results on paper, it can be hard to trust them, as you can’t tell what factors the model considered and what it viewed as important. This leads to my STS project, where I analyzed how responsibility and liability should be distributed in cases of accidents occurring with autonomous vehicles (AV). As AVs get more prevalent in today’s society, it becomes important to have a fair framework to delegate responsibility when accidents will inevitably occur. To thoroughly examine this issue, I used current law regulations, a sociological framework via Actor Network Theory, and the consequentialist ethical framework. By using these three types of analysis, I was able to get to the root of the problem and not only determine all actors within this complex system of humans and computers, but also who/what is in control of the vehicle. This led to a more deterministic approach in deciding responsibility in AV accidents. Both of these topics have led me to realize how much computers and algorithms play a role in our lives. While autonomous driving and sports betting seem unrelated, they both heavily depend on computer analysis. This shows how much we currently rely on computers/algorithms and whether we should continue to rely this heavily on them.

title: How sports betting is changing the way people watch sports
Experimental Assortments for Choice Estimation and Nest Identification
abstract: What assortments (subsets of items) should be offered, to collect data for estimating a choice model over $n$ total items? We propose a structured, non-adaptive experiment design requiring only $O(\log n)$ distinct assortments, each offered repeatedly, that consistently outperforms randomized and other heuristic designs across an extensive numerical benchmark that estimates multiple different choice models under a variety of (possibly mis-specified) ground truths. We then focus on Nested Logit choice models, which cluster items into "nests" of close substitutes. Whereas existing Nested Logit estimation procedures assume the nests to be known and fixed, we present a new algorithm to identify nests based on collected data, which when used in conjunction with our experiment design, guarantees correct identification of nests under any Nested Logit ground truth. Our experiment design was deployed to collect data from over 70 million users at Dream11, an Indian fantasy sports platform that offers different types of betting contests, with rich substitution patterns between them. We identify nests based on the collected data, which lead to better out-of-sample choice prediction than ex-ante clustering from contest features. Our identified nests are ex-post justifiable to Dream11 management.

title: Scale development: betting in sport
abstract: Scale development is widely used for systematically measuring individuals’ attitudes and behaviors. Scale development focuses on constructing psychometric instruments that ensure valid and reliable measurement of specific constructs. This chapter details the scale development procedure, followed by a case study demonstrating its application in identifying the motivations behind sports betting. Sports betting is considered a motivated behavior, and understanding the underlying drivers behind this behavior is crucial for sports management. The case study focuses on developing a valid and reliable measurement tool to assess how sports betting motivations influence consumer engagement and industry practices. As a result of the survey, seven core motivational dimensions emerged from the data analysis: Make Money, Fun, Socialization, Recreation-Escape, Knowledge of the Game, Interest in Sports, and Being in the Game. These findings provide valuable insights into the broader implications of sports betting motivations for stakeholders in sports management. The developed scale offers practical applications for industry professionals, regulatory bodies, and researchers, supporting the design of responsible gambling policies and effective consumer engagement strategies. The chapter concludes with recommendations for future research, emphasizing the potential for extending the scale's application to diverse populations and settings and further examining its impact on sports-related consumer behavior.

title: Stressful Life Events, Masculinity and Gambling Participation: An Age-Stratified Analysis of Australian Men
abstract: Gambling participation varies across genders and throughout the life course, yet little research has examined how stressful life events and masculinity-related factors influence gambling behaviour across different stages of adulthood among men. Using Wave 4 data from Ten to Men: The Australian Longitudinal Study on Male Health (n = 5,434), this study investigates age-stratified associations between stressful life events, self-perceived masculinity, masculinity strain and gambling frequency among Australian men. Negative binomial regression analysis reveals that masculinity and masculinity strain predict higher gambling frequency only among young men, highlighting the salience of masculine identity during early adulthood. Stressful life events also showed age-specific effects: job loss is associated with lower frequency of gambling among young men, while bereavement of loved ones is linked to higher gambling among middle-aged men. No stressful life events correlated with gambling among older men. Across all age groups, higher income was associated with more frequent gambling, while possessing a university degree was associated with less frequent gambling among those aged 30 and above only. These findings accentuate the importance of a life course perspective for understanding gambling participation and informing age-tailored interventions.

title: MLB Cross-Venue Matched Book (Polymarket × Kalshi) — Sample
abstract: Polymarket and Kalshi prices for the same MLB game, aligned tick-for-tick on one timeline, with the eventual winner labeled on every row. One settled game (Arizona Diamondbacks @ Minnesota Twins, 2026-06-21); the two venues tracked each other to under one cent through the Twins' comeback win. Neither venue sells its historical order book and it cannot be reconstructed after the fact. Polymarket runs one outcome per binary market (the other side is the exact complement, 1 − poly_mid); prices are book midpoints; ~30–60s granularity; settlement is Kalshi's finalized resolution. See README/SCHEMA for the full reference. The complete multi-day archive and more prediction-market datasets are at zenhodl.net/products.

title: O Novo Jogo dos Negócios: SAF, Apostas e Transformações no Futebol
abstract: O presente resumo analisa a metamorfose estrutural do futebol brasileiro a partir da transição do modelo associativo tradicional para um ecossistema complexo de entretenimento e negócios, fundamentando-se nas perspectivas de Evandro Ferreira Gomes sobre a implementação das Sociedades Anônimas do Futebol (SAFs) e a ascensão das casas de apostas. A discussão central demonstra que a adoção da SAF surge como uma resposta necessária ao endividamento histórico dos clubes, embora carregue o risco de uma financeirização excessiva que pode transformar as instituições em ativos meramente especulativos, distanciando investidores da identidade cultural das torcidas. Paralelamente, o estudo aborda a onipresença das empresas de apostas esportivas, destacando que, apesar do aporte financeiro vital para a competitividade técnica, essa dependência gera desafios éticos significativos, como o perigo da manipulação de resultados e os impactos sociais da ludopatia, fatores que colocam em risco a credibilidade e a integridade do esporte. O texto também ressalta o avanço na profissionalização da gestão e do marketing esportivo nos últimos quinze anos, enfatizando a importância da governança corporativa e da diversidade, com destaque para a crescente participação feminina em cargos diretivos. Por fim, argumenta-se que espaços de debate e inovação são essenciais para transformar o país em um polo de inteligência em gestão, concluindo que a sustentabilidade do futebol na era da economia criativa depende do equilíbrio rigoroso entre a busca pela rentabilidade financeira e a preservação da confiança do público e da ética esportiva.

title: O Novo Jogo dos Negócios: SAF, Apostas e Transformações no Futebol
abstract: Esta resenha científica analisa as transformações contemporâneas no cenário do futebol brasileiro, fundamentando-se nas discussões promovidas pelo especialista Evandro Ferreira Gomes em entrevista concedida ao canal O Marketeiro, sob a curadoria de Luiz Cláudio Zenoni. O estudo debruça-se sobre a transição do esporte de um modelo puramente associativo para um complexo ecossistema de entretenimento e negócios, balizado pela implementação das Sociedades Anônimas do Futebol (SAFs) e pela onipresença das casas de apostas esportivas, as chamadas "bets". A análise busca compreender como a profissionalização da gestão e o influxo de novos capitais reconfiguram o marketing, a ética e a sustentabilidade financeira das instituições esportivas no Brasil.

title: Guest editorial: Fundamentals of case study research for sport marketing studies
abstract: Case study research is an important method to investigate social phenomena, which has attracted increasing attention in marketing research, but its implementation still faces challenges, mainly from misunderstandings of definition and methodological rigor. Early studies regarded case studies as unique events that could not produce universal laws, and confused them with ethnography, field research and teaching case development, leading to the criticism of being descriptive, qualitative and lacking rigor. In recent decades, with the application of grounded theory, optimization of qualitative data analysis and multi-perspective triangulation, the scientificity and rigor of case study research have been significantly improved (Eisenhardt, 1989).A case study is defined as an empirical study that deeply investigates contemporary phenomena in real contexts, especially when the boundary between phenomena and contexts is blurred (Yin, 2017). On the one hand, it adopts inductive logic to build theory, collecting qualitative data through interviews, document analysis and observation to derive new hypotheses; on the other hand, it is good at answering “how” and “why” questions, focusing on complex problems that are difficult to define and observe, and presenting vivid research scenarios. Compared with experiments and questionnaire surveys, case studies have higher applicability in natural environments with less variable control.Case studies are divided into single-case and multiple-case designs, as well as comparative and embedded case studies. Single-case studies are selected for their extremity, revelatory nature or subversion to existing theories (Eisenhardt and Graebner, 2007; Yin, 2017), supporting in-depth exploration (Mao and Chen, 2017), but have limited generalizability. Multiple-case studies follow the principle of replication, and the conclusions are more universal and robust (Yin, 2017). Comparative studies select contrasting cases, while embedded studies set sub-cases in the main case for multi-level analysis.The core advantage of case study is the inductive exploration of real and interesting questions, and high-quality case studies are recognized as the most valuable research (Bluhm et al., 2011; Eisenhardt et al., 2016; Gibbert et al., 2008; Gibbert and Ruigrok, 2010). This feature of ‘telling stories scientifically” has important value for sport marketing with complex practical topics.With global economic development and rising quality of life, the value and economic functions of sport have been increasingly recognized (Zhang et al., 2016). The sport industry is becoming a mainstream sector with growth potential, and areas like professional sport operations, event marketing, venue management, fitness club promotions, and digital sports evolve rapidly. Coupled with globalization and technological advancement, the complexity and uniqueness of sport marketing stand out, and many practical problems cannot be fully explained by universal marketing models, providing opportunities for case study research. Drawing on Mao and Chen (2017), three types of research questions are suitable for case study research in sport marketing.Case study research is first and foremost suitable for exploring new research questions where established theories are lacking or theoretical gaps exist. This category represents the main area where case study research in sport marketing is concentrated. The goal is theory building (Eisenhardt, 1989) based on inductive logic to explain “how” and “why” questions. Researchers do not predefine relationships between constructs and theory; instead, hypotheses emerge from multi-source qualitative data. For instance, Kellett and Russell (2009) conducted a case study on skateboarding clusters, offering insights for the extreme sport industry. Tripodi et al. (2009) examined sponsors’ exploitation strategies and ambush marketing during the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games. Recent case studies have examined the sustainability of major events (Jiang et al., 2026), legacy utilization (Park et al., 2020), smart sport venues (Wang and Li, 2025), smart sport communities (Chen et al., 2025), and digital sport digital marketing (Wang et al., 2025).Case study research is also well-suited for exploring complex sport marketing and operation problems, building process theories, or investigating questions with hard-to-measure constructs. This methodological approach enables researchers to delve deeply into marketing operations as they unfold over time. For instance, the analytical framework from the Bradford studies has been applied to analyze decision-making processes surrounding potential mergers between university athletic associations. Questionnaire surveys cannot capture stakeholder behavioral patterns in such contexts. Similar studies have analyzed strategic failures in developing community sports (Morrison and Misener, 2022), examined the EU's role in global sport regulations (García and Meier, 2017), and conducted longitudinal analysis of strategic decision-making in professional clubs (Marthinus et al., 2025), revealing dynamic mechanisms of developing strategies. These case studies are highly suitable when newly proposed constructs lack valid measurement scales.A third area where case study research excels is in addressing research questions that require in-depth investigation of extreme phenomena. For example, research on elite sport systems has often neglected small countries, leading to an analysis of extreme contexts like Greenland (Storm et al., 2023). A longitudinal single-case study on the Essendon Football Club focused on doping scandals (Halabi and O'Connell, 2021), providing rare empirical insights into sport operations during crises. Kellison (2021) examined a stadium development project in suburban Atlanta, exploring public attention. Extreme competitive pressure's impact on athlete performance has been studied through analysis of the Norwegian ski jumping team during the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics (Kristiansen et al., 2023), offering insights into athlete psychological support and organizational communication. Such studies feature small sample sizes and limited reproducibility, but in-depth case analysis fosters resonance and understanding of these issues.Theoretical contribution stands as a core prerequisite for high-quality case study research (Pratt, 2008). As a methodological approach centered on theory development, case study research within sport marketing generates substantive scholarly value across theory building, theory testing, and theory transformation. A primary theoretical contribution lies in inductive theory building, a function widely recognized as central to the methodological value of qualitative case inquiry (Colquitt and Zapata-Phelan, 2011). This pathway focuses on addressing critical theoretical gaps and constructing novel theoretical frameworks to explain phenomena that existing marketing and management theories fail to adequately interpret. For novel formats and emerging trends in the sport industry that existing theories cannot adequately explain, case study research can identify key variables, clarify pathways of influence, and inductively derive new constructs and relationships among them through exploratory analysis. Final research outputs are typically formalized as testable theoretical propositions or distinct new conceptual constructs (Fisher and Aguinis, 2017). For instance, Pegoraro (2010) conducted an exploratory case study on athletes' social media use on Twitter and proposed an initial classification framework for athletes' social media communication, representing one of the early foundational contributions to research on athlete social media. Schulenkorf (2012) developed the Sport for Development and Peace Project Framework based on a comparative case analysis of multiple sport-for-development projects in the Asia–Pacific region, providing testable theoretical propositions for subsequent research on sport for social development. More recently, Banucha and Bielawa (2025) conducted an in-depth case study of top Polish basketball clubs and proposed the new construct of “goal alignment,” which suggests that aligning athletes' individual goals with team goals can significantly improve commitment and performance.Beyond novel theory construction, case study research also advances sport marketing scholarship through rigorous theory testing and incremental extension of existing theoretical frameworks (Colquitt and Zapata-Phelan, 2011). In this capacity, researchers design case studies, collect empirical data, and conduct systematic analysis based on established theories or conceptual models that offer partial explanatory power for target phenomena. Core objectives include validating construct relationships, testing the applicability of classic management theories in sport settings, expanding the theoretical application boundaries of existing theories, refining theoretical dimensions to enhance contextual fit for sport marketing dynamics, and reducing cross-context theoretical incompatibility. For instance, Mason et al. (2006) conducted a case study on marketing and communications associated with corruption issues that emerged during the IOC's Olympic bidding process, introducing classic principal-agent theory into research on the marketing and operation of non-profit international sport organizations and extending the application boundary of this theory in sport. Batuev and Robinson (2017) performed a cross-case study on the evolution of freestyle sports including snowboarding, skateboarding, and rock climbing, and constructed an analytical framework based primarily on neo-institutional theory supplemented by resource dependence theory, providing important theoretical insights for understanding the promotion and institutionalization of emerging sports. Miller (2026) used LeBron James's “The Decision” event as a teaching case to guide students in applying stakeholder theory to analyze how this decision would affect James's brand value, revealing the applicability of stakeholder theory in the context of athlete personal brand management.A final key contribution of case study research in sport marketing is embodied in theory transformation, which centers on bridging the translational gap between abstract theory and industry practice. Unlike research focused purely on theoretical construction, theoretical propositions derived from case study research originate from real-world sport marketing and operational contexts. This not only provides targeted guidance for decision-making in operating sport enterprises but also makes theoretical outcomes more easily accepted by industry practice. This stream of research places less emphasis on pure theory building and more on providing actionable guidance from a decision-making, consultation and marketing implications perspective. For example, in the field of elite athlete development, Berg et al. (2018) conducted a historical case study of the 1968 US Olympic delegation, analyzed the development pathways of elite athletes in different historical periods, and offered decision-making references for sport organizations to formulate long-term athlete development and promotional strategies. In the field of sport policy implementation, MacPherson and Moss (2025) performed a case study on the development and implementation of the Safe Sport Framework by Gymnastics Canada, translating the latest research findings into actionable practices and providing a referential model for sport managers. Baker and Gardner (2026) examined the complex decision-making dilemmas faced by USA Fencing in developing its national competition schedules and revealed how sport event managers should balance the demands of different stakeholders under such circumstances.From the perspective of theoretical contributions, whether providing new perspectives (Graebner, 2009), filling research gaps (Smith, 2014), resolving contradictions (Haveman, 1992), extending theoretical boundaries (Backhouse et al., 2006), or gaining new insights (Siggelkow, 2007), the case study's potential has been widely recognized. Of course, theoretical contributions require specific methods and strategies in case study design, including literature review, problem formulation, research design, theoretical sampling, data collection, data analysis, and writing (Eisenhardt, 2016).At present, no unified universal standard governs the design framework for case study research, though the process can generally be structured into a coherent, sequential workflow encompassing four core phases. The initial phase centers on problem formulation and data collection, during which researchers adopt an open, exploratory stance free from pre-determined assumptions. Facts and contextual details are gathered via a diverse range of data sources, including documents, archives, interviews, and observations. The entire process should be documented. Interviewing is the most common data collection method; questions should be open-ended to help generate research questions. This stage addresses how the case proceeds and why.Following the initial data collection phase, the research proceeds to a stage focused on analytical breakthroughs and rigorous data interpretation. Researchers systematically collect and analyze multi-source data to identify key elements. Data collection is saturated when further data gathering fails to yield new insights, analytical dimensions, or interpretive value. Core components of this analytical phase include narrative development, construct measurement, pattern identification, theory construction, and dialogue with existing literature. Recently, methods including econometric approaches, machine learning, and generative AI have been integrated into case study research. Regardless of method, high-quality case study research conveys value through vivid stories while forming a closed chain of evidence, building theory through iteration and comparison with existing literature.The subsequent phase focuses on the formal drafting and composition of the research manuscript, a step that directly reflects the researcher's scientific rigor and academic writing proficiency. Data findings and theoretical frameworks should be presented clearly through well-designed figures and tables, with logical conceptual models strongly recommended to visualize and clarify relationships between key theoretical constructs. When articulating core research propositions, researchers must conduct sufficient dialogue with existing literature to highlight theoretical contributions.The final phase of the process involves research verification and refinement. In this stage, researchers seek targeted feedback and solicit revision suggestions from key case informants and strengthen the discussion section to emphasize practical value. It is worth noting that alternative stage classifications exist within scholarly literature; for instance, some scholars have condensed the case study process into three overarching phases, including preparation, implementation, and dialogue (Chen and Liu, 2010). Researchers should develop comprehensive proposals including title, background, questions, theoretical foundation, design, methods, and references, particularly justifying case selection.To further elaborate the content of case study research, this study selects illustrative cases for concise analysis based on the combination of typicality and appropriateness. Anderski et al. (2024) analyzed athlete brands' role in international marketing of professional sports leagues, using the German Bundesliga's Asian market practices as a single case study. The research addressed two questions: athlete brands' current role and potential in international marketing, and their co-creation pathways toward league brand meaning. For case selection, the Bundesliga's uniqueness in terms of fan majority ownership, emphasis on local youth development, and high stadium attendance distinguishes its brand ecosystem, making it ideal for exploring athlete brands' role in marketing. The league's active expansion into the Asian market adds contextual relevance.The study employed semi-structured interviews with 17 stakeholders including Bundesliga executives, club managers, and broadcast media executives in Asian markets. Inductive thematic analysis across six phases integrated 40 codes through open coding. Following triangulation, theme refinement, and peer review, four themes emerged: athlete brands' international marketing role, league brand meaning co-creation pathways, brand co-creation prerequisites, and influence mechanisms within the brand ecosystem. Theoretically, it supplements understanding of athlete brands within sports brand ecosystems and refines co-creation pathways in cross-cultural contexts; methodologically, it demonstrates standardized application of interviews and thematic analysis; practically, it highlights risks of athlete brands in international marketing.Complementing this, our research team developed a case study protocol on the ATP Shanghai Masters 1000's localized development strategy in China. This longitudinal single case enables tracing the event's evolutionary trajectory over time. Following Yin's (2016) framework, we defined core parameters including research tasks, target groups, questions, and interviewee information. Supporting materials included checklist-based data collection, literature synthesis, and jointly refined interview questions, laying a foundation for subsequent data collection and analysis.As the lead article of this special issue on case-based research in sport marketing, this paper offers a foundational overview of case study methodology for diverse readers. Drawing on scholarly works and representative studies, it presents core definitions and classifications, reveals theoretical value and applicable characteristics, and provides intuitive explanations through typical examples.Admittedly, this paper lacks the detail required for a comprehensive step-by-step guide to rigorous case study research. Nevertheless, we hope this special issue stimulates innovative engagement with case study research in sport marketing and encourages more researchers to adopt this approach.We strongly encourage developing high-quality teaching cases tailored to sport marketing. The Harvard Case Library features rigorous sport-related cases, including Paris Saint-Germain: Building One of the World's Top Sports Brands, FC Barcelona: More Than a Club, More Than Data, Decathlon: Making Sports Accessible to All, Fantasy Sports: A Game of Skill or Chance, John Hancock Sports Sponsorship: 1993–2000 and Beyond, and Negotiating with Data: Analytics FC. These benchmark cases would greatly benefit sport marketing education and business decision-making.
venue: International Journal of Sports Marketing and Sponsorship

title: Shared and Distinct Neural Signatures of Cue-Induced Response in Substance and Behavioral Addictions: A Coordinate-Based Neuroimaging Meta-Analysis
abstract: Abstract As the global burden of addiction intensifies, the neurobiological commonalities and distinctions between substance use disorders (SUDs) and behavioral addictions (BAs) remain poorly characterized. This coordinate-based meta-analysis of 59 fMRI articles (n = 2,951) mapped the neural signatures of visual cue-reactivity across the addictive disorders. Our results revealed a universal core network shared by SUDs and BAs centered in the bilateral opercular inferior frontal gyrus, suggesting a shared disruption in inhibitory control. Distinctively, SUDs exhibited a stronger recruitment of a subcortical salience pathway, with greater involvement of the left thalamus ventral anterior nucleus than BAs, potentially reflecting pharmacologically amplified bottom-up salience attribution. Notably, recovery-related patterns diverged in the left medial superior frontal gyrus. Alcohol use disorder was associated with neural restoration, whereas heroin use disorder showed neural decompensation. These neural signatures establish a rigorous neurobiological basis for differentiating substance and behavioral phenotypes, supporting tailored circuit-based precision treatments.

title: Community Perspectives of MA Higher Education Students on their Exposure to and Participation in Sports Betting through Paid Media Advertising
abstract: The introduction of legal sports betting to Massachusetts is anticipated to impose social, health, and educational impacts on higher education students (aged 18-25) in Massachusetts, particularly regarding their exposure to and participation in sports betting through paid media advertising (Vander Linden et al., 2022). Funded by the Massachusetts Gaming Commission, we used a community-engaged research approach to bring together a diverse, engaged student group from various higher education institutions in Massachusetts to form a community research team (CRT), who took the lead in exploring relevant issues in a multi-year research project. The specific research questions were developed by the CRT upon participating in a series of workshops with industry and community stakeholders. The CRT utilized journey mapping techniques, informed by a set of innovative methodologies that involve reflection journals, in-depth interviews, and auto-ethnography during primary sports events conducted by community members. This multi-method approach allow the investigators and the CRT to develop understanding about how college students experience, and are impacted by, paid sports betting advertising in Massachusetts, build community awareness about the practice and its impact, and inform community-minded interventions designed to encourage positive play, and reduce problematic sports betting behaviors.
venue: Digital Scholarship - UNLV (University of Nevada Reno)

title: Replication package for "The Manager of the Month Curse: Recognition Effects or Regression to the Mean in the English Premier League?"
abstract: Analysis code, manuscript and appendix files, generated tables and figures, frozen analysis plan, source manifest, data-quality report, and project-authored correction ledgers for a study of 295 Premier League Manager of the Month awards linked to match results, betting odds, expected goals, Elo ratings, and announcement dates. Third-party raw snapshots are not redistributed where their terms do not clearly permit republication; the package records source URLs, access dates, terms, filenames, and SHA-256 hashes for audit and reacquisition.

title: Compressed Beliefs
abstract: Subjective beliefs are central to economic inference, and incentive-compatible belief elicitation mechanisms are widely assumed to identify these latent objects. This paper shows that elicited belief reports causally depend on an uninformative cognitive default induced by the elicitation design. From the lab to sports betting to official inflation expectations, reported beliefs are highly malleable, even under theoretically and behaviorally compatible incentives. I propose experimentally varying the cognitive default during belief elicitation. This exogenous variation allows the construction of inferred beliefs that are stable across elicitation designs and empirically outperform incentivized reports in predicting realized outcomes and participants’ own behavior.

title: You Bet?! - A cross-cultural content analysis of sports betting advertising during a crisis
abstract: This thesis examines how sports betting operators adapted their advertising communication during the disruption of live sport caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. It investigates whether communication strategies, thematic content, and emotional appeals differed across selected national contexts: the United States, Ireland, and the United Kingdom. Drawing on Hall’s high- and low-context communication theory and Taylor’s Six-Segment Message Strategy Wheel, the study applies a qualitative cross-cultural content analysis to 15 sports betting advertisements broadcast or distributed during the pandemic period. The advertisements were analysed using a deductive coding framework covering explicit informational appeals, implicit and relational appeals, emotional strategies, and regulatory elements, while allowing crisis-specific themes to emerge inductively. The findings indicate distinct patterns within the selected sample. Advertisements from the United States predominantly relied on explicit financial incentives, technological convenience, and efficiency-oriented messaging. Irish advertisements more frequently employed shared social references, humour, and ironic representations of lockdown experiences. UK advertisements combined emotional and socially contextualised messaging during the sports shutdown with more transactional appeals as live sport returned. These patterns suggest that crisis advertising in sports betting was not uniform across the examined markets, but reflected the interaction of communicative context, market conditions, and the changing availability of sport. The study contributes to research on cross-cultural advertising and gambling marketing by applying established communication frameworks to a crisis setting. Given the small purposive sample and focus on broadcast-style video advertising, the findings are analytically informative rather than statistically generalisable.
venue: University Library Linz repository (Johannes Kepler Universitat Linz)

title: GAMBLING INVOLVEMENT, HOPELESSNESS, AND SUICIDE-RELATED INDICATORS IN TURKİYE: A CROSS-SECTIONAL ONLINE SURVEY
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective: We aimed to estimate gambling participation and positive screening for probable gambling disorder and to examine their associations with hopelessness and suicide-related outcomes in a Turkish online sample. Methods: In this cross-sectional web-based survey, 1,057 adults completed the South Oaks Gambling Screen (SOGS), Beck Hopelessness Scale (BHS), and Suicide Probability Scale (SPS). Group differences were examined using non-parametric tests, followed by multivariable regression analyses. Results: Gambling participation was reported by 30.7% (95% CI 28.0–33.6) of participants; 4.9% (95% CI 3.8–6.4) screened positive for probable gambling disorder using the Turkish SOGS cut-off of ≥8. Participants reporting gambling had higher BHS and SPS scores, and differences were more pronounced among those screening positive for probable gambling disorder. The between-group difference in SPS scores among participants reporting gambling corresponded to a moderate-to-large effect (r=0.497, 95% CI 0.343–0.653). After covariate adjustment, gambling participation was associated with a 1.46-point higher BHS (95% CI 0.79–2.13) and 5.26-point higher SPS scores (95% CI 3.15–7.36). Among participants reporting gambling, positive screening was associated with 2.60-point higher BHS (95% CI 0.88–4.32) and 12.59-point higher SPS scores (95% CI 7.21–17.96). Gambling participation was also associated with histories of suicidal ideation (OR=1.71, 95% CI 1.17–2.50) and suicide attempt (OR=2.54, 95% CI 1.32–4.88). Conclusions: Gambling involvement, particularly positive SOGS screening, was associated with greater hopelessness and suicide-related symptom burden. The cross-sectional design and non-probability sampling preclude causal interpretation and population-level prevalence estimates.

title: Gambling in Sports: Validity and Reliability Study of the Gambling Passion Scale
abstract: Bu araştırmanın amacı, Rousseau ve arkadaşları (2002) tarafından geliştirilen “Bahis Tutkusu Ölçeği”nin Türk kültürüne uyarlanması, geçerlik ve güvenirlik analizlerinin gerçekleştirilmesidir. Araştırma, nicel araştırma desenlerinden tarama modeliyle yürütülmüştür. Uyarlama süreci literatürde önerilen beş aşamalı çeviri modeline göre gerçekleştirilmiştir: hedef dile çeviri, geri çeviri, uzman görüşü alınması, pilot uygulama ve geçerlik–güvenirlik analizleri. Araştırma grubu, 18–35 yaş aralığında yer alan ve aktif olarak spor bahsi oynayan toplam 344 katılımcıdan oluşmuştur (AFA=166; DFA=178). Elde edilen verilere ilişkin Açımlayıcı Faktör Analizi (AFA) sonucunda ölçeğin iki faktörlü (Obsesif Tutku ve Uyumlu Tutku) bir yapıya sahip olduğu ve toplam varyansın %63.9’unu açıkladığı belirlenmiştir (KMO=0.92; Bartlett χ²=801.495; p<0.001). Faktör yükleri 0.53 ile 0.92 arasında, Cronbach Alfa katsayıları 0.85–0.90, Omega güvenirlik katsayısı ise 0.90 olarak tespit edilmiştir. Doğrulayıcı Faktör Analizi (DFA) sonuçlarına göre uyum iyiliği indeksleri kabul edilebilir düzeydedir (χ²/sd=1.76; RMSEA=0.066; CFI=0.981; SRMR=0.292). Ayrıca yapı geçerliğini destekleyen CR (0.87–0.93) ve AVE (0.58–0.73) değerleri, ölçeğin birleşim ve ayrışım geçerliğini doğrulamaktadır. Bulgular, Türkçe Bahis Tutkusu Ölçeği’nin, bireylerin bahis tutkusu düzeylerini değerlendirmede geçerli ve güvenilir bir ölçme aracı olduğunu göstermektedir.

title: Gambling Involvement and Problem Gambling: Finding from a General Population Survey
abstract: Certain gambling formats, such as slot machines, have consistently been related to problem gambling. Extensive involvement in multiple gambling activities may also represent an important risk factor. This study explored the relationship between gambling involvement, gambling formats, and problem gambling in a subsample of 817 participants who reported engaging in gambling in the past month, drawn from a representative sample of Croatian residents aged 15-64 (N=4,988), Gambling involvement was assessed by the number of gambling formats and frequency of gambling in the past month, while problem gambling was assessed using the Problem Gambling Severity Index. Most participants (37.3%) engaged in one, 26.8% in two, 21.4% in three, and 14.5% in four or more gambling formats. Overall, 67.4% of participants were classified as non-problem, 10.1% as low-risk, 14.0% as moderate-risk, and 8.5% as participants with problem gambling. High gambling involvement was related to problem gambling, and frequent sports betting, casino games, and slot machines use. Participants with problem gambling most commonly engaged in four or more gambling formats. Findings suggest problem gambling is related not only to specific gambling formats but also to patterns of extensive and frequent involvement in multiple gambling activities, highlighting the importance of monitoring overall gambling behavior rather than focusing on specific games to identify high-risk individuals and inform prevention efforts.

title: «Έπειτα γήπεδο, στοιχήματα, καυγάς» : δράσεις και αντιδράσεις κοινωνίας και πολιτικών φορέων στην ίδρυση του ΟΠΑΠ και την κυκλοφορία του ΠΡΟΠΟ (1958–1959)
abstract: This thesis examines the social and political framework surrounding the establishment of the Greek Organization of Football Prognostics (OPAP) and the introduction of the football betting game PROPO in Greece, focusing on the sociopolitical reactions provoked by the institutionalization of a state-controlled game of chance during the period 1958–1959. The main objective of the study is to investigate how Greek society, political parties, and institutional actors perceived and interpreted a new phenomenon that combined sports, entertainment, and economic risk. Through the analysis of primary archival material, the research seeks to reveal the contradictions, moral concerns, and political motivations that accompanied the emergence of the institution. The study shows that early public reactions were deeply ambivalent: part of society welcomed PROPO as a means of economic hope and as a mechanism for supporting Greek athletics, while others expressed fears of moral corruption and social decay, particularly among the youth. These perceptions were reflected in the press of the time, with characteristic examples including the Eikones magazine poll and the articles of Eleftheria and Avgi newspapers. At the same time, institutional bodies such as the Supreme Confederation of Parents’ Associations of Greek Pupils and the Panhellenic Union of National Lottery Agents highlighted distinct aspects of the issue—from moral anxiety about youth behavior to the economic interests of professional groups. Secondly, The public debate culminated in Parliament in April 1959, when members of the United Democratic Left (EDA) strongly criticized PROPO, denouncing it as a form of “state gambling” that undermined social ethics, while the government defended it as an instrument of modernization and athletic development. By juxtaposing these conflicting discourses, the study reveals the complexity of a phenomenon that transcended the boundaries of sports and leisure, reflecting broader social and ideological tensions in post–Civil War Greece. Η παρούσα εργασία εξετάζει το κοινωνικό και πολιτικό πλαίσιο ίδρυσης του Οργανισμού Προγνωστικών Αγώνων Ποδοσφαίρου (ΟΠΑΠ) και την κυκλοφορία του ΠΡΟΠΟ στην Ελλάδα, εστιάζοντας στις κοινωνικοπολιτικές αντιδράσεις που προκάλεσε η θεσμοθέτηση ενός κρατικά ελεγχόμενου τυχερού παιχνιδιού κατά την περίοδο 1958-1959. Στόχος της μελέτης είναι η διερεύνηση του τρόπου με τον οποίο η ελληνική κοινωνία, τα πολιτικά κόμματα και οι θεσμικοί φορείς προσέλαβαν και ερμήνευσαν ένα νέο φαινόμενο, που συνδύαζε τον αθλητισμό, τη διασκέδαση και το οικονομικό ρίσκο. Μέσα από την ανάλυση πρωτογενούς αρχειακού υλικού. Η εργασία φιλοδοξεί να αναδείξει τις αντιφάσεις, τις ηθικές ανησυχίες και τις πολιτικές στοχεύσεις που συνόδευσαν τη γέννηση του θεσμού. Ενώ παράλληλα, η μελέτη αποκαλύπτει, πως οι πρώτες αντιδράσεις της κοινής γνώμης ήταν αμφίθυμες: ένα τμήμα της κοινωνίας υποδέχθηκε το ΠΡΟΠΟ ως μέσο οικονομικής ελπίδας και ενίσχυσης του ελληνικού αθλητισμού, ενώ ένα άλλο εξέφρασε φόβους για ηθική διαφθορά και κοινωνικό εκφυλισμό, ιδίως μεταξύ των νέων. Οι απόψεις αυτές εκφράστηκαν μέσα από τον Τύπο της εποχής, με χαρακτηριστικά παραδείγματα το δημοψήφισμα του περιοδικού Εικόνες και τα άρθρα των εφημερίδων Ελευθερία και Αυγή. Ταυτόχρονα, θεσμικοί φορείς όπως η Ανώτατη Συνομοσπονδία Συλλόγων Γονέων Μαθητών Ελλάδος και η Πανελλήνια Ένωση Πρακτόρων Εθνικού Λαχείου ανέδειξαν διαφορετικές διαστάσεις του ζητήματος, από την ηθική αγωνία για τη νεολαία έως τα οικονομικά συμφέροντα επαγγελματικών κλάδων. Η αντιπαράθεση κορυφώθηκε στη Βουλή τον Απρίλιο του 1959, όπου η ΕΔΑ άσκησε έντονη κριτική για τον «κρατικό τζόγο», ενώ η κυβέρνηση υπερασπίστηκε το ΠΡΟΠΟ ως μέσο κοινωνικής και αθλητικής προόδου. Με τα σχετικά συμπεράσματα να αποτελούν το επιστέγασμα της μελέτης.
venue: Πάντειον Πανεπιστήμιο Κοινωνικών και Πολιτικών Επιστημών

title: Η ΧΡΗΣΗ ΤΗΣ ΤΕΧΝΗΤΗΣ ΝΟΗΜΟΣΥΝΗΣ ΣΤΑ ΜΕΓΑΛΑ ΑΘΛΗΤΙΚΑ ΓΕΓΟΝΟΤΑ. Η ΠΕΡΙΠΤΩΣΗ ΤΟΥ FIFA WORLD CUP 2025.
abstract: Αντικείμενο της παρούσας διπλωματικής εργασίας αποτελεί η διερεύνηση του μετασχηματιστικού ρόλου της Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης (ΤΝ) στη διαχείριση και την κατανάλωση περιεχομένου μεγάλων αθλητικών διοργανώσεων (Mega Events). Μέσα από τη μελέτη περίπτωσης (case study) του FIFA World Cup 2025, αναλύεται ο τρόπος με τον οποίο οι αναδυόμενες τεχνολογίες αναδιαμορφώνουν την εμπειρία των φιλάθλων και τη λειτουργία των αθλητικών οργανισμών. Η εργασία εξετάζει την εφαρμογή καινοτόμων συστημάτων, όπως το ημι-αυτοματοποιημένο οφσάιντ (SAOT 2.0), η τεχνολογία διασυνδεδεμένης μπάλας (Connected Ball Technology) και η χρήση των Smart Stadiums μέσω του Internet of Things (IoT). Τα ευρήματα καταδεικνύουν μια θεαματική τεχνολογική μετάβαση από το Παγκόσμιο Κύπελλο του 2022 στην εποχή της «Προληπτικής ΤΝ» του 2025, όπου η υπολογιστική ισχύς (Edge Computing) και η υπερ-υψηλή ταχύτητα επεξεργασίας δεδομένων μειώνουν δραστικά τον χρόνο λήψης αποφάσεων. Ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στην εξατομίκευση της εμπειρίας του θεατή μέσω των AI-Generated Highlights και των FAST Channels, καθώς και στην παιχνιδοποίηση (gamification) της κατανάλωσης μέσω του Real-Time Fantasy Sports. Παράλληλα, η έρευνα προσεγγίζει κριτικά τις ηθικές προκλήσεις που προκύπτουν, όπως η ψηφιακή επιτήρηση και η προστασία των βιομετρικών δεδομένων των αθλητών. Συμπερασματικά, η εργασία αναδεικνύει ότι το FIFA World Cup 2025 αποτελεί το σημείο καμπής για τη μετάβαση σε ένα «Phygital» αθλητικό μοντέλο. Η Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη δεν λειτουργεί πλέον ως επικουρικό εργαλείο, αλλά ως το θεμελιώδες λειτουργικό σύστημα που διασφαλίζει τη βιωσιμότητα, την ασφάλεια και την εμπορική επιτυχία του παγκόσμιου ποδοσφαίρου στην ψηφιακή εποχή.

title: Σχεδίαση και ανάπτυξη προσωποποιημένης διαλογικής διεπαφής για εφαρμογή "Fantasy football"
abstract: Fantasy Premier League (FPL) is one of the world’s most popular online fantasy sports games, in which millions of managers worldwide are required to make a series of critical decisions regarding their virtual teams every gameweek, in order to accumulate as many points as possible from the real-world performances of the footballers they select. However, the official platform primarily provides raw statistical information and limited decision-support capabilities, while existing third-party applications are mainly targeted at experienced users and frequently organise information through dense tables and long lists of metrics. Managers are therefore forced to switch between multiple websites and tools to analyse players, compare alternatives, and manage their squads, frequently through subscription-based services. They are left with a fragmented and demanding environment that imposes a considerable cognitive load and requires substantial time to learn, and that becomes difficult to use for those without much experience. This thesis presents the design, development, and evaluation of a complete full-stack Fantasy Football web application with a personalized conversational interface (AI chatbot). The central contribution is twofold: first, it implements the game itself and comprehensively redesigns the overall user experience (UI/UX) compared with both the official Fantasy Premier League application and existing third-party platforms, bringing together team management, data analysis, player-performance predictions, and decisionsupport functionalities within a single coherent and user-friendly environment. Second, it integrates a conversational Artificial Intelligence coaching assistant that personalises its recommendations according to each manager’s preferences, playing style, and current squad status, providing tailored explanations and decision support through natural language interaction. Underneath runs a machine-learning pipeline that forecasts points, minutes played and likelihood of appearance for the next gameweek, using gradient-boosted tree models with rolling-origin cross-validation and an acceptance check that retains the previous model whenever a retrained one performs worse. The resulting predictions are utilised by a hybrid recommendation engine that combines machine-learning techniques with heuristic rules, as well as by an integer linear programming optimiser for constructing the initial squad. A Large Language Model layer then turns these structured numerical recommendations into natural, explanatory dialogue. The platform is supported by a complete backend, a relational database, an automated data-synchronisation mechanism, a job-scheduling system, and user authentication. The implementation employs the Next.js and Express frameworks with TypeScript, Python for the machinelearning pipeline, and PostgreSQL for data management. The system was evaluated with respect to the accuracy of its predictive models, the quality of its recommendations, and the usability, clarity, and overall user experience delivered by the application.

title: المكاسب المالية عبر وسائل التواصل المعاصرة (دراسة فقهية مقارنة) Financial Gains Through Modern Communication Media (A Comparative Jurisprudential Study)
abstract: تهدف الدراسة من هذا البحث إلى بيان المعاملات المالية التي انتشرت على وسائل التواصل المعاصرة ومن هذه المعاملات المالية التجارة الإلكترونية، التسويق الشبكي، المراهنات الإلكترونية منصات عرض المحتوى(Tik Tok) – فأردت أن أبين من الناحية الفقهية مدى شرعية هذه المعاملات المالية والمكاسب الناتجة عنها حتى يتبين ما هو مباح وندع منها ما خالف قواعد وأحكام الشريعة الغراء، ولقد نهجت في كتابة هذا البحث المنهج العلمي الاستقرائي، وذلك بتتبع المعلومات المتعلقة بمادة موضوع البحث من مظانها كلما اعتمدت على المنهج المقارن محاولة جمع آراء العلماء، والفقهاء، وجعلت الآراء المتفقة في قول واحد يجمع بين أصحابه وحدة الرأي في المسألة الواحدة كما قمت بعزو الآيات إلى سورها ،وكذلك قمت بتخريج الأحاديث وفق المنهج العلمي في التخريج من الصحيحين فإن لم يكن في الصحيحين بينت درجة الحديث والحكم عليه، كما ختمت هذا البحث بخاتمة ضمنتها أهم النتائج التي توصلت إليها في هذا البحث، وأهم نتائج البحث: المكاسب المادية الناتجة عن التجارة الإلكترونية إذا كانت الصفة مكتملة شروط الصحة وخالية من الموانع الشرعية فهي مباحة ومكاسبها المادية مباحة أما إذا كانت تحتوى على الغرر والجهالة فهي محرمة شرعاً وما نتج عنها من مكاسب مادية فهو محرم، التسويق الشبكي حرام شرعاً وما نتج عنه من مكاسب مالية فهي حرام، المراهنات الإلكترونية التي تعتمد على دفع أموال للفوز بمال، أو جوائز يعتبر من القمار المحرم شرعاً وما نتج عنه من مكاسب مالية فهو حرام – أما المراهنات الإلكترونية إذا كانت في مجال الرياضة وكانت الجائزة مقررة من ولى الأمر ولم يشترط فيها دفع مال فهي جائزة وما نتج عنها من أرباح مالية فهي حلال. This research aims to examine the financial transactions that have become prevalent on modern social media platforms. These transactions include e-commerce, network marketing, online betting, and content-sharing platforms (such as TikTok). The research seeks to determine the permissibility of these transactions and the resulting profits from a jurisprudential perspective, clarifying what is permissible and rejecting what violates the principles and rulings of Islamic sharia. The research employs an inductive scientific methodology, tracing information related to the research topic from its primary sources. Whenever the research relies on a comparative approach, it attempts to gather the opinions of scholars and jurists, presenting those who agree on a single issue. The research also cites Quranic verses to their respective chapters and authenticates hadiths according to the established methodology of hadith authentication, relying on the two Sahih collections (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim). If a hadith is not found in these two collections, its authenticity and ruling are indicated. The research concludes with a summary of the most important findings. The most significant finding is the financial gains resulting from e-commerce. If a transaction fulfills all the conditions of validity and is free from any legal impediments, it is permissible, and its financial gains are permissible. However, if it involves uncertainty and ambiguity, it is forbidden according to Islamic sharia , and any resulting financial gains are also forbidden. Network marketing is forbidden according to Islamic sharia, and any financial gains resulting from it are also forbidden. Electronic betting, which involves paying money to win money or prizes, is considered gambling, which is forbidden according to Islamic sharia , and any resulting financial gains are forbidden. However, if electronic betting is in the field of sports and the prize is determined by the governing authority and does not require payment, then it is permissible, and any resulting financial profits are lawful.

abstract: 본 연구는 축구 스포츠토토 의사결정에서 경기 참고요인의 중요도와 우선순위를 분석하고, 참여자 특성에 따라 이러한 인식 구조가 어떻게 달라지는지를 확인하는 데 목적이 있다. 연구대상은 최근 1년 이내 축구 스포츠토토 구매 경험이 있는 성인 400명이었으며, 자료는 설문조사를 통해 수집하였다. 설문 문항은 축구 경기 결과 판단과 스포츠토토 의사 결정 과정에서 반복적으로 활용되는 경기 참고요인을 중심으로 구성하였다. 구체적으로 팀 시장가치, 팀 명성·인지도, 시즌 순위·승점, 최근 5경기 성적, 홈/원정 조건, 주전 선수의 부상 및 결장 정보, 일정 혼잡도·휴식일 차이, 최근 상대전적, 아시안핸디캡 개장정보, 유럽배당 개장정보 등 10개 요인의 중요도를 평정하도록 하였고, 실제 의사결정에서 우선적으로 고려하는 요인을 1~3순위로 선택하도록 하였다. 수집된 자료는 SPSS 통계프로그램을 활용하여 빈도분석, 기술통계 분석, Friedman 검정, 우선순위 분석 및 주요 하위집단 비교분석을 실시하였다. 분석 결과, 중요도 평균은 주전 선수 부상·결장 정보가 가장 높았고, 최근 5경기 성적, 일정 혼잡도·휴식일 차이, 아시안핸디캡 개장정보, 유럽배당 개장정보순으로 나타났다. 우선순위 분석에서는 최근 5경기 성적, 주전 선수 부상·결장 정보, 일정 혼잡도·휴식일 차이가 핵심 판단요인으로 확인되었다. 또한 구매경력과 배당 이해도가 높은 고경험·고배당이해 집단은 최근 경기 성적, 일정 관련 정보 및 배당정보를 상대적으로 더 중시하는 경향이 나타난 반면, 저경험·저배당이해 집단은 팀 시장가치와 팀 명성·인지도를 상대적으로 더 중요하게 평가하는 경향이 나타났다. 이러한 결과는 축구 스포츠토토 참여자의 경기 참고요인 인식이 단일한 구조가 아니라 참여 경험과 시장정보 이해 수준에 따라 달라질 수 있음을 시사한다.

abstract: Gambling poses a significant threat to societal norms and can impede national progress on both material and spiritual fronts.Consequently, a rational approach is imperative in addressing this issue, which includes robust law enforcement policies and the prosecution of offenders.This research delves into the Surabaya City Police's efforts to combat online soccer gambling and seeks to analyze the modus operandi of suspects involved in such activities, as well as the challenges and obstacles encountered by the Cyber Unit III of the Surabaya City Police Criminal Investigation Unit.Employing a qualitative descriptive exploratory methodology, this study utilizes primary and secondary data gathered through observation, interviews, and document analysis.The findings of this research are anticipated to serve as a valuable resource for understanding the complexities of combating online gambling and to inform strategies for enhancing police effectiveness in responding to public reports of this illicit activity.

title: Chapter La prima vicenda del calcioscommesse in Italia (1980)
abstract: The football betting scandal that broke out in the first months of 1980, although it was the one that left the most unpleasant memories in the collective memory, especially due to the notoriety of the teams and players involved, was not the first scandal of its kind in our football. Between the fascist period, when football really began to be a mass phenomenon, and the eighties there were a series of “fixed” matches that dirty the image of our best-known sport, starting with the scandal involving the Juventus and national team full-back Luigi Allemandi in the 1926-1927 season. The paper analyzes this long period, marked by the events that between the fifties and seventies involved important clubs such as Milan, Udinese, Atalanta, Genoa and Foggia, and then faced the scandal of clandestine betting at the origin of the first major sporting process in our history.

abstract: Betting on Neuromodulation: Efficacy of Adjunctive Theta HD-tACS in Gambling Disorder Aaditya S., Sourav Khanra, Premaja Bhatt Joshi, Anshul Yadav, Justin Raj PC, Sanjay Kumar Munda. Central Institute of Psychiatry, Ranchi. Introduction: Recent years have witnessed an unprecedented growth in commercial gambling, fueled by ready online access. The relapsing nature of gambling disorder, with poor retention on current management protocols, requires novel treatment modalities to be explored. Aim: To investigate the efficacy of neuromodulation in the form of theta high-definition transcranial alternating current stimulation (HD-tACS) as an adjunctive intervention for patients with gambling disorder. Methodology: Three inpatients from a tertiary care hospital - Mr. X, a 38-year old male with a ten-year history of online sports betting, Mr. Y, a 31-year old who had incurred a loss of eight lakhs on offline card gambling and Mr. Z, a 24-year old with a history of online casino gambling - were included in the case series. Appropriate clinical scales were applied to assess gambling related cognitions, severity and craving, along with any comorbid anxiety and depression. This was followed by Stroop Task, Iowa Gambling Task, qEEG and resting state fMRI. 10 sessions of 6Hz theta HD-tACS of 20 minutes each were then administered to the left DLPFC over 5 days, after which assessments and imaging were repeated. Results: All subjects showed improvements in gambling related cognitions, severity and craving. They also displayed reduced risk-taking behaviour on Iowa Gambling Task, and reduced anxiety and depressive symptoms. qEEG and resting state fMRI findings will be reported at the time of presentation. Discussion: Prefrontal theta asymmetry between the right and left cortices has been hypothesised to underlie increased risk-taking behaviour. Exogenous theta HD-tACS to the left DLPFC leading to entrainment of theta oscillations, thereby reducing interhemispheric asymmetry, could increase cognitive control and risk aversiveness in gambling. Conclusion: The successful application of theta HD-tACS represents a possible breakthrough in our quest to treat gambling disorder, and warrants urgent further research to generalise these findings. Keywords: Gambling, Neuromodulation, tACS, DLPFC. Capturing Real-Time Moments: Exploring Ecological Momentary Assessment for Alcohol Dependence in India Ankita Chattopadhyay, Shalini Singh, Rakesh Lal Jawaharlal Institute of Postgraduate Medical Education and Research (JIPMER), Puducherry, India, National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, India Aims/Objectives: Ecological momentary assessment (EMA) is emerging as a valuable method for real-time behavioural monitoring in substance-using population in natural settings. However, most EMA research has been conducted in developed countries and predominantly among non-dependent or non-treatment-seeking individuals, often with varied protocols and heterogeneous samples. This study aims to explore feasibility of EMA in treatment-seeking alcohol-dependent patients in India. Methods: A total of 102 males diagnosed with alcohol-dependence were recruited during outpatient detoxification phase. Ethical approval was obtained, and participants provided written informed consent. Participants completed a socio-demographic-clinical proforma, alongwith assessment of alcohol use severity, affective states (depression, anxiety, psychological stress), and alcohol craving using standardized clinical scales. EMA prompts addressing mood (sadness), anxiety, stress, and craving were sent to participants’ phones thrice daily for one week. Additionally, participants were required to self-initiate a response once daily. Results: Overall response rate was 24.47%, comprising 0.08% for self-initiated responses and 32.35% for random prompts. Acceptance rate for participation was high at 91.07%, but retention rate was low (34.31%). Compliance assessed by tracking response frequency revealed decline in responses over study duration. Feedback from participants indicated that both the length and frequency of assessments were perceived as “just right.” Notably, no significant clinical differences emerged between responders and non-responders. Reliability analysis showed moderate reliability for mood and stress measures, but poor reliability for anxiety and craving. Discussion: This study is pioneering in assessing EMA feasibility among treatment-seeking alcohol dependent patients in India, with findings suggesting that EMA can be useful for monitoring drinking behavior and related parameters, but challenges in compliance must be addressed. Conclusion: EMA studies involving larger samples and strategies to enhance adherence, such as incentivization and personalized interventions should be conducted in India. Additionally, developing tailored digital applications for alcohol-dependent patients in India could improve efficacy of EMA methodologies. Navigating the Aftermath: The Impact of Patient’s Suicide on Mental Health Professionals Akansha Bharadwaj, Shipra Singh, Yogender Malik AIIMS, New Delhi Introduction: The impact of patient suicides on mental health professionals (MHPs) is profound, affecting their emotional well-being and profession. This study explores MHPs’ experiences with patient suicides and their adequacy of managing such incidents. Aim/Objectives: The aim of the study is to explore the effect of patient suicides on MHPs. Objectives include evaluating the perceived psychological and professional impacts, understanding the support MHPs need and receive, and assessing their views on training related to dealing with patient suicides. Methodology: A mixed-methods approach was employed, utilizing a semi-structured online survey, following Institutional Ethical approval. The questionnaire, validated by professionals, covered demographics, details of incidents, emotional and professional impacts and support systems. The survey was open for 8 weeks, and responses from 96 MHPs were analysed using descriptive statistics and thematic analysis to derive insights from both quantitative and qualitative data. Results: Among 96 MHPs surveyed, 51% had treated patients who died by suicide, with a majority being males aged 20-40 years, primarily diagnosed with psychotic or affective disorders. The emotional impact varied: 49% reported mild, 28% moderate effects, with sadness, regret, and guilt being common responses. Support-seeking behaviours were prevalent, with 52.2% of respondents finding support from colleagues, family, or professional communities helpful, but formal training on managing patient suicides was found lacking. Discussion: The impact of patient suicides on MHPs is multifaceted, affecting personal and professional aspects. A significant portion of MHPs experienced patient suicides after completing their training. Majority of suicides occurred outside controlled environments, highlighting need for stronger follow-up and community support. Conclusion: The emotional and professional consequences of patient suicides underscores importance of a supportive environment, integrating enhanced psychiatry training and fostering open dialogue. Addressing these needs can help mitigate adverse effects and promote resilience among MHPs, ultimately benefiting practitioners and quality of mental health services. A comparative study on Cognitive impairment among patients with chronic skin inflammatory disorder (Psoriasis and Vitiligo) Tarun Narang, Anupama Arora, Rahul Chakravarty, Aseem Mehra PGIMER, Chandigarh, Dr YS Parmar Government Medical College, Nahan Background: A limited number of studies have associated the prevalence of cognitive impairment among patient with chronic inflammatory skin disorders. Aim and objectives: To evaluate and compare the presence of cognitive impairment among patients with psoriasis and vitiligo. Methods: This was a cross-sectional study with a convenient sampling technique. A total of 200 patient with a diagnosis of Psoriasis and Vitiligo (100 each) were included. Participants were evaluated on the Hindi version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment for cognitive impairment, Patient Health Questionnaire- 9 for depression, Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 for anxiety disorder and Metabolic syndrome as per the consensus criteria given by World Health Organization. Results: A total of 200 patients were recruited. Those with Psoriasis were significantly older (p 10). Cardiovascular risk was significantly higher in inactive (6.36 ± 8.5, p =0 .015) group compared to HEPA active group (1.92 ± 4.0). There was no significant difference between HEPA and minimally active groups (p =0 .291). Age, but not duration of illness or antipsychotic exposure was positively associated with QRISK-3 score. Among antipsychotics, clozapine was significantly associated with increased BMI (p<0.001) but not with QRISK-3. Discussion: This aligns with previous research indicating that individuals with SMI, especially those on antipsychotics, are at increased cardiovascular risk due to adverse effects compounded with lifestyle factors such as physical inactivity and obesity.4 Conclusion: There is a need to emphasise lifestyle modifications and regular cardiovascular monitoring in women on antipsychotics. title: Sporting integrity and preventing abuse in football: a coherent, holistic and systems-based approach
abstract: Integrity is generally perceived to be positive by its presence and problematic in its absence. In football, absence of integrity is demonstrated by the ‘unholy trinity’ of corruption, match-fixing and irregular sports betting. Other abuses that happen in and through football include child abuse and trafficking of children, and yet to date, these integrity issues are typically viewed as outliers to its nature. This chapter argues that all threats to the integrity of football should be viewed as residing within the same football system and that any ‘out of integrity’ behaviours show a deviation from the nature of the sport to promote sustainability, and through it, and ultimately threaten the game in its core. It is further argued that abuse in football (e.g. sexual, physical, emotional) and abuse through football (e.g. trafficking) are both manifestations of systemic failures within football, indicative of a broken sports system that lacks coherence and therefore fails to prevent abuse. The chapter calls for a broader holistic systems-based approach to promote sporting integrity in football which results in a coherent system designed, implemented and used with the intended purpose of identifying and preventing all forms of abuse.
